## Problem

`config/exports:12` and `config/fish/exports.fish:7` export `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$HOME/.local/run"` whenever the session has not set one — always the case on macOS, and on any Linux login that bypasses pam_systemd. `dotbot-links.yaml` creates that directory with no `mode:`, so it inherits the repo-wide default of `0755` from `tools/dotbot-defaults.yaml`.

The XDG Base Directory Specification is not permissive about this directory: "The directory MUST be owned by the user, and he MUST be the only one having read and write access to it. Its Unix access mode MUST be 0700." Every program that honours `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` puts sockets, lock files and short-lived credential material there on the assumption that mode holds.

The repo already knows the mechanism — `~/.ssh`, `~/.ssh/local.d` and `~/.local/share/gnupg` each carry an explicit `mode: 0700` in the same `create:` block. The runtime dir was left out.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">`dotbot-links.yaml` `create:` block, annotated by whether the next line supplies a mode:

```
none ~/.local/run:
none ~/.local/state:
none ~/.local/state/tmux:
none ~/.local/state/zsh:
MODE ~/.local/share/gnupg:      <- mode: 0700
MODE ~/.ssh:                    <- mode: 0700
MODE ~/.ssh/local.d:            <- mode: 0700
```

`tools/dotbot-defaults.yaml` supplies the fallback:

```yaml
- defaults:
    create:
      mode: 0755
```

`config/exports:12`:

```sh
[ -z "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-}" ] && export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$HOME/.local/run"
```

On the maintainer's machine the directory is worse than the declared default — `stat -c '%a %n'` reports:

```
777 /home/ivuorinen/.local/run
700 /home/ivuorinen/.ssh
777 /home/ivuorinen/.local/state
```

0755 is the best case this config can produce; 0777 is what it actually left behind (see the companion finding on creation-only modes).</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">On any host with more than one local account — a work machine with a service user, a shared box, a container that runs as a second uid — every other local user can list and read whatever lands in `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. At the observed 0777 they can also write it: replace a socket with their own, or plant a file where a program expects to create one. The exposure is silent, because nothing in the repo checks the mode after installation.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Give the runtime dir the same treatment as `~/.ssh` in `dotbot-links.yaml`:

```yaml
    ~/.local/run:
      mode: 0700
```

`~/.local/state` deserves the same, since `config/exports` puts zsh history (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/zsh/history`), the 1Password cache (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/1password`) and the theme daemon's pidfile under it:

```yaml
    ~/.local/state:
      mode: 0700
```

This alone will not repair the machines already at 0777 — dotbot skips paths that exist. Apply the companion finding's fix as well, or chmod once by hand:

```
chmod 0700 ~/.local/run ~/.local/state
```</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added `mode: 0700` to `~/.local/run` (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, per the XDG spec's mandatory 0700) and to `~/.local/state`, `~/.local/state/tmux`, `~/.local/state/zsh` in dotbot-links.yaml, each with a comment naming what it protects. Declared modes now read: 0700 for run/state/state-tmux/state-zsh/gnupg/ssh/ssh-local.d, default 0755 for the cache and share paths. yamllint and prettier both clean. Note the drift on already-provisioned machines is a separate matter, handled by audit-066b5404's `dfm check perms`.
title: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (~/.local/run) is created world-readable, against the XDG spec's mandatory 0700

body:
## Problem

`./install` is documented and used as a re-runnable operation — `./install --links` exists precisely to refresh state. For directory permissions it is not: dotbot's `create` plugin applies the declared `mode:` only when the path does not yet exist. On every subsequent run it logs "Path exists" and returns success without looking at the mode.

That makes every `mode:` in `dotbot-links.yaml` a one-shot assertion tied to the moment a machine was first provisioned. Adding or tightening a mode later — including the `mode: 0700` fix for `~/.local/run` — is a no-op on every machine that already has the directory, while `./install` still exits 0. `dfm check` does not cover the gap either: it contains no `stat`, `chmod`, or permission logic at all.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">`tools/dotbot/src/dotbot/plugins/create.py:47-61`:

```python
def _create(self, path: str, mode: int) -> bool:
    success = True
    if not self._exists(path):
        self._log.debug(f"Trying to create path {path} with mode {mode}")
        try:
            self._log.lowinfo(f"Creating path {path}")
            os.makedirs(path, mode)
            os.chmod(path, mode)
        except OSError:
            self._log.warning(f"Failed to create path {path}")
            success = False
    else:
        self._log.lowinfo(f"Path exists {path}")
    return success
```

The `else` branch is the whole defect: an existing path is never chmod'ed.

Observed drift on the maintainer's machine, against a config whose default is `mode: 0755`:

```
$ stat -c '%a %n' ~/.local/run ~/.local/state ~/.local/state/zsh ~/.local/state/tmux
777 /home/ivuorinen/.local/run
777 /home/ivuorinen/.local/state
777 /home/ivuorinen/.local/state/zsh
777 /home/ivuorinen/.local/state/tmux
```

`./install` has been run many times against this tree and has corrected none of them.

`dfm check` has no permission coverage:

```
$ grep -nE 'stat |chmod|perm|mode|0700|0755' local/bin/dfm-check
(no output)
```</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every permission hardening added to `dotbot-links.yaml` after a machine's first provisioning is silently inert on that machine, and `./install` reports success. The `mode: 0700` entries on `~/.ssh`, `~/.ssh/local.d` and `~/.local/share/gnupg` are only as good as the day each host was set up. A drift introduced by any other tool — the 0777 above — persists indefinitely with no gate that notices.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add a permission check to `dfm check`, which is already the repo's "is this machine correctly set up" command, and have it read the declared modes rather than a second hardcoded list:

```bash
# dfm-check: verify declared create modes still hold.
python3 - <<'PY' | while read -r want path; do
  have=$(stat -c '%a' "$path" 2>/dev/null) || continue
  [ "$have" = "$want" ] || msgr warn "mode drift: $path is $have, expected $want"
done
import os, re, yaml
doc = yaml.safe_load(open("dotbot-links.yaml"))
default = 755
for block in doc:
    for path, opts in (block.get("create") or {}).items():
        mode = (opts or {}).get("mode", default)
        print(f"{mode:o} {os.path.expanduser(path)}")
PY
```

Then add `mode: 0700` to `~/.local/run` and `~/.local/state` per the companion finding, and chmod the existing directories once by hand — the check will keep them honest from then on.

Do not "fix" this by patching `tools/dotbot/`: it is a submodule and `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md` forbids editing it. A repair belongs in `dfm check`, not upstream.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added a `perms` subcommand to `dfm check`, wired into `dfm check all`, the MENU, and the `#USAGE` tree. It parses the declared modes straight out of dotbot-links.yaml with awk (falling back to the `create.mode` default in tools/dotbot-defaults.yaml), so there is no second hardcoded list to drift; comment lines inside the create block are skipped, and absent paths are ignored since several entries are host-specific. Uses `stat -c '%a'` with a `stat -f '%Lp'` fallback for BSD/macOS. Verified both directions: against this machine it reports the real drift and exits 1 (`mode drift: /home/ivuorinen/.local/run is 0777, declared 0700` + a paste-ready `chmod 0700 ...` line), and against a synthetic fixture whose modes match it reports "All 2 created directories match their declared mode" and exits 0. shellcheck -x and shfmt clean. Deliberately did not touch tools/dotbot — it is a submodule under .claude/rules/vendored-files.md.
title: Declared create modes are applied only at first creation, so ./install never repairs a drifted permission and nothing detects one

body:
## Problem

`.claude/rules/bash-routing.md` names exactly one git reader that stays on `Bash`: "`git status` is the one git reader the hook lets through, with or without `-s`: it is a common one-line check." `pre-bash-route.sh` repeats the promise in its own comment at lines 59-60.

The implementation does not keep it. `status` is absent from `allow_git_subcmd_re`, and the git branch denies any subcommand not on that list. So `git status` is denied on every invocation, with a reason that says the subcommand "is not on the allow list (output-reader)" — contradicting the rule the reason cites.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">`pre-bash-route.sh:51` — the allow list, with `status` missing:

```
allow_git_subcmd_re='^(add|commit|mv|rm|checkout|push|fetch|reset|restore|stash|tag|init|clone|branch|merge|remote|cherry-pick|revert|switch|am|apply|format-patch|gc|prune|reflog|worktree|notes|submodule|rerere|update-ref|symbolic-ref|update-index|hash-object|cat-file|rev-parse|rev-list|ls-files|check-ignore|config)$'
```

`pre-bash-route.sh:59-60` — the comment it contradicts:

```
# Note: `git status` (with or without `-s`) is _allowed_ — it's a common one-line
# check. `git log/diff/show/blame` always produce reviewable output and route through
```

Feeding the hook its own PreToolUse JSON:

```
$ printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"git status"}}' | bash .claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh \
    | jq -r .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision
deny
```

For contrast, the cases that are meant to deny do deny, so the guard is otherwise working:

```
git log --oneline -5   -> deny
yarn lint              -> deny
cat README.md          -> deny
```</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">`git status` is the most frequent one-line check in this repo's workflow, and it is blocked on every attempt. Each block costs a round trip and pushes a one-line query into `ctx_batch_execute`, which the rule explicitly says is not required for it. Worse for the enforcement chain as a whole: the denial reason cites `bash-routing.md`, so an agent that reads the rule to resolve the conflict finds the rule saying the opposite of what just happened. A guard that contradicts its own documentation trains the reader to distrust both, which is the failure mode `no-hook-bypass.md` depends on not happening.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add `status` to the git allow list in `pre-bash-route.sh:51`:

```
allow_git_subcmd_re='^(status|add|commit|mv|rm|checkout|push|fetch|reset|restore|stash|tag|init|clone|branch|merge|remote|cherry-pick|revert|switch|am|apply|format-patch|gc|prune|reflog|worktree|notes|submodule|rerere|update-ref|symbolic-ref|update-index|hash-object|cat-file|rev-parse|rev-list|ls-files|check-ignore|config)$'
```

Verify both directions, since the deny cases must not regress:

```bash
for c in "git status" "git status -s" "git log --oneline" "git diff"; do
  printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"%s"}}' "$c" \
    | bash .claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh \
    | jq -r --arg c "$c" '$c + " -> " + (.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision // "allow")'
done
```

Expect allow, allow, deny, deny.

The hook has no test file. Add `tests/pre-bash-route.bats` covering that table — every claim `bash-routing.md` makes about a specific command is a test case, and this defect is precisely what such a test would have caught.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added `status` to `allow_git_subcmd_re` in .claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh, with a comment recording why it is there so it is not dropped again. Verified in both directions via the new tests/pre-bash-route.bats: `git status` and `git status -s` now return allow, while `git log`, `git diff`, `git show` and `git blame` still deny. The hook now matches what .claude/rules/bash-routing.md and its own lines 59-60 say.
title: `git status` is denied by the router although the rule and the hook's own comment both promise it is allowed

body:
## Problem

The router decides using `first_word()` on each pipeline segment, after `strip_env_prefix()` removes `env VAR=…` and inline `VAR=…` prefixes. That covers exactly two wrapper shapes. Everything else that puts a different token in first position walks straight through:

- an absolute or relative path (`/bin/cat`) — the deny regex is anchored `^cat$`;
- a shell wrapper (`command`, `nohup`, `time`, `timeout`, `stdbuf`, `xargs`) — the wrapper is the first word, the denied command is the second;
- `env -i` — `strip_env_prefix` strips `env ` but its `VAR=` group matches zero times, leaving `-i` as the first word;
- a backslash-escaped name (`\cat`) — quoting-removal is a shell step the hook never performs.

`/bin/bash -c '<denied>'` is the sharpest case: lines 54-55 add `bash|sh|zsh|dash|ksh` to the deny list specifically "to block `bash -c '<denied>'` … bypasses called out in no-hook-bypass.md", and prefixing the interpreter with its own path defeats that in one character class.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">Each command below was fed to the hook as PreToolUse JSON; `deny` means blocked, blank means no decision (the call proceeds):

```
cat README.md                              -> deny
/bin/cat README.md                         ->
command cat README.md                      ->
timeout 5 rg foo .                         ->
nohup grep foo README.md                   ->
git ls-files | xargs cat                   ->
env -i cat README.md                       ->
\cat README.md                             ->
/bin/bash -c "cat README.md"               ->
```

The relevant code, `pre-bash-route.sh:100-121`:

```sh
first_word()
{
  local segment=$1
  printf '%s' "$segment" | awk '{print $1}'
  return 0
}

strip_env_prefix()
{
  local segment=$1
  printf '%s' "$segment" | sed -E '
    s/^env[[:space:]]+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*//
    s/^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)+//
  '
  return 0
}
```

`pre-bash-route.sh:53-56` states the intent the evidence defeats:

```sh
# Denylist: first-word commands that almost always produce reviewable output.
# Includes `bash`/`sh`/`zsh`/`dash`/`ksh` to block `bash -c '<denied>'` and
# `bash <<EOF<denied>EOF` heredoc bypasses called out in no-hook-bypass.md.
```</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The router is the mechanical half of the context-window protection; `bash-routing.md` and `no-hook-bypass.md` are the prose half. `no-hook-bypass.md` already forbids these forms by policy — "using `Bash -c '…'` / heredoc tricks to hide a denied command inside an allowed one all count as bypass" — so an agent taking any of them is out of compliance. The defect is that nothing stops it: a single unrouted `/bin/cat` on a large file dumps the file into context, which is the exact failure the whole chain exists to prevent, and it does so while reporting no violation. The `BASH_OK` marker exists as the documented, visible escape hatch; these seven are undocumented and invisible ones.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Normalise the token before matching, in two steps.

Basename-and-unescape the first word so a path or backslash cannot hide a name:

```sh
# Reduce a command token to its bare name: strip any leading directory
# component and a backslash escape, so `/bin/cat` and `\cat` both match the
# `cat` entry on the deny list.
normalise_cmd()
{
  local w=${1#\\}
  printf '%s' "${w##*/}"
}
```

Peel transparent wrappers until a real command name is in first position, mirroring what `strip_env_prefix` already does for `env`:

```sh
# Wrappers that execute their argument list: the denied command is the next
# word, not the first. Loop, because `nohup timeout 5 rg …` nests them.
strip_wrappers()
{
  local seg=$1
  while :; do
    case "$(normalise_cmd "$(first_word "$seg")")" in
      command | builtin | exec | nohup | time | timeout | stdbuf | xargs | nice | ionice)
        seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's/^[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+//')
        # Drop the wrapper's own flags and its numeric argument (timeout 5).
        seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's/^(-[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+|[0-9]+[a-z]?[[:space:]]+)*//')
        ;;
      *) break ;;
    esac
  done
  printf '%s' "$seg"
}
```

Call both in the loop at line 127:

```sh
segment=$(strip_env_prefix "$segment")
segment=$(strip_wrappers "$segment")
fw=$(normalise_cmd "$(first_word "$segment")")
```

`env -i` falls out of this too, once `strip_env_prefix` also drops leading flags:

```sh
    s/^env[[:space:]]+(-[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+)*//
```

Then lock the behaviour down in `tests/pre-bash-route.bats` with the nine-row table above as the fixture — the hook currently has no test file at all, which is why a deny list can drift from its own comment without anything noticing.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added `normalise_cmd` (strips a leading backslash and any directory component, so `/bin/cat` and `\cat` match the anchored deny entries) and `strip_wrappers` (peels command/builtin/exec/nohup/time/timeout/stdbuf/xargs/nice/ionice plus their flags and numeric args, looping for nested wrappers), and extended `strip_env_prefix` to drop `env`'s own flags so `env -i` no longer leaves `-i` in first position. The main loop now calls both before matching. All seven bypasses from the finding now deny: `/bin/cat`, `command cat`, `timeout 5 rg`, `nohup grep`, `git ls-files | xargs cat`, `env -i cat`, `\cat`, plus `/bin/bash -c "cat …"` and `/usr/bin/grep`. `command -v X` is explicitly exempted from wrapper stripping — it is a probe that never executes X — and is asserted to stay allowed. Locked down by 15 tests in the new tests/pre-bash-route.bats, all passing; full suite 879/879 green.
title: Seven trivial command forms bypass the bash router: absolute paths, wrapper commands, and xargs

## Problem

`LICENSE` and `package.json` both declare the whole repository MIT. The tree includes `local/bin/iterm2_shell_integration.zsh`, which carries a GNU GPL v2-or-later header, plus five vendored fish plugin functions and six vendored fzf files whose upstream licenses are recorded nowhere in the distribution. There is no `NOTICE` or `THIRD-PARTY` file.

The GPL header itself is intact in the file, which is the part that matters most — the notice travels with the code. What is wrong is the repo-level claim: a reader (or an automated license scanner, or anyone copying from this repo) is told "MIT" for a tree that is not uniformly MIT. `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md` names every upstream and its URL, but that file is an agent rule, not a license declaration, and it records no license for any entry.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">`LICENSE:1-3` and `package.json:35`:

```
MIT License

Copyright (c) 2022 Ismo Vuorinen
```

```json
"license": "MIT",
```

`local/bin/iterm2_shell_integration.zsh:2-14`:

```
# This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or
# modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License
# as published by the Free Software Foundation; either version 2
# of the License, or (at your option) any later version.
...
# You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
# along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software
# Foundation, Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.
```

No attribution file exists:

```
$ ls NOTICE THIRD-PARTY*
ls: cannot access 'NOTICE': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access 'THIRD-PARTY*': No such file or directory
```

The other vendored files carry no license header at all in their first eight lines — `local/bin/fzf-tmux`, `config/fzf/key-bindings.bash`, `config/fish/functions/fisher.fish`, `config/fish/functions/bass.fish`, `config/fish/functions/__z_add.fish`. `.claude/skills/graphify/` contains only `SKILL.md` and `references/`, no license file.

`.claude/rules/vendored-files.md` lists every upstream URL and, for the fish group, a table of projects — but no license column and no license text.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">A public repository that says MIT while distributing GPL-2.0-or-later code misrepresents its own terms. Anyone who takes the repo at its word and copies `iterm2_shell_integration.zsh` into a proprietary or MIT project inherits a GPL obligation they were told did not exist. License scanners run against the repo (Codacy, Snyk, and the `license` lens of this audit) will flag the conflict on every run with nothing in-tree to reconcile it against. The fzf and fish files have the opposite problem — their licenses are permissive, but nothing in the distribution says so, so a downstream reader cannot establish they are safe to reuse.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add a `NOTICE` file at the repo root enumerating each vendored tree, its upstream and its license, and point `LICENSE` at it. Draw the entries straight from the table `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md` already maintains:

```markdown
# Third-party components

The MIT license in LICENSE covers this repository's own work. The files
below are vendored from upstream projects and keep their own terms.

| Path                                    | Upstream                          | License           |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------|
| `local/bin/iterm2_shell_integration.zsh`| iTerm2                            | GPL-2.0-or-later  |
| `local/bin/fzf-tmux`, `config/fzf/*`    | junegunn/fzf                      | MIT               |
| `config/fish/functions/fisher.fish`     | jorgebucaran/fisher               | MIT               |
| `config/fish/functions/bass.fish`, `__bass.py` | edc/bass                   | MIT               |
| `config/fish/functions/__z_add.fish`, `__z_clean.fish` | jethrokuan/z      | MIT               |
| `.claude/skills/graphify/`              | (record upstream + license)       |                   |
```

Add one line to `LICENSE` above the MIT text: `Portions of this repository are third-party; see NOTICE.` Confirm each license against the upstream repo before writing it down rather than assuming MIT — the `no-schema-guessing` discipline applies to license facts too.

Add the `NOTICE` row to `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md`'s maintenance instructions so the two stay in step, the same way `.codacy.yml`, `pyproject.toml` and `.mega-linter.yml` are already kept in step there.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Added a root `NOTICE` enumerating every vendored tree with its upstream and license, and prefixed `LICENSE` with a pointer to it stating the repo is not uniformly MIT. Licenses were established from the GitHub license API in this session rather than assumed: junegunn/fzf MIT, jorgebucaran/fisher MIT, edc/bass MIT, jethrokuan/z MIT (all HTTP 200). iTerm2 shell integration is recorded as GPL-2.0-or-later from the notice preserved in the file's own header. The graphify skill is recorded as "license not recorded" with an instruction to verify against the plugin source before redistributing — deliberately not guessed, per .claude/rules/no-schema-guessing.md. NOTICE carries a Maintenance section naming itself as the fourth copy of the vendored list, alongside the rule frontmatter, .codacy.yml exclude_paths, and [tool.bandit] exclude_dirs. `yarn lint` rc=0.
title: Repo declares MIT while shipping a GPL-2.0-or-later file, and carries no attribution for any vendored upstream

## Problem

`CLAUDE.md` is the file loaded into every session, so its Gotchas list is the first and often only description an agent reads of what is vendored. The working tree extends `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md` from three groups to four — adding `fisher.fish`, `bass.fish`, `__bass.py`, `__z_add.fish`, `__z_clean.fish` under `config/fish/functions/` — and extends `.claude/hooks/pre-edit-block.sh` to block edits to all five. `CLAUDE.md` was not updated and still enumerates three groups.

The rule file itself states exactly why this matters: those five files "sit beside hand-written functions with no naming signal, which is exactly why they are listed here." An agent working from the `CLAUDE.md` summary has no signal at all.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">`CLAUDE.md:119-121`, unchanged in the working tree:

```markdown
- **Vendored files**: the six fzf files, `.claude/skills/graphify/`, and
  `local/bin/iterm2_shell_integration.zsh`.
  Edit policy: `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md`.
```

`.claude/rules/vendored-files.md`, working tree — frontmatter and prose both moved to four groups:

```yaml
paths:
  - "local/bin/fzf-tmux"
  - "config/fzf/completion.bash"
  ...
  - "config/fish/functions/fisher.fish"
  - "config/fish/functions/bass.fish"
  - "config/fish/functions/__bass.py"
  - "config/fish/functions/__z_add.fish"
  - "config/fish/functions/__z_clean.fish"
```

```markdown
Never modify vendored files. Four groups are vendored in-tree rather
```

`.claude/hooks/pre-edit-block.sh:52-61`, working tree — the same five paths now hard-blocked:

```sh
  */config/fish/functions/fisher.fish | \
    */config/fish/functions/bass.fish | \
    */config/fish/functions/__bass.py | \
    */config/fish/functions/__z_add.fish | \
    */config/fish/functions/__z_clean.fish)
    echo "BLOCKED: $fp is a vendored fish plugin function — refresh it" >&2
```</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">An agent plans an edit to `config/fish/functions/fisher.fish` on the strength of `CLAUDE.md`'s three-group list, gets it denied by the hook mid-task, and has to re-plan. The hook is the backstop, so nothing incorrect ships — but the cost is a wasted turn on work the always-loaded doc could have prevented, which is the whole reason that Gotchas entry exists. `CLAUDE.md`'s own convention is that a rule file is the authority and the summary must not contradict it; here it does.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Update `CLAUDE.md:119-121` to name the fourth group without restating the rule's table:

```markdown
- **Vendored files**: the six fzf files, `.claude/skills/graphify/`,
  `local/bin/iterm2_shell_integration.zsh`, and five fish plugin
  functions under `config/fish/functions/` (`fisher.fish`, `bass.fish`,
  `__bass.py`, `__z_add.fish`, `__z_clean.fish`).
  Edit policy: `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md`.
```

Ship it in the same commit as the rule and hook change, so the three copies of the list never disagree in history.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md's Gotchas entry now names the fourth vendored group explicitly — the five fish plugin functions under config/fish/functions/ (fisher.fish, bass.fish, __bass.py, __z_add.fish, __z_clean.fish) — matching .claude/rules/vendored-files.md and the paths pre-edit-block.sh blocks. Also added a pointer to the new NOTICE for third-party licenses. `yarn lint` rc=0 (markdownlint, md-table and editorconfig-checker all clean on the edited lines).
title: CLAUDE.md's vendored-files list omits the five fish plugin functions the rule and hook now cover
