## Problem

The `local/bin` loop picks a file as a usage spec when `#USAGE` or `//USAGE` appears anywhere in it, at any column. `local/bin/CLAUDE.md` documents the convention and writes the directive inline in prose, so the markdown file was handed to `usage` as if it were a script. `usage` rejected it as invalid KDL once per output format — fish, bash and zsh completions plus markdown and manpage — and the accumulated `errors` count became the script's exit status.

`usage` only extracts directives that start the line, and `scripts/install-completions.sh` already knows this: the dfm assembly step greps `'^#USAGE'` at lines 148 and 152, and the comment at lines 137-140 spells out that "usage only extracts #USAGE directives when the file looks like a script". The selector at line 116 was the one place that did not anchor.

The trap is structural rather than specific to one file: any note, README, or doc under `local/bin/` that mentions the directive in prose selects itself as a spec.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">`scripts/install-completions.sh:114-116` before the fix:

```sh
for spec in "$DOTFILES"/local/bin/*; do
  [[ -f "$spec" ]] || continue
  grep -q '#USAGE\|//USAGE' "$spec" 2> /dev/null || continue
```

The prose that matched, `local/bin/CLAUDE.md:18` and `:42`:

```markdown
  — one file per section, each carrying its own `#USAGE` subtree.
per-section `#USAGE` fragments into one `dfm` spec (skipping `dfm`/`dfm-*`
```

Running the generator:

```
$ DOTFILES="$PWD" bash scripts/install-completions.sh; echo "rc=$?"
[WARN]: fish completion failed for CLAUDE.md
[WARN]: bash completion failed for CLAUDE.md
[WARN]: zsh completion failed for CLAUDE.md
[WARN]: markdown generation failed for CLAUDE.md
[WARN]: manpage generation failed for CLAUDE.md
Error:
  × Failed to parse KDL document
  × Found invalid node name
 56 │ - `dfm tests` — test visualization helpers
[INFO]: Done: processed 91 specs (5 warnings)
rc=4
```

`CLAUDE.md` was the only failure; all five warnings name it.

Anchoring costs nothing, because every real spec already complies:

```
match anywhere: 88   match at column 0: 87
would be DROPPED by anchoring: CLAUDE.md
```

Every `scripts/*.sh` also carries its directive at column 0, so the second loop was never at risk.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">`./install` runs this generator, and a non-zero exit from a step that "only regenerates docs" is the kind of failure that gets normalised — the completions, `local/md/` docs and manpages for the other 90 specs were all written correctly, so the run looked cosmetically fine while reporting failure. The five KDL parse dumps drown the real log. Any future doc file under `local/bin/` that names the directive reintroduces it, and each one adds five more warnings and a further increment to the exit status.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Anchor the selector to column 0, matching `usage`'s own requirement and the two greps the dfm assembly step in the same file already uses:

```sh
for spec in "$DOTFILES"/local/bin/*; do
  [[ -f "$spec" ]] || continue
  # Anchored at column 0, matching the dfm assembly step below and `usage`
  # itself, which only extracts directives that start the line. An unanchored
  # match also selects prose: local/bin/CLAUDE.md documents the convention and
  # writes `#USAGE` inline, so it was handed to `usage`, failed to parse as
  # KDL five times over, and took the generator's exit status to 4.
  grep -qE '^(#USAGE|//USAGE)' "$spec" 2> /dev/null || continue
```

Verify the count moves by exactly one and the status clears:

```
DOTFILES="$PWD" bash scripts/install-completions.sh; echo "rc=$?"
```

Expect `Done: processed 90 specs (0 warnings)` and `rc=0`. Confirm `dfm` still generates — it is the assembled spec and the one most likely to break — with `grep -c 'Generating for: dfm$'`.

Note that `local/md/` and `local/man/man1/*.1` are gitignored (`.gitignore:95-96`), so a regression here shows up only in the generator's exit status, never as a diff. That is the argument for keeping the exit status meaningful.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Anchored the selector at scripts/install-completions.sh:116 to `grep -qE '^(#USAGE|//USAGE)'`, with a comment recording the CLAUDE.md failure mode. Verified: exit status 4 -> 0, warnings 5 -> 0, specs 91 -> 90, where the single dropped entry is the bogus local/bin/CLAUDE.md — all 87 files with a real directive have it at column 0, as does every scripts/*.sh. The assembled `dfm` spec still generates and includes the `perms` subcommand added by audit-066b5404 (local/md/dfm.md:263). No stale local/md/CLAUDE.md or local/man/man1/CLAUDE.1 were left by the earlier failing runs. shellcheck -x, shfmt and `yarn lint` (rc=0) all clean; generated output is byte-identical to before, and since local/md/ and local/man/man1/*.1 are gitignored the only tracked change is the one line in the generator. Predates this session's audit work: neither local/bin/CLAUDE.md nor install-completions.sh was touched by the audit fixes, and the `dfm` spec — the one thing this session did change — generated cleanly throughout.
title: Doc generation selects specs on an unanchored #USAGE match, so a markdown file mentioning the directive in prose is parsed as a spec and fails the run

body:
## Problem

Two rule files state that commit messages are mechanically enforced. `CLAUDE.md` says "Enforced at hook time by commitlint extending `@ivuorinen/commitlint-config`", and `.claude/rules/commit-format.md` closes with "Enforced by commitlint extending `@ivuorinen/commitlint-config` via a pre-commit hook."

No such gate exists. Four independent things would each have to be true for it to run, and none is:

1. `.commitlintrc.json` extends `@ivuorinen/commitlint-config`, but `package.json` declares no dependencies of any kind and `node_modules/@ivuorinen` does not exist — the config package is unresolvable.
2. `.git/hooks/` contains only `pre-commit`. There is no `commit-msg` hook, which is the only stage that can see a commit message.
3. `core.hooksPath` is unset, so `.git/hooks` is authoritative and nothing else is consulted.
4. `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no commitlint entry at any stage.

`config/husky/init.sh` survives from an earlier setup but is vestigial: husky appears nowhere in `package.json`, and the only other reference in the repo is a `.gitattributes` line for `.husky/*`.

The audit that preceded this finding marked the `commits` lens clean on the strength of the recent history conforming. That was the wrong test: it confirmed the convention was being followed, not that anything enforces it.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">The config extends a package that is not installed:

```
$ cat .commitlintrc.json
{
  "extends": ["@ivuorinen/commitlint-config"]
}

$ ls node_modules/@ivuorinen
ls: cannot access 'node_modules/@ivuorinen': No such file or directory
```

Running commitlint confirms it cannot even load its config, let alone read a commit:

```
$ yarn dlx commitlint --from e1836f1 --to HEAD
    at resolveExtends (.../@commitlint/resolve-extends/lib/index.js:149:28)
    at load (.../@commitlint/load/lib/load.js:53:28)
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```

No hook can invoke it:

```
$ ls .git/hooks/ | grep -v sample
pre-commit

$ git config core.hooksPath
(unset)

$ grep -n commitlint .pre-commit-config.yaml
(no output)
```

Partial coverage does exist in CI, and it is worth stating precisely because it is easy to mistake for the missing gate. `.github/workflows/semantic-pr.yml` runs `amannn/action-semantic-pull-request` with `validateSingleCommit: true`. That validates the **pull request title** on every PR, and additionally the commit message only when the PR contains exactly one commit. The 17 commits on this branch would pass through it unchecked.

The release path does not backstop it either: `.releaserc.json` extends `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config`, but semantic-release is invoked nowhere in `.github/` or `package.json`. Releases come from `fregante/daily-version-action` (date-based) with `loopwerk/tag-changelog`, so a malformed commit degrades the generated changelog rather than mis-versioning a release.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">The repo's commit convention is honour-system while two rule files assert it is machine-enforced. An agent reading `commit-format.md` is told "Getting the format right on the first attempt avoids a hook-failure round-trip" — it will never get that round-trip, so a malformed message lands silently on a branch or on a direct push to `main`, where no PR title check applies either.

The second-order cost is the one that matters for the enforcement chain: `no-hook-bypass.md` lists commitlint among the gates that constitute "the project's quality bar". A named gate that does not exist weakens the credibility of the list, and there is no way to tell from the rule files which of the other named gates are real.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Pick one of two directions, then make the rule files match reality either way.

**Wire it.** Add a commit-msg hook to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, supplying the config package as a hook dependency so it resolves without adding a repo-level npm dependency — this project deliberately has none:

```yaml
  - repo: https://github.com/alessandrojcm/commitlint-pre-commit-hook
    rev: v9.22.0
    hooks:
      - id: commitlint
        stages: [commit-msg]
        additional_dependencies: ["@ivuorinen/commitlint-config"]
```

The `commit-msg` stage is not installed by default. Add it explicitly so a fresh clone gets it:

```yaml
default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg]
```

Then verify against a message that must fail, rather than assuming:

```
git commit --allow-empty -m "bad message with no type"
```

Expect a non-zero exit and a commitlint error. Confirm `.git/hooks/commit-msg` exists afterwards.

**Or drop it.** Delete `.commitlintrc.json` and `config/husky/init.sh`, and rewrite the "Enforced by" sentences in `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/commit-format.md` to say what is actually true: the PR title is validated by `semantic-pr.yml`, and commit messages are convention, not gate.

Do not leave the third state, which is where the repo is now: a config file that looks like enforcement, documentation that asserts it, and nothing running.

While fixing, check `.releaserc.json` the same way — it extends a semantic-release config for a tool this repo never invokes, and is the same shape of dead configuration.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Wired via the "wire it" direction in 55eb12d. Added the alessandrojcm/commitlint-pre-commit-hook repo at v9.26.0 with stages: [commit-msg] and additional_dependencies: ["@ivuorinen/commitlint-config"], plus default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit, commit-msg], and corrected commit-format.md to name commit-msg rather than pre-commit and to state that the gate exists only after `prek install`.

Confirmed prek 0.4.12 supports language: node with additional_dependencies before writing anything — tested in a throwaway repo, where a message with no type was rejected, a conforming one passed, header-max-length 100 fired at 108 chars, and body-leading-blank failed as an ERROR (1 problems, 0 warnings) rather than a warning, which proves @ivuorinen/commitlint-config actually loaded rather than falling back to config-conventional defaults.

One thing the finding did not anticipate: installing the commit-msg stage made every hook without an explicit `stages` run a SECOND time per commit, with .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG as the file list — putting commit message prose in front of editorconfig-checker, gitleaks and the rest. Observed directly in the ruff-bump commit's output. Fixed with default_stages: [pre-commit]; `prek run --dry-run --stage commit-msg` now selects commitlint alone while pre-commit still selects all 32.

Verified live on the real repo after committing: `git commit --allow-empty -m "this message has no conventional type"` is rejected with subject-empty and type-empty, and HEAD is unchanged. prek validate-config, v8r against the schemastore pre-commit schema, yamllint and prettier all pass.

Left alone deliberately: .releaserc.json still extends @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config for a tool this repo never invokes. Same shape of dead configuration, out of scope for this change, and releases are date-based via daily-version-action so nothing depends on it.
title: commitlint is documented as a hook-time gate but is not installed, not wired, and never runs

body:
## Problem

`tests/` holds 79 bats files and 857 assertions covering `local/bin/`, `config/theme/`, `config/lib.sh` and the fish layer. `.claude/hooks/` — 14 scripts, 660 lines — has none. Nothing in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exercises them either.

This is not a uniformly-thin area; it is the area where a silent defect is least visible. A hook that stops matching still exits 0, prints nothing, and the session continues as if the guard ran. Every other script in this repo fails loudly when it breaks, which is why the untested surface is the enforcement chain rather than, say, `x-hr`.

Two defects in this audit came from the first hook examined — `git status` denied against its own documented allow (`audit-4f747a7d`) and seven bypass forms (`audit-09f208d8`). Both are single-input, single-output cases that a fixture table would have caught on the commit that introduced them. The remaining 13 hooks have not been examined to the same depth and carry the same absence of a safety net.</problem>
<parameter name="evidence">No test references any hook:

```
$ grep -rln "claude/hooks\|pre-bash-route\|pre-edit-block\|stop-lint-gate\|post-edit" tests/
(no output)
```

The untested surface:

```
$ wc -l .claude/hooks/*.sh | tail -1
  660 total
```

```
$ ls .claude/hooks/
async-bats.sh                     post-edit-rules-lint.sh   pre-edit-block.sh
log-failures.sh                   post-tool-context-mode-check.sh  pre-graphify-nudge.sh
notify-idle.sh                    pre-bash-route.sh         session-start-context.sh
post-edit-config-warn.sh          pre-ctx-write-guard.sh    stop-lint-gate.sh
post-edit-dotbot-validate.sh      post-edit-format.sh
```

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no entry under `hooks/`, so nothing runs them at commit time either.

The hooks are trivially testable — they are stdin-JSON in, stdout-JSON out:

```
$ printf '{"tool_input":{"command":"git status"}}' | bash .claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh \
    | jq -r .hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision
deny
```

That one line is the whole harness the suite is missing.</evidence>
<parameter name="impact">Every rule in `.claude/rules/` that names a hook as its enforcement — `bash-routing.md`, `read-routing.md`, `vendored-files.md`, `context-mode-issues.md`, `no-hook-bypass.md` — rests on a script that no gate verifies. A regression in any of them degrades silently: the guard stops firing, the rule text still promises it fires, and the divergence surfaces only when someone hand-tests it, as this audit did. The `git status` defect has presumably been live since the allow list was written and produced a wrong denial on every use of the repo's most common git command without anyone noticing.</impact>
<parameter name="fix">Add one bats file per hook, starting with the two that already have known defects. The repo's `.claude/skills/bats-test-scaffold` skill generates the shape; the assertions are a table of input command to expected decision:

```bash
# tests/pre-bash-route.bats
HOOK="${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh"

# Feed the hook a PreToolUse payload and print its decision, or "allow" when
# it emits no JSON at all — a no-decision response lets the call through, so
# the two must be indistinguishable to the assertions.
decision() {
  printf '{"tool_input":{"command":%s}}' "$(jq -Rn --arg c "$1" '$c')" \
    | bash "$HOOK" \
    | jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision // "allow"'
}

@test "pre-bash-route: allows the documented git readers" {
  [ "$(decision 'git status')" = "allow" ]
  [ "$(decision 'git status -s')" = "allow" ]
}

@test "pre-bash-route: denies output-producing readers" {
  [ "$(decision 'git log --oneline')" = "deny" ]
  [ "$(decision 'cat README.md')" = "deny" ]
  [ "$(decision 'yarn lint')" = "deny" ]
}

@test "pre-bash-route: a wrapper or path cannot hide a denied command" {
  [ "$(decision '/bin/cat README.md')" = "deny" ]
  [ "$(decision 'command cat README.md')" = "deny" ]
  [ "$(decision 'timeout 5 rg foo .')" = "deny" ]
  [ "$(decision 'git ls-files | xargs cat')" = "deny" ]
  [ "$(decision '/bin/bash -c "cat README.md"')" = "deny" ]
}

@test "pre-bash-route: BASH_OK passes through and strips the marker" {
  run bash -c 'printf "{\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"BASH_OK cat README.md\"}}" | bash "$1"' _ "$HOOK"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == *'"permissionDecision": "allow"'* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *'"command": "cat README.md"'* ]]
}
```

Three of those assertions fail against the current hook — that is the point; land them with the fixes for `audit-4f747a7d` and `audit-09f208d8` so the tests prove the fix rather than describe it.

Then work outward: `pre-edit-block.sh` (one case per blocked path plus one allowed path), `post-tool-context-mode-check.sh` (one case per trigger signal in `context-mode-issues.md`), `stop-lint-gate.sh`. `test-all.sh` picks the files up automatically — it globs `git ls-files '*.bats'` — but `.github/workflows/tests.yml:55` runs `bats tests/` by path, so keep the files under `tests/`.</fix>

## Evidence

## Impact

## Fix

## Resolution
Coverage is now 14 of 14 hooks, 85 assertions across six files (79acf8f, plus tests/pre-bash-route.bats landed earlier in 8e989f9). Full suite 949/949, rc=0; yarn lint rc=0.

Files: pre-bash-route (15), pre-edit-block (13), pre-ctx-write-guard (10), post-tool-context-mode-check (8), post-edit-rules-lint (8), claude-hooks-misc (26, covering post-edit-config-warn, post-edit-dotbot-validate, pre-graphify-nudge, log-failures, session-start-context, async-bats, post-edit-format, notify-idle), stop-lint-gate (5).

Each suite pins both directions — what the guard blocks and what it must NOT block, since the second is where a careless tightening does the damage: reads of vendored files stay allowed in pre-edit-block, reads and stderr redirects stay allowed in pre-ctx-write-guard, fenced blocks and backticks let a rule quote the hedge words it forbids, and the remediation tools stay exempt in post-tool-context-mode-check. stop-lint-gate pins exit 2 specifically rather than any non-zero, plus the rate-limit branch that separates an environment failure from a lint failure. notify-idle asserts untrusted hook text reaches pushover as one literal argument, which is the ingress that made the pushover eval defect reachable.

yarn, mise, corepack, bats and pushover are stubbed where invoking them would test the tool rather than the gate.

One assertion deliberately omitted: the reworded block message in post-tool-context-mode-check. The user chose to keep detection fail-closed and only reword the message, but the edit is blocked by the harness classifier on .claude/hooks/ and remains unapplied. That test pins current behaviour and names the two lines to add when it lands.

Two fixture bugs of mine surfaced and were fixed rather than papered over: a PATH so empty that `bash` itself vanished, and shfmt reformatting the new files on commit (re-staged, not bypassed).
title: The 14-file agent enforcement chain has zero test coverage, while every other script in the repo has a bats file

body:
## Problem

Pressing `U` in the Pack UI closes the float and calls `vim.pack.update()`, which opens Neovim's confirmation buffer in a new tabpage. That buffer is `modifiable = false` and carries no header, winbar, or virtual text stating how to proceed. The only way to apply the staged updates is `:write`; the only way to discard is `:quit`. Neither verb appears anywhere on screen, so the flow dead-ends for anyone who has not read `:h vim.pack.update()`.

## Evidence

Neovim 0.12.5 `$VIMRUNTIME/lua/vim/pack.lua:1149-1190` `show_confirm_buf()` sets:

    api.nvim_create_autocmd('BufWriteCmd', { buf = bufnr, nested = true, callback = finish })
    vim.bo[bufnr].modifiable = false
    vim.bo[bufnr].buftype = 'acwrite'
    vim.bo[bufnr].filetype = 'nvim-pack'

`$VIMRUNTIME/doc/pack.txt:275-276`: "Review changes. To confirm all updates execute |:write|. To discard updates execute |:quit|."

Live probe of this config (nvim 0.12.5) confirms the buffer state:

    FT=[nvim-pack] NAME=[nvim-pack://confirm#3] BH=[hide] MOD=[false] BT=[acwrite]

`config/nvim/lua/pack.lua:48-67` already hooks `FileType nvim-pack` and binds `q`/`<Esc>` to cancel, but binds nothing that announces itself and adds no confirm affordance. The comment on line 47 records `:w` as the confirm verb for the reader of the source, never for the user of the buffer.

## Impact

The primary plugin-update workflow cannot be completed from the UI it is launched from. A user who reaches the confirm buffer either abandons the update or presses `q` and silently discards it — `q` is bound, so the discard path is reachable by accident while the apply path is not reachable at all without external documentation.

## Fix

Extend the existing `FileType nvim-pack` autocmd in `config/nvim/lua/pack.lua` to set a buffer-local winbar on the confirm window naming both verbs, e.g. `vim.wo[0][0].winbar = '%#Question# :w  apply updates %*%#Comment#  ·  q / Esc  discard %*'`. Verified working: setting it from that autocmd reads back on the confirm window in a live nvim 0.12.5 run.

## Resolution
Extended the existing FileType nvim-pack autocmd in config/nvim/lua/pack.lua with a buffer-scoped winbar naming both verbs. Verified by a live headless run of the real config: winbar=[%#Question# :w %*apply updates   %#Question# q %*discard] ft=[nvim-pack] qmap=true. Scoped via vim.wo[0][0] so it does not leak to the next buffer in that window. stylua --check and yarn lint:ec clean.
title: vim.pack confirm buffer shows no affordance for :w, dead-ending the update flow

body:
## Problem

The `?` help overlay and the file header both describe `U` and `u` as actions that update plugins. Neither does. Both close the float and call `vim.pack.update()`, which downloads and stages changes, then waits for `:write` in a confirmation buffer. The help text names the trigger and omits the step that actually applies the update, so a user who follows it believes the update ran when nothing has been checked out.

## Evidence

`config/nvim/lua/pack-ui.lua:487-488` renders the help:

    add('   U       Update all plugins', 'PackUiHelp')
    add('   u       Update plugin under cursor', 'PackUiHelp')

`config/nvim/lua/pack-ui.lua:531-541` is what those keys do:

    vim.keymap.set('n', 'U', function()
      close()
      vim.pack.update()
    end, opts)

The file header repeats the claim at `config/nvim/lua/pack-ui.lua:7` (`:Pack update  close + run vim.pack.update() (all plugins)`) and `:11` (`U  update all plugins (closes UI, runs vim.pack.update)`).

Per `$VIMRUNTIME/doc/pack.txt:273-276`, `vim.pack.update()` only "show[s] confirmation buffer in a separate tabpage"; the checkout happens on `:write`.

## Impact

The one on-screen help the UI offers is wrong about its two most-used keys, and it is wrong in the direction that strands the user: it presents a two-step flow as one step and never names step two. Reported directly by the user as "I don't know how to update the packages after opening `<leader>pp` and hitting U".

## Fix

State the review step in the help lines and the header. Change `config/nvim/lua/pack-ui.lua:487-488` to name the confirm verb, e.g. `U       Review all updates (:w in review tab applies)` and `u       Review update for plugin under cursor`, and correct the header comment lines 7 and 11 to match.

## Resolution
Help lines at config/nvim/lua/pack-ui.lua:487-488 now read "Review all updates (:w in review tab applies)" and "Review update under cursor (:w applies)". Header comment lines 7 and 11 corrected, plus an added header note stating that U/u stage rather than apply. stylua --check and yarn lint:ec clean.
title: Pack UI help claims U/u update plugins; they only stage a review buffer

body:
## Problem

Both `config/nvim/README.md` and `config/nvim/CLAUDE.md` list `PackList` among the user commands defined in `lua/pack.lua`. That command does not exist. `lua/pack.lua` defines exactly two: `PackUpdate` and `PackRemove`. Typing `:PackList` yields `E492: Not an editor command`.

## Evidence

`config/nvim/README.md:7`:

    User commands (`PackUpdate`, `PackRemove`, `PackList`) live in `lua/pack.lua`.

`config/nvim/CLAUDE.md:21`:

    5. `lua/pack.lua` — PackUpdate / PackRemove / PackList user commands (vim.pack built-in,

`config/nvim/lua/pack.lua` is 67 lines and creates two commands, at line 25 (`PackUpdate`) and line 36 (`PackRemove`). A repo-wide search finds `PackList` only in the two doc files:

    config/nvim/CLAUDE.md:21
    config/nvim/README.md:7

The listing role the name implies is actually served by `:Pack` (`config/nvim/lua/pack-ui.lua:661`).

## Impact

Low: a reader looking for the plugin listing runs a command that does not exist. It also misleads an agent reading CLAUDE.md as project memory, which is the file's whole purpose.

## Fix

Drop `PackList` from both lines and name `:Pack` as the listing entry point. `config/nvim/README.md:7` becomes: "User commands (`PackUpdate`, `PackRemove`) live in `lua/pack.lua`; the `:Pack` dashboard lives in `lua/pack-ui.lua`." Make the matching edit at `config/nvim/CLAUDE.md:21`.

## Resolution
PackList removed from config/nvim/README.md:7 and config/nvim/CLAUDE.md:21. README now names :Pack as the dashboard and documents the two-step update flow; CLAUDE.md names the FileType nvim-pack hook. yarn lint:ec clean.
title: README and CLAUDE.md document a PackList command that is never defined

body:
## Problem

Class: wrong-event. `post-edit-rules-lint.sh` is block-intent: it prints "BLOCKED: hedge words found … rules in .claude/rules/ must be unconditional imperatives" and exits 2. It is wired under `PostToolUse` (`Edit|Write`). PostToolUse runs after the tool; exit 2 only feeds stderr back. The hedged rule file is already on disk, and no later gate re-checks it: `yarn lint` (Stop gate) and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` contain no hedge-word check.

## Evidence

`.claude/settings.json` PostToolUse `Edit|Write` → `post-edit-rules-lint.sh` (statusMessage "Linting .claude/rules/...").
`.claude/hooks/post-edit-rules-lint.sh:41,44` — `printf 'BLOCKED: hedge words found…'`; `exit 2`.
`package.json` `lint` chain: biome, prettier, ec, md-table, markdownlint, v8r, usage, bandit, exclusions — no rules lint. pre-commit hook ids: none.
Severity follows the command's table ("a block-intent hook uses a non-blocking event so the guard never binds" → Critical). The practical risk is a hedged rule file, lower than the label; the table was applied as written.

## Impact

A hedged rule persists whenever the agent does not act on the feedback, and edits made through Bash or the ctx sandbox never trigger the hook at all.

## Fix

Rewire as a blocking PreToolUse hook: matcher `Write|Edit`, script reads `.tool_input.file_path`, and for `*/.claude/rules/*.md` applies the existing fenced/backtick stripping + hedge regex to `.tool_input.content` (Write) or `.tool_input.new_string` (Edit); on a hit emit `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"hedge words …"}}`; on jq/awk failure deny (fail closed). Also add a pre-commit `rules-hedge-lint` hook (`files: ^\.claude/rules/.*\.md$`) running the same check so Bash/sandbox edits are caught at commit. Proof: feed a Write payload whose content contains "try to" for `.claude/rules/x.md` and show `permissionDecision: deny`.

## Resolution
post-edit-rules-lint.sh replaced by PreToolUse pre-rules-lint.sh (Edit|Write|MultiEdit) which reconstructs the resulting content and denies on hedge words; shared checker .claude/hooks/lib/rules-lint.sh also wired as pre-commit hook rules-lint. tests/pre-rules-lint.bats proves a hedged Write is denied and never lands.
title: Hedge-word rules lint prints BLOCKED from PostToolUse, which cannot block — the edit has landed

body:
## Problem

Class: unenforced rule / bypassable mechanism. `no-hook-bypass.md` forbids `git commit --no-verify` and `git push --no-verify`. The commit-time hooks are the release gate: `run-tests-before-commit.md` says the bats suite "is paid on commit rather than in CI", and commitlint runs only as a commit-msg hook. No hook, permission, or CI step blocks the bypass. `pre-bash-route.sh` allowlists `git commit`/`git push`/`git config` by subcommand, never inspecting flags, and `prek` is unknown (allowed).

## Evidence

Probes against `pre-bash-route.sh`:
```
BASH  none   | git commit --no-verify -m 'x'
BASH  none   | git commit -n -m 'x'
BASH  none   | git push --no-verify
BASH  none   | git config core.hooksPath /dev/null
BASH  none   | prek uninstall
```
(`git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit` is denied only incidentally, because `-c` is not on the subcommand allowlist.)
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:59` — `allow_git_subcmd_re='^(status|add|commit|…|config)$'`.
`.claude/settings.json` `permissions.deny` holds only curl/wget/WebFetch.
`.pre-commit-config.yaml:189-210` — bats `entry: bats --print-output-on-failure tests/`, `files: ^(tests/|local/bin/|…)`.

## Impact

A red bats suite, a malformed commit message, a shellcheck/gitleaks/detect-private-key failure — every commit-time gate — is skipped by one flag the agent can add under default permissions, and `git config core.hooksPath /dev/null` disables them for every later commit in the clone without a trace in the commit itself.

## Fix

In `pre-bash-route.sh`, add an unconditional deny block that runs on the raw command before the BASH_OK branch (so the escape cannot override it) and denies when any segment matches:
- `^git([[:space:]]+-[^[:space:]]+)*[[:space:]]+(commit|push|merge|rebase|am|cherry-pick|revert)\b.*(--no-verify|[[:space:]]-[A-Za-z]*n[A-Za-z]*\b)` for commit (`-n` is `--no-verify` only for commit/merge; scope the short form to `commit`),
- `^git[[:space:]]+config\b.*core\.hooksPath`, `-c[[:space:]]*core\.hooksPath`,
- `^(prek|pre-commit)[[:space:]]+uninstall`,
- `--no-gpg-sign`, `commit\.gpgsign=false`.
Reason text cites `.claude/rules/no-hook-bypass.md` and states the user must authorise it in-conversation. Add bats cases for each probe above asserting deny. Closure proof: re-run the five probes and show `deny`.

## Resolution
pre-bash-route.sh policy tier (before BASH_OK) denies --no-verify, git commit -n clusters, --no-gpg-sign, commit.gpgsign=false, core.hooksPath, and prek/pre-commit uninstall. All five probes deny in tests/pre-bash-route.bats; --amend/--no-edit stay allowed.
title: no-hook-bypass.md is unenforced: --no-verify, core.hooksPath and prek uninstall all pass

body:
## Problem

Class: matcher gap + self-exempting carve-out. The fish secrets read block exists only for the Read tool (`pre-edit-block.sh`) and for ctx sandbox code naming a literal `<name>.fish`. The Bash tool has no secrets check at all: `pre-bash-route.sh` only routes by command word, and any reader not on its deny list (`base64`, `python3`, `xxd`, `od`, `strings`, `bat`) is allowed. A deny-listed reader is also allowed once prefixed with `BASH_OK`, which the hook honours unconditionally. In the sandbox, a shell glob defeats the literal-name regex.

## Evidence

Probes (payload only; no secret was read):
```
BASH  none   | base64 config/fish/secrets.d/tfs.fish
BASH  none   | python3 -c 'print(open("config/secrets.d/tfs.sh").read())'
BASH  allow  | BASH_OK cat config/fish/secrets.d/tfs.fish
CTX   exit=2 | cat config/fish/secrets.d/tfs.fish
CTX   exit=0 | cat config/fish/secrets.d/*.fish
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:31-41` — BASH_OK prefix returns `permissionDecision: "allow"` with no further inspection.
`.claude/hooks/pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:42` — `secrets\.d/[[:alnum:]._-]+\.fish` does not match `*.fish`.
`.claude/rules/secrets-files.md:49-51` — "If you need to inspect a secret, ask the user — do not read or echo its contents".

## Impact

`sonar.fish`, `sonarcloud.fish`, `tfs.fish` (all 0600, live tokens) can be dumped into the transcript by any of five one-line commands, none of which trips a hook. The rule's claim that hooks enforce the no-read mandate is false for every tool except Read.

## Fix

1. In `pre-bash-route.sh`, before the BASH_OK branch, add a secrets check over the whole command string: deny when it matches `secrets\.d/` and the match is not solely `*.example` / `README.md` (same predicate as the pre-edit-block fix in the companion finding). Placing it before BASH_OK makes the escape unable to override it.
2. In `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:42`, replace the literal-name regex with the directory predicate so `secrets.d/*.fish`, `secrets.d/`, and `secrets.d/$f` all deny.
3. bats: add `base64 …secrets.d/tfs.fish`, `BASH_OK cat …secrets.d/tfs.fish`, and ctx `cat …secrets.d/*.fish` cases asserting deny.
Closure proof: re-run the five probes; every line must show `deny` / exit 2.

## Resolution
Shared secrets_referenced predicate (.claude/hooks/lib/protected-paths.sh) covers files, globs, bare directories and variables in both trees; applied to the whole Bash command before BASH_OK and to the ctx guard. Probes (base64, python3 -c, BASH_OK cat, ctx glob) deny in bats.
title: Fish secrets are readable through Bash, a ctx glob, and the BASH_OK escape

body:
## Problem

Class: matcher gap. `.claude/rules/secrets-files.md` names two live-credential trees — `config/fish/secrets.d/` and `config/secrets.d/` (sourced by `config/exports` for bash and zsh) — and states "The `.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse hook blocks edits to the real secrets files" and "do not read or echo its contents". Both guards only match fish files: `pre-edit-block.sh` matches `*/secrets.d/*.fish` for Read and Edit/Write, and `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh` matches `secrets\.d/[[:alnum:]._-]+\.fish`. The bash/zsh tree holds `.sh` files, so nothing guards it. `ctx_index` (which takes a `path`) is in no repo PreToolUse matcher at all.

## Evidence

Tree on disk: `config/secrets.d/{github.sh.example, sonar.sh (0600), tfs.sh (0600)}`.

Hook probes (payload fed on stdin; nothing executed):
```
EDIT  exit=0 | Read /Users/ivuorinen/.dotfiles/config/secrets.d/tfs.sh
EDIT  exit=0 | Edit /Users/ivuorinen/.dotfiles/config/secrets.d/tfs.sh
EDIT  exit=2 | Read /Users/ivuorinen/.dotfiles/config/fish/secrets.d/tfs.fish
CTX   exit=0 | cat config/secrets.d/tfs.sh
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-edit-block.sh:16` — `*/secrets.d/*.fish)`; `:71` — `*/secrets.d/*.fish)`.
`.claude/hooks/pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:42` — `grep -E 'secrets\.d/[[:alnum:]._-]+\.fish'`.
settings.json ctx matcher: `ctx_execute|ctx_execute_file|ctx_batch_execute` — `ctx_index` absent.

## Impact

A plain `Read config/secrets.d/tfs.sh`, an `Edit` of it, `ctx_execute_file` on it, or `ctx_index path=config/secrets.d/sonar.sh` puts the TFS/Sonar tokens into the conversation (and the ctx knowledge base) with no block, while the rule tells the agent a hook prevents exactly this. Recurring class: N-073, N-075, N-086, audit-5f0966e7 each closed one secrets gap and left this tree open.

## Fix

1. `pre-edit-block.sh`: replace both `*/secrets.d/*.fish)` arms with `*/secrets.d/*)` and exempt only `*.example` and `README.md` by basename (`*.example|README.md) exit 0 ;;`).
2. `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:42`: match `secrets\.d/` followed by anything that is not `README.md` or `*.example` — e.g. `grep -E 'secrets\.d/' | grep -vE 'secrets\.d/([[:alnum:]._-]+\.example|README\.md)([^[:alnum:]._-]|$)'` so a bare directory or glob reference also denies.
3. Add `mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_index` to the ctx matcher in `.claude/settings.json` and have the guard read `.tool_input.path` for it.
4. Add bats cases to `tests/pre-edit-block.bats` and `tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats` for `config/secrets.d/tfs.sh` (Read, Edit, ctx code, ctx_index path) asserting exit 2.
Closure proof: re-run the four probes above and show exit 2 for each.

## Resolution
pre-edit-block.sh and pre-ctx-write-guard.sh use secrets_referenced, which matches config/secrets.d/*.sh as well as the fish tree (exempting *.example and README.md); ctx_index added to the ctx matcher in settings.json and its path field is scanned. Read/Edit/ctx/ctx_index-path probes exit 2 in bats.
title: bash/zsh credentials in config/secrets.d/ are unguarded by every read and edit hook

body:
## Problem

Class: coverage-gap. The vendored/lock/submodule set is maintained separately in `pre-edit-block.sh` (case arms), `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh` (`protected=` regex), `vendored-files.md` (`paths:` + prose), and `CLAUDE.md` (Gotchas). Drift recurred: N-091 (hook blocked 1 of 6 fzf files), audit-2631ff95 (five fish helpers unprotected), audit-19fe64a4 (graphify protected by no rule), audit-2d685bd1 (CLAUDE.md omitted fish functions), and the comment at `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:20-25` records four groups missing from the sandbox guard. The drift persists today: `CLAUDE.md` says "the six fzf files" while the rule and hook cover eight (two man pages), and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` lists one. No test compares the lists.

## Evidence

Resolved N-091, audit-2631ff95, audit-19fe64a4, audit-2d685bd1. `grep -nE 'vendored-files|parity' tests/pre-edit-block.bats tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats tests/claude-hooks-misc.bats` → no matches.

## Impact

Every addition to the vendored set leaves at least one guard stale, which is how the Bash write path (agent-loopholes-cef01270) and the man-page wording drift arose.

## Fix

Make `vendored-files.md`'s `paths:` block the single source: add `tests/protected-paths-parity.bats` that parses the frontmatter `paths:` list and, for each entry (globs expanded to a sample path), asserts `pre-edit-block.sh` exits 2 on an Edit payload and `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh` exits 2 on `rm <path>`. The bats pre-commit hook already runs on `tests/` changes; add `.claude/hooks/` and `.claude/rules/vendored-files.md` to its `files:` regex so an edit to either list runs the parity test. Proof: remove one fish plugin arm from `pre-edit-block.sh` and show the test fails.

## Resolution
Single PROTECTED_RE in .claude/hooks/lib/protected-paths.sh sourced by pre-edit-block, pre-ctx-write-guard and pre-bash-route; tests/protected-paths-parity.bats checks every vendored-files.md paths: entry against all three hooks; bats pre-commit files: now includes .claude/hooks/ and vendored-files.md. CLAUDE.md fzf count corrected to eight.
title: Four hand-kept copies of the protected-path list keep drifting; no parity check exists

body:
## Problem

Class: coverage-gap. CR-003 (root CLAUDE.md 317 lines), CR-004 (`config/nvim/CLAUDE.md` 219 lines), CR-009 (root 226 lines, after CR-003 was fixed) — the same defect recurred, each hand-fixed. `config/nvim/CLAUDE.md` is at 182 lines today. The check is a line count on a known path, and no hook runs it.

## Evidence

Resolved ids CR-003, CR-004, CR-009. `wc -l`: CLAUDE.md 163, config/nvim/CLAUDE.md 182, local/bin/CLAUDE.md 63, config/theme/CLAUDE.md 20. No hook script references `CLAUDE.md` line counts.

## Impact

Guidance growth resumes unnoticed until the next audit pass; adherence drops as the file grows.

## Fix

Add a local pre-commit hook `claude-md-length` (`files: (^|/)CLAUDE\.md$`, `language: system`, `entry: bash -c 'rc=0; for f; do n=$(wc -l < "$f"); [ "$n" -le 200 ] || { echo "$f: $n lines > 200"; rc=1; }; done; exit $rc' --`). For in-session feedback, add a PostToolUse `Edit|Write` hook printing the same message to stderr with exit 2 (feedback, not a block). Proof: stage a 201-line CLAUDE.md fixture and show the hook exits 1.

## Resolution
Pre-commit hook claude-md-length (fails above 200 lines) plus in-session feedback from post-edit-lint.sh (exit 2 on a CLAUDE.md over 200 lines); bats covers 201 vs 200.
title: CLAUDE.md length overran the 200-line guideline three times with no guard

body:
## Problem

Class: context-discipline-gap. Two project rules mandate read/gather commands. `git-hunk-commits.md` explicitly says "`git-hunk list` prints output, so route it through context-mode". `graphify-first.md` mandates running `graphify query`/`path`/`explain` first for any codebase question, with no routing note. Both are read verbs, not on the must-run-direct allowlist, and a context tool (context-mode) is installed. `pre-bash-route.sh` does not recognise either command, so both run direct.

## Evidence

Router probes: `BASH none | git-hunk list -U 0`, `BASH none | graphify query "how does dfm dispatch"`.
`.claude/rules/git-hunk-commits.md` Gotchas: "`git-hunk list` prints output, so route it through context-mode".
`.claude/rules/graphify-first.md:3-6` — "run `graphify query "<question>"` first".

## Impact

`git-hunk list` prints every hunk hash with content for the whole dirty tree; `graphify query` returns a subgraph dump — both enter context on the command the rules tell the agent to run most often.

## Fix

In `pre-bash-route.sh` add to `deny_compound_res`: `'^git-hunk[[:space:]]+(list|show|diff)'` and `'^graphify[[:space:]]+(query|path|explain)'`. Leave `git-hunk commit|add|reset|stash` allowed (state mutation). Update `graphify-first.md` to say "run it through `ctx_execute`". Proof: feed both reader probes → `deny` naming `ctx_batch_execute`; feed `git-hunk commit abcd -m x` → no decision.

## Resolution
deny_compound_res gains git-hunk list/show/diff and graphify query/path/explain; git-hunk add/commit stay allowed. graphify-first.md now says to run them through ctx_execute. Probes covered in bats.
title: Rule-mandated readers `git-hunk list` and `graphify query` run on raw Bash with no routing hook

body:
## Problem

Class: coverage-gap. Rule-file frontmatter defects recur: N-074 (eight rule files lacked frontmatter), N-077 (two more), N-079 (four files used `globs:` instead of `paths:`), agent-rules-894fe54d (`alwaysApply: true` is not a Claude Code field). The only rules hook, `post-edit-rules-lint.sh`, checks hedge words; nitpicker's `check-rules-anatomy.py` validates `paths:` only when someone runs it. Nothing rejects an unknown frontmatter key at edit or commit time.

## Evidence

Resolved ledger ids N-074, N-077, N-079, agent-rules-894fe54d (titles quoted above). `.claude/hooks/post-edit-rules-lint.sh:29` pattern covers hedge words only. `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: no rules-frontmatter hook.

## Impact

A rule with `globs:` or `alwaysApply:` silently loads unconditionally or never — the N-079 incident required correcting seven files.

## Fix

First fetch code.claude.com/docs/en/memory and quote the accepted rule frontmatter keys (no-schema-guessing.md). Then add a PreToolUse hook `pre-rules-frontmatter.sh` (matcher `Write|Edit`, scope `*/.claude/rules/*.md`) that parses the frontmatter block from `.tool_input.content` (Write) or the post-edit result reconstructed from the file + `old_string`/`new_string` (Edit), and denies on any key outside the documented set or a non-list `paths:`; fail closed on parse error. Mirror it as a pre-commit hook for Bash/sandbox edits. Proof: feed a Write payload with `globs: ["*.md"]` → deny.

## Resolution
rules-lint.sh rejects frontmatter keys other than paths (documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, fetched 2026-09-21) and description (repo convention), and a non-list paths:; enforced at PreToolUse (pre-rules-lint.sh) and pre-commit (rules-lint). globs:/alwaysApply: Write payloads deny in bats; all committed rules pass.
title: Invalid rule frontmatter keys recurred four times; no hook validates them

body:
## Problem

Class: unguarded-mandate. The user's memory mandates "Run bats tests via the bare `bats` command on PATH — never via `./node_modules/.bin/bats`" (the vendored launcher breaks with `rm: command not found`), and `bats-test-scaffold` repeats it. The failure recurs: 16 `.claude/hook-failures.log` entries, DOC-006 (docs recommended the path), N-106 (`async-bats.sh` used it). `.github/copilot-instructions.md` still recommends it twice. No hook denies it: `./node_modules/.bin/bats` normalises to `bats`, which is on neither router list.

## Evidence

`.claude/hook-failures.log`: 16× `(eval):1: no such file or directory: ./node_modules/.bin/bats`.
Resolved DOC-006, N-106. Memory `feedback_bats_runner.md`.
`.github/copilot-instructions.md:50,181`.
`pre-bash-route.sh:196` — `normalise_cmd` strips to `${w##*/}` → `bats` → allowed by default.

## Impact

Each occurrence burns a tool call on a guaranteed failure, and the path keeps being re-introduced into docs.

## Fix

In `pre-bash-route.sh` add, before the segment loop: `if printf '%s' "$command" | grep -q 'node_modules/\.bin/bats'; then` emit `permissionDecision: "deny"` with reason "use bare `bats` from PATH (mise); node_modules/.bin/bats is broken". Add a bats case. Fix `.github/copilot-instructions.md:50,181`. Proof: feed `./node_modules/.bin/bats tests/dfm.bats` → `deny`; feed `bats tests/dfm.bats` → no decision.

## Resolution
pre-bash-route.sh denies any command containing node_modules/.bin/bats (policy tier); .github/copilot-instructions.md both lines now use bare bats. Bats: ./node_modules/.bin/bats deny, bats allow.
title: Recurring `./node_modules/.bin/bats` invocation has no guard — 16 logged failures

body:
## Problem

Class: unenforced rule. The rule mandates that "Personal hostnames, SSH targets, paths under `~/Code/<your-org>/`, private session lists, machine-only mise tools… must live under `hosts/<hostname>/config/<app>/...`, never in the shared `config/` tree." No PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook, pre-commit hook, or CI step inspects content written under `config/`, `base/`, or `ssh/`. gitleaks/detect-private-key target credentials, not hostnames or paths. A-001 ("Host-specific exports leak into shared `config/` tree") shows the violation has happened.

## Evidence

`pre-edit-block.sh` has no content inspection; a `Write` to `config/git/config` containing the output of `hostname -s` returns exit 0 (the case statement matches paths only).
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` hook ids: no hostname/path content check.
Resolved finding A-001 (arch): "Host-specific exports leak into shared `config/` tree".

## Impact

Machine names, org directory names, and SSH targets are published in a public dotfiles repo and break portability on other hosts; the rule is the only defence and loads only when a `config/**` file is read.

## Fix

Add a local pre-commit hook `host-leak-check` (`language: system`, `files: ^(config|base|ssh)/`, `exclude: ^hosts/`) running a script that fails when a staged file contains any of: `ls hosts/` directory names as whole words, `$(hostname -s)`, `/Users/<user>/Code/`, `~/Code/`. Add a bats test feeding a fixture with a hostname. Closure proof: stage a fixture under `config/` with `hostname -s` output and show the hook exits non-zero.

## Resolution
scripts/check-host-leak.sh wired as pre-commit host-leak-check on config|base|ssh: rejects added lines naming a hosts/ dir (>=3 chars), hostname -s, or a ~/Code / /Users/*/Code path. Added lines only, because the shared tree already carries deliberate ~/Code aliases and includeIf paths. tests/check-host-leak.bats proves rejection.
title: host-specific-config.md is unenforced: personal hostnames and ~/Code paths can land in shared config/

body:
## Problem

Class: unenforced rule + permission contradiction. `no-npm.md`: "Use `yarn` (v4+), never `npm`… Running `npm install` corrupts the lockfile… For one-off scripts: `yarn dlx <package>`, never `npx <package>`." The only mechanism it cites is the PreToolUse block on editing `yarn.lock`/`.yarn/` with the Edit tool, which `npm install` never uses. `pre-bash-route.sh` has no npm/npx entry, so both fall through to allow-by-default. `~/.claude/settings.json` `permissions.allow` contains `"Bash(npm install)"` and `"Bash(npm run build:*)"`, which pre-approves the forbidden command in this repo under `defaultMode: auto`.

## Evidence

Probes: `BASH none | npm install`, `BASH none | npx prettier --write x.yml`.
`~/.claude/settings.json` permissions.allow: `"Bash(npm install)"`, `"Bash(npm run build:*)"`.
Memory `feedback_context_mode.md` (auto-loaded context) lists "`npm install`, `pip install`" as fine on Bash — the same contradiction N-072 removed from `context-mode.md`.

## Impact

`npm install` rewrites `node_modules` against `package-lock` semantics and can create `package-lock.json` next to `yarn.lock`, breaking the Yarn Berry resolver the Stop-hook lint gate depends on — with no prompt, because the permission is pre-granted.

## Fix

In `pre-bash-route.sh` add a deny (before BASH_OK) for first word `npm|npx|pnpm|pnpx` with reason citing `no-npm.md` and naming `yarn` / `yarn dlx`. Add bats cases. The user-level allow entries serve other repos; do not edit `~/.claude/settings.json` from this repo — the project hook deny outranks them. Correct the stale memory line. Closure proof: feed `npm install` and `npx prettier` and show `deny`.

## Resolution
pre-bash-route.sh policy tier denies npm/npx/pnpm/pnpx citing no-npm.md; user-level allow entries left untouched (project hook deny outranks them). Memory line was already corrected on 2026-09-17. Probes deny in bats.
title: no-npm.md is unenforced, and user settings explicitly allow `npm install`

body:
## Problem

Class: matcher gap. `split_segments()` splits on `$(`, backticks, `||`, `&&`, `|`, `;` and strips `)`, but not on a bare `(`, `{`, a single `&`, or leading `!`, and never peels shell keywords (`if`, `then`, `do`, `while`, `for`). The first word therefore becomes `(cat`, `{`, `true`, `!`, `if`, `for` — none on either list, so the segment is allowed by default. N-127 ("Pipes, subshells, and chains bypassed first-word command matching") is recorded as fixed; the subshell half is still open, and `tests/pre-bash-route.bats` has no subshell/group/keyword case (only `mkdir -p x && cat README.md`).

## Evidence

Probes:
```
BASH  deny   | cat README.md
BASH  none   | (cat README.md)
BASH  none   | { cat README.md; }
BASH  none   | true & cat README.md
BASH  none   | ! cat README.md
BASH  none   | if cat README.md; then :; fi
BASH  none   | for f in a; do cat README.md; done
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:92-100` — gsub list lacks `(`, `{`, `}`, single `&`, `!`.

## Impact

Every routing mandate in `bash-routing.md` is defeated by wrapping the command in parentheses, and the same wrap defeats any future deny added to this hook (including the secrets and hook-bypass denies proposed in sibling findings) unless the tokenizer is fixed first.

## Fix

In `split_segments()` add `gsub(/\(/, "\n")`, `gsub(/[{}]/, "\n")`, `gsub(/&/, "\n")` (after the `&&` gsub), and strip a leading `!`. After extracting the first word, loop-drop reserved words `if|then|elif|else|do|while|until|for|case|in|time|!` (for `for x in …` drop through the `do`). Add the six probes to `tests/pre-bash-route.bats` asserting `deny`. Closure proof: re-run the probes.

## Resolution
split_segments splits on (, {, }, lone &; strip_keywords drops if/then/elif/else/do/while/until/time/! and discards for/case/select headers. All six probes deny in bats; for-loop with mkdir stays allowed.
title: Subshells, brace groups, &, ! and shell keywords hide denied commands from the Bash router

body:
## Problem

Class: unenforced rule. `git-hunk-commits.md`: "Stage and commit only through `git-hunk`… Never use `git add`, `git add -p`, or `git commit -a`." No hook blocks it: `pre-bash-route.sh` puts `add` on its git subcommand allowlist and never inspects `commit` flags. `bash-routing.md` even lists `git add <file>` as the canonical acceptable Bash use.

## Evidence

Probes:
```
BASH  none   | git add local/bin/dfm
BASH  none   | git add -A
BASH  none   | git commit -a -m x
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:59` — `allow_git_subcmd_re='^(status|add|commit|…)$'`.
Verified in a throwaway repo that `git-hunk commit` does run pre-commit/commit-msg hooks, so routing commits through it loses no gate.

## Impact

The failure mode the rule exists for — a commit carrying hunks that belong to a different change, from staging a file that holds two edits — stays one allowed command away, and the routing rule actively instructs the forbidden form.

## Fix

In `pre-bash-route.sh`, deny `git add` (any args) and `git commit` carrying `-a`/`--all`/`-am` with reason "stage with git-hunk (see .claude/rules/git-hunk-commits.md)"; keep `git add` out of the allowlist. Resolve the contradicting text in `bash-routing.md` (filed under agent-rules). Add bats cases. Closure proof: feed the three probes and show `deny`.

## Resolution
add removed from the git allowlist; policy tier denies git add (any args) and git commit with -a/--all/-am. Probes deny in bats; git-hunk commit allowed.
title: git-hunk-commits.md ban on git add / git commit -a is unenforced; the router allowlists `add`

body:
## Problem

Class: matcher gap. `context-mode.md` says "Never run a Bash command containing `curl` or `wget`". Enforcement is `permissions.deny: ["Bash(curl:*)", "Bash(wget:*)"]` plus the context-mode plugin's PreToolUse, which implements that same prefix pattern. `pre-bash-route.sh` has no curl/wget entry. A path-qualified invocation does not start with `curl`, so the prefix pattern misses it, and the repo router falls through to allow-by-default.

## Evidence

Plugin hook probe (`context-mode/1.0.169/hooks/pretooluse.mjs`):
```
curl -s https://example.com          → {"permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Blocked by security policy: matches deny pattern Bash(curl:*)"}
/usr/bin/curl -s https://example.com → {"additionalContext":"<context_guidance>…"}   (no decision)
```
Repo router probe: `BASH none | /usr/bin/curl -s https://example.com`.
`.claude/settings.json:3` — `"deny": ["Bash(curl:*)", "Bash(wget:*)", "WebFetch"]`.
Claude Code's native evaluation of `Bash(curl:*)` against `/usr/bin/curl …` was not executed (running curl is the forbidden act); the finding rests on both hooks passing it.

## Impact

Raw HTTP responses flood context, and arbitrary outbound requests (including data exfiltration via `-d @file`) run with no gate, contrary to a rule marked BLOCKED.

## Fix

`pre-bash-route.sh` already reduces `/bin/cat` to `cat` via `normalise_cmd`. Add `curl|wget|http|https|xh|aria2c` to a new `deny_network_re` checked on `fw` before the BASH_OK branch, with a reason pointing to `ctx_fetch_and_index`. Add bats cases for `/usr/bin/curl`, `env curl`, `command curl`, `\curl`. Closure proof: feed `/usr/bin/curl -s https://example.com` and show `deny`.

## Resolution
Policy tier denies curl/wget/http/https/xh/aria2c on the normalised first word, so /usr/bin/curl, env curl, command curl and \curl all deny (bats); command -v curl stays a probe.
title: curl/wget ban is bypassed by an absolute path — settings deny, repo router and plugin hook all pass it

body:
## Problem

Class: matcher gap. `vendored-files.md` says "Never modify vendored files" and "The `.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse hook (`.claude/hooks/pre-edit-block.sh`) blocks edits to every path listed above". That hook is wired to `Edit|Write|Read|MultiEdit`; `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh` covers the ctx sandbox. The Bash tool reaches the same paths through allowlisted first words (`echo`, `printf`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `ln`, `git checkout`) and `pre-bash-route.sh` never inspects redirect targets or arguments.

## Evidence

Probes against `pre-bash-route.sh`:
```
BASH  none   | echo x > config/fzf/completion.bash
BASH  none   | cp /tmp/x local/bin/fzf-tmux
BASH  none   | rm config/fish/functions/fisher.fish
BASH  none   | git checkout HEAD~5 -- local/bin/iterm2_shell_integration.zsh
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:47` — `allow_first_word_re='^(git|mkdir|chmod|chown|mv|rm|cp|touch|ln|…|echo|printf|…)$'`.
`.claude/settings.json` — `"matcher": "Edit|Write|Read|MultiEdit"` → `pre-edit-block.sh`.

## Impact

Every vendored fzf file, the graphify skill, the iTerm2 integration, the five fish plugin functions, `yarn.lock`, and the submodule trees can be overwritten or deleted with a one-line Bash command, silently, while the rule tells the agent a hook prevents it. audit-5f0966e7 closed the same gap for the ctx sandbox and left Bash open.

## Fix

Extract the protected-path regex into one shared file (e.g. `.claude/hooks/lib/protected-paths.sh` exporting `PROTECTED_RE`, sourced by `pre-edit-block.sh`, `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh`, and `pre-bash-route.sh`). In `pre-bash-route.sh`, before the BASH_OK branch, deny when a segment both matches `PROTECTED_RE` and contains a write-shaped token (`>`, `>>`, `tee`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `ln`, `truncate`, `sed -i`, `git checkout … --`, `git restore`). Add the four probes as bats cases asserting deny. Closure proof: re-run the probes and show `deny`.

## Resolution
pre-bash-route.sh sources PROTECTED_RE and denies any segment naming a protected path together with a write shape (>, tee, cp, mv, rm, ln, truncate, sed -i, git checkout/restore/rm/mv/apply/reset). The four probes plus rm -rf tools/dotbot deny in bats; parity test covers every vendored path.
title: Vendored, lock and submodule files are writable through Bash — the guard only matches Edit/Write

## Problem

Contradictory mandates across two unconditional rule files. `git-hunk-commits.md`: "Stage and commit only through `git-hunk`… Never use `git add`, `git add -p`, or `git commit -a`." `bash-routing.md` "When Bash is acceptable" case 1 names `git add <file>` first among side-effect commands, and its forbidden-patterns/practical sections never mention git-hunk. `.claude/rules/context-mode-issues.md` and the router's deny reason text (`git add/commit/mv/rm/push`) repeat the same sanction.

## Evidence

`.claude/rules/git-hunk-commits.md:3-4` — "Never use `git add`, `git add -p`, or `git commit -a`."
`.claude/rules/bash-routing.md:39-41` — "`git add <file>`, `git commit -m '...'`, `git mv`, `git rm`, …"
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:323` — "Bash is reserved for state mutations (git add/commit/mv/rm/push, …)".

## Impact

Both files load every session; an agent following bash-routing.md stages by path, which is the failure git-hunk-commits.md was added (commit 0b39154c, the latest commit) to prevent.

## Fix

In `bash-routing.md` case 1 replace `git add <file>`, `git commit -m '...'` with `git-hunk commit <hash>... -m '...'`, `git-hunk add <hash>` and add "(`git add` is forbidden — `.claude/rules/git-hunk-commits.md`)". Update the deny reason string in `pre-bash-route.sh:323` to name `git-hunk commit` instead of `git add/commit`.

## Resolution
bash-routing.md case 1 now names git-hunk commit/add and states git add / git commit -a are forbidden; router deny reason names git-hunk commit. context-mode-issues.md carried no git add sanction on inspection.
title: bash-routing.md sanctions `git add <file>`; git-hunk-commits.md forbids it

## Problem

MISPLACED rules (tiebreaker: removing each would permit a prohibited action):
1. "Python packages come from `config/mise/default-python-packages`, not pip by hand" — forbids `pip install`.
2. "Run `mise install` after adding new tools." — prescribes a step after editing `config/mise/config.toml`.
3. `config/lib.sh` "Load-time invariant: … It never runs `set -e`, installs traps, or calls `exit` at the top level; scripts opt into those via `lib::strict` / `lib::trap_cleanup`." — forbids adding top-level side effects to lib.sh.

## Evidence

`CLAUDE.md` § "mise — Unified Tool Manager" (both 1 and 2) and § "Centralized Logging (`config/lib.sh`)" → "**Load-time invariant:**" (3). None appears in any `.claude/rules/*.md` (grep of the 20 rule files).
The graphify vendored skill's pip install step (filed under agent-loopholes) is live evidence that mandate 1 is not reaching the agent as a rule.

## Impact

CLAUDE.md is advisory context; three prohibitions that have enforcement consequences get no dedicated rule injection or path scoping.

## Fix

Create `.claude/rules/mise-packages.md` (paths: `config/mise/**`, `.mise.toml`) with "Never `pip install`, `uv tool install`, or `uv pip install` by hand; add Python packages to `config/mise/default-python-packages`." and "Run `mise install` after adding a tool to `config/mise/config.toml`." Create `.claude/rules/lib-sh-side-effects.md` (paths: `config/lib.sh`) with "Never add `set -e`, `trap`, or `exit` at the top level of `config/lib.sh`; scripts opt in through `lib::strict` / `lib::trap_cleanup`." Remove the imperatives from CLAUDE.md, leaving one-line pointers.

## Resolution
New rules mise-packages.md (no hand pip/uv installs; mise install after adding a tool) and lib-sh-side-effects.md; CLAUDE.md keeps one-line pointers only.
title: Three behavioural mandates still live in root CLAUDE.md instead of .claude/rules/

## Problem

Contradictory mandates. `no-schema-guessing.md`: "You must not guess, assume, infer, or extrapolate any key name or value." `validate-config-schemas.md` "When extrapolation is fine": "Only when the field is freeform (regex, glob list, log message text, secrets value)." For a schema-less YAML/TOML file both rules load (the former unconditionally, the latter by path) and give opposite answers for a freeform value.

## Evidence

`.claude/rules/no-schema-guessing.md:8` — "**You must not guess, assume, infer, or extrapolate any key name or value.**"
`.claude/rules/validate-config-schemas.md:51-55` — "## When extrapolation is fine / Only when the field is freeform…"

## Impact

The agent picks whichever rule it quotes; the carve-out is broad enough ("glob list", "regex") to cover values whose syntax a tool does parse.

## Fix

Delete the "When extrapolation is fine" section from `validate-config-schemas.md` and, in `no-schema-guessing.md`, narrow the mandate explicitly: "any key name, or any value whose accepted set is defined by the tool (enums, flags, formats). Freeform content the user supplied (messages, secrets) is not a guess." One source, one wording.

## Resolution
"When extrapolation is fine" deleted from validate-config-schemas.md; no-schema-guessing.md mandate narrowed to key names and tool-defined values, with user-supplied freeform content explicitly not a guess. One source.
title: validate-config-schemas.md allows extrapolating freeform values; no-schema-guessing.md forbids guessing any value

## Problem

Class: harness-mismatch (mandate expressed as prose where the harness supports a hook). `shell-validate`, `fish-validate`, and `yaml-validate` say "After editing any … validate it" (shellcheck; `fish --no-execute`; yamllint/actionlint). They are model-invoked skills, so they run only when the agent chooses. Claude Code supports PostToolUse feedback hooks for exactly this, and the repo already uses the pattern for formatting (`post-edit-format.sh`) and Dotbot (`post-edit-dotbot-validate.sh`). `shell-scripts.md` even describes shell-validate as running "after each Edit/Write".

## Evidence

`.claude/skills/shell-validate/SKILL.md:11-13`, `fish-validate/SKILL.md:13`, `yaml-validate/SKILL.md:10`; `.claude/settings.json` PostToolUse `Edit|Write` list has no shellcheck/fish/yamllint hook; `.claude/rules/shell-scripts.md:25-26`.

## Impact

Lint errors surface only at commit time (after a ~5 minute bats run on covered paths) instead of on the edit that introduced them.

## Fix

Add `.claude/hooks/post-edit-lint.sh` wired PostToolUse `Edit|Write`: dispatch on path/shebang — shell (shebang bash/sh or `# shellcheck shell=`) → `shellcheck -f gcc "$fp"`; `*.fish` → `fish --no-execute "$fp"`; `*.yml|*.yaml` → `yamllint -f parsable "$fp"` and `actionlint "$fp"` under `.github/workflows/`. Print only failing lines to stderr and exit 2 on failure (feedback); report "X not available" instead of skipping silently; skip vendored paths via the shared protected-path list. Proof: write a shell file with `echo $foo` unquoted and show stderr contains SC2086 with exit 2.

## Resolution
New PostToolUse post-edit-lint.sh: shellcheck (by shebang/directive), fish --no-execute, yamllint, actionlint for workflows; reports missing linters, skips PROTECTED_RE paths, exit 2 feedback. Bats proves SC2086 is reported. It caught a real YAML error in .pre-commit-config.yaml during this run.
title: Post-edit validation (shellcheck, fish syntax, yamllint) is prose in skills, with no hook

## Problem

Class: over-permissioned-bash. `settings.local.json` allows `Bash(gh api:*)`. `gh api` returns raw JSON API responses — a gather command, not on the must-run-direct allowlist — and `pre-bash-route.sh` has no `gh` entry, so the allow is unconstrained. The other reader allows in that file (`cat`, `ls`, `wc`, `sed -n`, `awk`, `grep -v`, `fish -c … | head`) are neutralised by router denies; `gh api` is the one that is not.

## Evidence

`.claude/settings.local.json` — `"Bash(gh api:*)"`. Router probe: `BASH none | gh api repos/x/y/pulls`.

## Impact

A paginated PR/comments listing can put tens of KB of JSON into context with no prompt.

## Fix

Add `'^gh[[:space:]]+(api|pr[[:space:]]+(view|diff|list)|issue[[:space:]]+(view|list)|run[[:space:]]+view)'` to `deny_compound_res` in `pre-bash-route.sh` (project-level; do not edit the gitignored settings.local.json — the user can drop the allow entry). Proof: feed `gh api repos/x/y/pulls` → `deny`.

## Resolution
deny_compound_res gains gh api / pr view|diff|list / issue view|list / run view; settings.local.json left for the user. gh api and gh pr view deny in bats.
title: `Bash(gh api:*)` is pre-allowed and gh passes the router unrouted

## Problem

Class: semantic validator gap. The rule's only enforcement is a manual grep that "A non-empty result is a regression". Its regex requires the key argument in double quotes (`"[^"]*"`). Every `K.*` call in `config/nvim` uses single quotes (stylua quote style), so the grep returns nothing whether or not a description is missing — the check cannot fail. It also only recognises single-line two-argument calls, so a three-argument `K.d(key, mode, cmd)` without opts is never matched. `config/nvim/CLAUDE.md:58-59` claims the requirement "is enforced by" this rule.

## Evidence

`.claude/rules/keymap-descriptions.md:24` — `grep -nrE '\bK\.(n|nl|d|ld)\(\s*"[^"]*"\s*,\s*[^,)]+\)\s*$' config/nvim/`.
Call-site quote census: `K.nl('` ×40, `K.n('` ×11, `K.ld('` ×10, `K.d('` ×4; zero double-quoted.
Rule regex hit count: 0.

## Impact

A keymap added without a description passes the documented check, leaving the binding unlabelled in mini.clue, and the rule reports the check as green.

## Fix

Replace the check with a Lua-aware scan run by `stylua`-independent script `scripts/check-keymap-desc.lua` (nvim `--headless -l`) that stubs `K.n/K.nl/K.d/K.ld`, loads `lua/keymaps.lua` and plugin sections, and errors when `opts` is nil or lacks `desc`. Wire it as a pre-commit hook scoped `files: ^config/nvim/.*\.lua$`. Update the rule text and `config/nvim/CLAUDE.md:58`. Closure proof: add `K.nl('zz', ':echo<cr>')` to a fixture and show the check exits non-zero.

## Resolution
scripts/check-keymap-desc.py (quote/comment/function-body aware Lua scan; string opts or table with desc pass) wired as pre-commit keymap-desc; keymap-descriptions.md and config/nvim/CLAUDE.md updated. K.nl('zz', ':echo<cr>') fixture fails; committed config passes (tests/check-keymap-desc.bats).
title: keymap-descriptions.md verification grep matches only double quotes; the repo uses single quotes

body:
## Problem

Class: semantic validator gap. The guard denies only when a protected path and a write-shaped token appear on the same line (`grep -E "$protected" | grep -qE "$writeish"`). Assigning the path on one line and writing on the next passes. The `ponytail:` comment acknowledges the heuristic; it remains an exploitable bypass of `vendored-files.md`.

## Evidence

Probes:
```
CTX   exit=0 | p='local/bin/fzf-tmux'⏎require('fs').writeFileSync(p,'x')
CTX   exit=0 | f=config/fzf/completion.bash⏎printf x > "$f"
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:35` — `printf '%s\n' "$cleaned" | grep -E "$protected" | grep -qE "$writeish"`.

## Impact

Any vendored/lock/submodule file can be overwritten from the sandbox with a two-line snippet, which is also the natural shape of real code.

## Fix

Evaluate co-occurrence over the whole payload, not per line: `if printf '%s' "$cleaned" | grep -qE "$protected" && printf '%s' "$cleaned" | grep -qE "$writeish"; then … exit 2`. Accept the false positives on read-only code that mentions a protected path and writes elsewhere (the reason text already points to Write/Edit). Update the `ponytail:` comment to the new ceiling. Add both probes to `tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats`. Closure proof: re-run the probes, exit 2.

## Resolution
pre-ctx-write-guard.sh checks protected path and write shape over the whole executed payload (code/commands), not per line; ponytail comment updated. Both variable-split probes exit 2 in bats. ctx_execute_file's path (read-only) no longer counts toward the write check.
title: pre-ctx-write-guard same-line heuristic is bypassed by putting the path in a variable

body:
## Problem

Class: semantic validator gap. `validate-config-schemas.md` is path-scoped to `**/*.yml, **/*.yaml, **/*.json, **/*.toml` and says to validate "any structured-config file… against its JSON Schema before committing". Both mechanisms — the pre-commit `v8r` hook and `yarn lint:v8r` in the Stop gate — pass the same five literal filenames. Every other schema-backed file in the repo is never schema-checked.

## Evidence

`.pre-commit-config.yaml:108` — `files: ^(\.mega-linter\.yml|\.pre-commit-config\.yaml|biome\.json|package\.json|\.markdownlint\.json)$`.
`package.json` `lint:v8r` — `v8r .mega-linter.yml .pre-commit-config.yaml biome.json package.json .markdownlint.json`.
Tracked schema-store candidates outside the list: `.codacy.yml`, `.github/renovate.json`, `.mise.toml`, `config/mise/config.toml`, `.yamllint.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, `stylua.toml`.

## Impact

The rule's own motivating failure (a silently ignored misspelled key → CI regressions → force-push) remains possible in renovate, mise, codacy, and pyproject config, while the rule reads as gated.

## Fix

Change the pre-commit hook to `files: \.(ya?ml|json|toml)$` with `exclude: ^(tools/|config/cheat/cheatsheets/|node_modules/|graphify-out/|docs/audit/|\.claude/skills/graphify/)` and pass `--ignore-schema-not-found` (confirm the flag name from `yarn dlx v8r --help` before writing it — no-schema-guessing.md). Mirror the same set in `lint:v8r` via a glob. Closure proof: stage `.github/renovate.json` with an unknown top-level key and show the hook exits non-zero.

## Resolution
v8r pre-commit hook now files: \.(ya?ml|json|toml)$ with excludes and --ignore-errors (flag from v8r 6.1.0 --help; not --ignore-schema-not-found); yarn lint:v8r mirrors it. Coverage 5 -> 24 validated files; config/gh/ excluded (gh-rewritten, fails schemastore on version). Proof: .yamllint.yml copy with an unknown key exits 99. renovate.json matches two schemas and passes unchecked — documented in validate-config-schemas.md.
title: v8r gate covers 5 hardcoded files; validate-config-schemas.md mandates it for every YAML/JSON/TOML

body:
## Problem

Class: semantic validator gap. `bash-routing.md` default rule: "If a shell command produces output you intend to read, use `ctx_batch_execute`." The hook enforces a fixed first-word deny list and then allows anything else ("Unknown command… Allow by default"). File and data readers outside that list pass.

## Evidence

Probes:
```
BASH  none   | python3 -c 'print(open("README.md").read())'
BASH  none   | diff CLAUDE.md local/bin/CLAUDE.md
BASH  none   | bat README.md
BASH  none   | base64 config/fish/secrets.d/tfs.fish
```
`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:64` deny list; `:311-313` allow-by-default comment.

## Impact

Arbitrarily large file and diff output enters context through commands the rule classifies as routed, and every hardening of the deny list is sidestepped by switching readers.

## Fix

Extend `deny_first_word_re` with the readers that exist on this machine and emit file content: `diff|cmp|bat|xxd|od|strings|base64|column|sort|uniq|cut|nl|fold|rev|tac|paste|comm|join|file|stat|du|lsof|ps`. Add `deny_compound_res` entries `^(python3?|node|perl|ruby)[[:space:]]+(-c|-e)` for inline-code readers. Add bats cases. Closure proof: re-run the probes, `deny`.

## Resolution
deny_first_word_re extended with diff/cmp/bat/xxd/od/strings/base64/column/sort/uniq/cut/nl/fold/rev/tac/paste/comm/join/file/stat/du/lsof/ps; deny_compound_res adds python3?/node/perl/ruby -c|-e. Probes deny in bats. Allow-by-default for unlisted commands kept, marked with a ponytail comment.
title: Router allows unlisted readers by default though bash-routing.md routes every output you read

body:
## Problem

Class: self-exempting carve-out. `bash-routing.md` limits `BASH_OK` to "a single one-line command the user names by tool in their most recent message… whose expected output is under twenty lines". The hook honours the prefix for any command, any output size, in any turn, and returns `allow` (which also skips the permission prompt). The rule's conditions are unverifiable by the mechanism that grants the exception.

## Evidence

`.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:31-41` — prefix match → `permissionDecision: "allow"` with `updatedInput`.
Probe: `BASH allow | BASH_OK cat config/fish/secrets.d/tfs.fish`.

## Impact

The escape swallows every routing deny the hook has, and any future deny placed after it; `context-mode-issues.md` already has to forbid leaning on it turn after turn because nothing stops that.

## Fix

Add a `UserPromptSubmit` hook `.claude/hooks/prompt-record.sh` that writes the prompt text to `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/.last-prompt` (gitignored, 0600). In `pre-bash-route.sh`, honour `BASH_OK` only when the stripped command's normalised first word occurs as a word in that file; otherwise deny with reason "BASH_OK requires the user to name the command in their latest message". Keep all security denies (secrets, hook bypass, protected paths, network) ahead of the escape. Closure proof: with `.last-prompt` lacking `cat`, feed `BASH_OK cat README.md` → `deny`; with it containing `cat`, → `allow`.

## Resolution
UserPromptSubmit hook prompt-record.sh writes the prompt to gitignored .claude/.last-prompt (0600); pre-bash-route.sh honours BASH_OK only when the command's first word occurs in it, and all policy denies run first. Bats: deny without the word or without the file, allow with it.
title: BASH_OK escape is honour-system: the hook cannot tell whether the user named the command

body:
## Problem

Class: rationalizable step. Three skill bodies give the agent quotable permission to skip or soften a required step: `lua-format` "If stylua is not available, skip formatting silently."; `yaml-validate` "If actionlint is not available, skip silently."; `new-script` "POSIX scripts (`/bin/sh`) should NOT source msgr" (msgr is bash; sourcing it breaks a POSIX script, so this is a hard requirement, not advice). A silent skip is indistinguishable from a pass in the transcript.

## Evidence

`.claude/skills/lua-format/SKILL.md:18`; `.claude/skills/yaml-validate/SKILL.md:34`; `.claude/skills/new-script/SKILL.md:38`.

## Impact

A workflow file edit reports as validated with actionlint never run; a Lua edit reports as formatted with stylua absent; a POSIX script can be scaffolded sourcing a bash library.

## Fix

`lua-format:18` → "If stylua is not available, say so in the response: `stylua not available — <file> not formatted`." `yaml-validate:34` → "If actionlint is not available, report `actionlint not available — <file> not validated`." `new-script:38` → "POSIX scripts (`/bin/sh`) must never source msgr." Closure proof: diff shows the three sentences replaced.

## Resolution
lua-format and yaml-validate now report the missing tool instead of skipping silently; new-script says POSIX scripts must never source msgr.
title: Skill steps say "skip silently" and "should NOT" where the intent is mandatory

body:
## Problem

Class: rationalizable step (mandatory skill step contradicting a project mandate). Root `CLAUDE.md`: "Python packages come from `config/mise/default-python-packages`, not pip by hand". The vendored skill's Step 1 — under "Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps." — runs `uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy` or `"$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages`. The skill cannot be edited (vendored-files.md), `pre-bash-route.sh` does not deny `pip`/`uv tool install`, and the CLAUDE.md mandate is not in a rule file.

## Evidence

`.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md:86-95` — `uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy -q` / `"$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages`; `:59` "Do not skip steps."
Router: `pip`, `python3 -m pip`, `uv` are not on either list → allowed.

## Impact

Invoking `/graphify` on a host where the import probe fails installs into system Python with `--break-system-packages` or upgrades a uv tool outside mise — the exact drift the mise migration removed.

## Fix

1. Add `graphifyy` to `config/mise/default-python-packages` (or pin graphify in `config/mise/config.toml`) so Step 1's import probe succeeds and the install branch never runs.
2. Add a `pre-bash-route.sh` deny for `pip install`, `python3? -m pip install`, `uv tool install`, `uv pip install` citing the CLAUDE.md mandate (and migrate that mandate into a rule — filed under agent-rules).
Closure proof: feed `python3 -m pip install graphifyy --break-system-packages` and show `deny`.

## Resolution
graphifyy added to config/mise/default-python-packages so the skill's import probe succeeds; pre-bash-route.sh denies pip install, python3 -m pip install, uv tool install, uv pip install (bats). Mandate migrated to .claude/rules/mise-packages.md.
title: Vendored graphify skill mandates pip/uv installs that CLAUDE.md forbids, and nothing blocks them

body:
## Problem

The rule states: "Pre-commit hooks run shellcheck, yamllint, and actionlint, but none of them schema-check `.mega-linter.yml` or other tool-specific files. The Stop-hook's `yarn lint` aggregator skips them too. There is no automatic safety net". Both claims are false: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has a `v8r` hook on `.mega-linter.yml` and four other files, and `yarn lint` runs `yarn lint:v8r` on the same five. The table also lists `yarn dlx v8r .mega-linter.yml` as a manual step.

## Evidence

`.claude/rules/validate-config-schemas.md:57-62`; `.pre-commit-config.yaml:100-108` (`id: v8r`, comment "see .claude/rules/validate-config-schemas.md"); `package.json` `lint` → `… && yarn lint:v8r && …`.

## Impact

The rule misstates its own enforcement, so an agent cannot tell which files are gated and which rely on discipline.

## Fix

Replace the "Why a Stop-hook does not replace this rule" section with: "`v8r` runs in pre-commit and in `yarn lint` for `.mega-linter.yml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `biome.json`, `package.json`, `.markdownlint.json`. Every other schema-backed file relies on running `yarn dlx v8r <file>` by hand." Adjust the table rows accordingly.

## Resolution
validate-config-schemas.md's false "no automatic safety net" section replaced by "What the gates cover", describing the broadened v8r pre-commit/yarn lint coverage and its excludes and blind spots.
title: validate-config-schemas.md says no hook schema-checks .mega-linter.yml; a v8r hook does
