## Problem

Each file mixes two distinct competency areas.
- `context-mode.md` = tool routing, plus "## Output constraints": "Keep responses under 500 words." and "Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to FILES — never return them as inline text." Response length and artifact delivery are not routing.
- `run-tests-before-commit.md` = running the bats suite before commit, plus "## Deleting something means grepping for it first" (repo-wide `git grep` before removing any subcommand/key, graphify usage for coverage).

## Evidence

`.claude/rules/context-mode.md` § "Output constraints"; `.claude/rules/run-tests-before-commit.md:39-72`.

## Impact

The deletion mandate is path-scoped with the test rule and never loads when deleting a key from, e.g., `config/tmux/tmux.conf` or `install.conf.yaml`; the reply-length mandate is hidden inside a routing file where no one looks for it.

## Fix

Move "Deleting something means grepping for it first" into a new unconditional `.claude/rules/grep-before-delete.md`. Move the output constraints to the user-level `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (they are personal reply preferences, see the Advisory finding) or to `.claude/rules/response-format.md`. Leave each source file with its single topic.

## Resolution
Deletion hygiene moved to new unconditional rule grep-before-delete.md; output constraints removed from context-mode.md (global destination tracked in agent-rules-296b9ec8). Each source file now holds one topic.
title: Two grab-bag rule files: context-mode.md adds reply-length rules; run-tests-before-commit.md adds deletion hygiene

## Problem

A `paths:`-scoped rule loads when a matching file is read. `secrets-files.md` is scoped to `config/fish/secrets.d/**` and `config/secrets.d/**`, and its central mandate is "do not read or echo its contents". The rule therefore enters context only after the read it forbids, and never for Bash or ctx sandbox access (which do not trigger path loading). The same structure affects `vendored-files.md` for Bash writes.

## Evidence

`.claude/rules/secrets-files.md:3-5` (`paths:`) and `:49-51` (never read). Hook gaps that let the read happen are filed as agent-loopholes-da375736 and agent-loopholes-4cafa9a8.

## Impact

For a security mandate the scoping inverts the purpose; the agent has no instruction in context at the moment it decides whether to open a secrets file.

## Fix

Remove the `paths:` block from `secrets-files.md` so it loads every session (it is ~50 lines; keep only the never-commit / never-read / modes mandates and move the `dfm secrets` procedure to `docs/`).

## Resolution
paths: removed from secrets-files.md so it loads every session; trimmed to never-read / never-commit / modes / enforcement; dfm secrets procedure and mode rationale moved to docs/secrets.md.
title: secrets-files.md is path-scoped, so its never-read rule loads only after a secret is read

## Problem

Rules-to-rules duplication without contradiction. `context-mode.md` § "Bash shell commands" restates the bash-routing default ("`ctx_batch_execute` is the default for any command producing output you intend to read — searches … included, and never truncated with `| head`"), and § "Read for analysis" restates read-routing's default ("Reading to analyze, explore, or summarize → use `ctx_execute_file`"). Both target files exist precisely to own those mandates, and prior findings agent-rules-7ecfe1c4 and N-084 were this same duplication drifting.

`.claude/rules/context-mode.md` §§ "Bash shell commands", "Read for analysis"; `.claude/rules/bash-routing.md` § "The default rule"; `.claude/rules/read-routing.md` § "The default rule".

Three unconditional files carry the same two mandates; the next edit to one drifts from the others, as it already did twice.

Cut both sections in `context-mode.md` down to a single pointer line each ("Bash: `.claude/rules/bash-routing.md`." / "Read: `.claude/rules/read-routing.md`.") with no restated imperative.

## Resolution
context-mode.md "Bash shell commands" and "Read for analysis" cut to one pointer line each, no restated imperative.
title: context-mode.md restates mandates owned by bash-routing.md and read-routing.md

body:
## Problem

1. `run-tests-before-commit.md:88` — "The suite takes about 30 seconds." `.pre-commit-config.yaml:191` — "~5min for 1005 tests (measured 2026-09-13; the "~30s" this comment used to claim predates most of the suite)".
2. `shell-scripts.md:25-26` — "The `shell-validate` skill runs both shellcheck and shfmt after each Edit/Write." The skill has no shfmt step and is prose, not a hook; shfmt runs from `post-edit-format.sh`, shellcheck runs from no edit hook.
3. `vendored-files.md:60-61` — "`.pre-commit-config.yaml` excludes the vendored shell files from `shfmt`." The exclude covers only `config/fzf/(key-bindings|completion).(bash|zsh)`; `local/bin/fzf-tmux` (bash, vendored) is not excluded. Separately, `pre-edit-block.sh:39` tells the agent to "update via submodule sync" while the rule says "The repo has no fzf submodule".
4. `bash-routing.md` — "`git status` is the one git reader the hook lets through". The allowlist also passes `reflog`, `stash` (`stash show -p`), `branch`, `remote`, `tag`, `notes`, `worktree`.

## Evidence

Quoted lines above; `.pre-commit-config.yaml:120` shfmt `exclude`; `.claude/hooks/pre-bash-route.sh:59` allowlist.

## Impact

Agents budget a 30s gate that takes 5 minutes (and reach for `--no-verify`), assume shellcheck runs on every edit, and trust vendored-file and routing claims that are wrong.

## Fix

1. "about 30 seconds" → "about five minutes (1005 tests)". 2. Rewrite to "`post-edit-format.sh` runs shfmt after each Edit/Write; shellcheck runs at commit time (pre-commit) — run the `shell-validate` skill for it during editing." 3. Add `local/bin/fzf-tmux` to the shfmt `exclude` (or correct the sentence), and change the hook message to "refresh from upstream (see vendored-files.md)". 4. Rewrite to "`git status` and the plumbing/state subcommands on the allowlist pass; `git log/diff/show/blame` are denied."

## Resolution
1) run-tests-before-commit.md now says ~five minutes (1005 tests). 2) shell-scripts.md names post-edit-format (shfmt) and post-edit-lint (shellcheck). 3) local/bin/fzf-tmux added to the shfmt exclude; pre-edit-block message no longer says "submodule sync". 4) bash-routing.md describes git status plus the allowlisted state/plumbing subcommands.
title: Four rule files make factual claims the implementation contradicts

body:
## Problem

In light mode the prompt's `[directory]` and `[os]` modules use `style = "sky"`, which is `#04a5e5`. Measured against Latte base `#eff1f5`, that is 2.47:1. WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for normal text. The path is on screen at every prompt, and this is the light-blue text reported as hard to read. Other modules also fall below 3:1: hostname and php (lavender, 2.81), username (peach, 2.64), git_branch, git_status and nodejs (green, 2.96), and git_state and python (yellow, 2.31).

## Evidence

`[os] style = "sky"` (L78) and `[directory] style = "sky"` (L120). The palette block sets `sky = "#04a5e5"`. Ratios were computed with the WCAG 2 relative-luminance formula against `base = "#eff1f5"`. Upstream catppuccin/catppuccin#2588 ("Align palette colours to WCAG Level AA") is open and marked as not being pursued, so no official higher-contrast Latte exists.

## Impact

The current directory, which is the most-read prompt segment, is hard to read in light mode. Git state and language segments are also below 3:1.

## Fix

Override accent values inside `[palettes.catppuccin_latte]` only. That keeps the file's invariant that dark and light differ only in the palette block. Each value keeps its HSL hue and saturation and has its lightness lowered to reach 4.5:1 or more on base: sky `#0374a1` (4.62), sapphire `#187787` (4.61), lavender `#3d5afc` (4.57), green `#327c21` (4.60), yellow `#996114` (4.56), peach `#be4601` (4.57), teal `#13797e` (4.57). Add a comment stating the deviation from upstream Latte and the reason for it.

## Resolution
The [palettes.catppuccin_latte] accents now use values darkened to reach AA with the same hue (sky #0374a1 is 4.62:1). A re-check shows no accent below 4.5:1, and yarn lint passes.
title: Light starship prompt renders the path in Latte sky at 2.47:1 on base

`eza.light.yml` (copied from catppuccin/eza, latte-green) puts 32 of its 80 colour values below 3:1 against `#eff1f5`. That includes directories and executables (green `#40a02b`, 2.96), write permissions and modified files (yellow `#df8e1d`, 2.31), and `symlink_path`, `minor` and `unit_kilo` (sky `#04a5e5`, 2.47). `dircolors.light` is derived from the same palette, so `ls` shows the same colours: DIR/EXEC `38;2;64;160;43` at 2.96.

## Evidence

eza.light.yml L9 `directory: {foreground: "#40a02b"}`, L36 `minor: {foreground: "#04a5e5"}`, L43 `unit_kilo`, L102 `symlink_path: {foreground: "#04a5e5"}`, L62 `modified: {foreground: "#df8e1d"}`. dircolors.light L94 `DIR 38;2;64;160;43;01`, L104 `EXEC 38;2;64;160;43;01`.

Directory names, sizes and symlink targets are hard to read in every `eza`/`ls` listing in light mode.

In dircolors.light, change the matching 38;2 triplets (green becomes `50;124;33`). Record the deviation from upstream in each file's header comment.

In eza.light.yml and dircolors.light, the accent hex values and RGB triplets were replaced with the AA set. Muted greys stay as upstream on purpose. gdircolors -b parses the file, and the eza/dircolors handler bats tests pass.

## Problem

The dark-mode AA pass lifted only the terminal ANSI red (autumnRed #c34043 -> #cf6769) in wezterm and fish. The vendored Wave vim scheme, the Wave bat tmTheme and nvim's Wave still use upstream foregrounds below 4.5:1 on #1f1f28: samuraiRed #e82424 (Error, ErrorMsg, diagnostics) 3.66:1, autumnRed #c34043 (DiffDelete) 3.22:1, dragonBlue #658594 (MoreMsg) 4.15:1. nvim overrides only autumnRed; samuraiRed and dragonBlue are untouched.

## Evidence

config/vim/colors/kanagawa_wave.vim:48 `hi DiffDelete ... guifg=#c34043`; :52-53 `hi Error`/`hi ErrorMsg ... guifg=#e82424`; :71 `hi MoreMsg ... guifg=#658594`. config/bat/themes/Kanagawa Wave.tmTheme:384 `#E82424`. config/nvim/init.lua:613-632 palette overrides: autumnRed only among Wave colours. check_contrast (tests/theme-contrast.bats) run over the Wave files reports: `#e82424 is 3.66:1`, `#c34043 is 3.22:1`, `#658594 is 4.15:1` on #1f1f28. ## Impact

The migration's stated goal was dark-mode readability. Error messages and diagnostics — the text that most needs reading — are less legible in Kanagawa Wave than in the Catppuccin Mocha it replaced, and no test would notice a regression.

Extend tests/theme-contrast.bats with a Wave check mirroring the Lotus one (check_contrast '#1f1f28' 4.5 over palettes.d/kanagawa/dark, the Wave vim/bat/television/fish-[dark] files; muted #727169 #717c7c), plus a planted-negative case.

## Resolution
Lifted samuraiRed #e82424->#ed4f4f, autumnRed #c34043->#cf6769, dragonBlue #658594->#6b8b9a (HSL lightness only, >=4.5:1 on #1f1f28) in kanagawa_wave.vim, Kanagawa Wave.tmTheme, nvim colors.palette and wezterm brights. tests/theme-contrast.bats now checks every Wave file like Lotus, plus a planted samuraiRed negative; nvim DiagnosticError verified as #ed4f4f.

## Problem

tests/theme-handlers.bats (tmux reload-once, slow-reload budget, missing-config) and tests/theme-palettes.bats (every tmux palette parses; every YAML palette parses) start with `command -v tmux ... || skip` / `command -v yamllint ... || skip`. The Bats job installs only bats, fish and python3-packaging (Linux) or bats-core, fish, bash, coreutils (macOS).

## Evidence

.github/workflows/tests.yml:39-40 `sudo apt-get install -y bats fish python3-packaging`; :47 `brew install bats-core fish bash coreutils`. tests/theme-handlers.bats `command -v tmux > /dev/null 2>&1 || skip "tmux not installed"` in each tmux test; tests/theme-palettes.bats `command -v yamllint ... || skip`.

## Impact

The guard against the handler re-entering itself through tmux.conf's bootstrap (an infinite reload loop, reproduced during this work) and the 5 s budget guard run only on developer machines. A regression merges with a green CI run.

## Fix

Add `tmux` and `yamllint` to both install steps (`apt-get install -y bats fish python3-packaging tmux yamllint`; `brew install bats-core fish bash coreutils tmux yamllint`), so the skips never fire in CI.

## Resolution
tests.yml installs tmux and yamllint on Linux (apt, verified candidates tmux 3.4 / yamllint 1.33) and macOS (brew formulae verified via formulae.brew.sh). The tmux/yamllint skips no longer fire in CI.
title: CI never installs tmux or yamllint, so the tmux recursion/budget tests and palette parse checks always skip there

body:
## Problem

apply logs a handler's captured stderr only inside `if ((rc != 0))`, then deletes the errlog unconditionally. The missing-palette paths added for the per-family layout (`_link_palette` "removed stale link", dircolors/bat/gh-dash/television/tmux-palette notes) deliberately exit 0 and write to stderr, so none of them ever reaches the log.

## Evidence

config/theme/apply:92 `if ((rc != 0)); then ... _log "WARN handler '$name': $line"`; :100 `rm -f "$errlog"` runs for every handler. config/theme/_lib.sh:90 `printf 'theme: active family ships no palette for %s; removed stale link\n' "$dst" >&2` followed by `return 0`. The plan (docs/plans/2026-09-30-kanagawa-theme-families.md:301-303) claims these paths "log through the existing stderr→apply log channel, so a missing palette is visible in dotfiles-theme logs, not silent".

## Impact

When a family lacks a palette, the app silently falls back to defaults with no trace in $XDG_STATE_HOME/dotfiles-theme/log. The documented diagnostic path does not exist.

## Fix

In apply's wait loop, also log a non-empty errlog when rc == 0, at INFO: `elif [[ -s "$errlog" ]]; then while IFS= read -r line; do _log "INFO handler '$name': $line"; done < "$errlog"; fi`. Add a tests/theme-actor.bats case with a stub handler that writes to stderr and exits 0, asserting the line appears in the log.

## Resolution
apply logs a non-empty errlog at INFO when the handler exits 0. New tests/theme-actor.bats case asserts the stale-link note reaches the log and the errlog is cleaned up.
title: apply discards a handler's stderr on exit 0, so every "family ships no palette" note is lost

body:
## Problem

handlers.d/tmux now re-sources tmux.conf on every dark/light flip. tmux.conf appends to the terminal-features array with `set -as`, which adds a new element each time it is sourced.

## Evidence

config/tmux/tmux.conf:18 `set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB:clipboard:usstyle:strikethrough:overline"`. Reproduced on tmux 3.7c: sourcing a file holding that line three times leaves `tmux show -s terminal-features | grep -c xterm-256color:RGB` at 3.

## Impact

A long-lived tmux server gains one duplicate entry per flip (two a day with an OS schedule), indefinitely. Before this change it grew only on a manual `prefix r`.

## Fix

Make the line idempotent by assigning a fixed array index instead of appending (e.g. `set -s terminal-features[100] "xterm-256color:RGB:clipboard:usstyle:strikethrough:overline"` — verify the index syntax against `man tmux` "array options" before committing), and add a bats case that sources tmux.conf's line twice and asserts one entry.

## Resolution
tmux.conf uses `set -s terminal-features[100] ...` (a fixed index, verified idempotent on tmux 3.7c: 3 reloads, 1 entry). tests/theme-palettes.bats sources the line three times and forbids an appending set on terminal-features.
title: Automated tmux reload appends a duplicate terminal-features entry on every theme flip

body:
## Problem

The --now path shows `tmux source-file`'s error output through `tmux display-message "<text>"` without -l. display-message expands formats, so `#{...}` in the text is substituted and `#(...)` is executed as a shell command. tmux parse errors quote the offending config line, and this tmux.conf contains `#(...)` status segments.

## Evidence

config/theme/handlers.d/tmux:35 `tmux display-message "theme: tmux reload failed: ${err//$'\n'/ }"`. On tmux 3.7c, `display-message -p 'fmt #(echo pwned) #{session_name}'` printed `fmt  g` (format expanded, command substituted) while `display-message -l -p '...'` printed the text literally.

## Impact

The diagnostic meant to explain a failed reload is mangled, and quoted config commands run again. The text comes from the user's own config, so this is not attacker-controlled, but the message is unreliable exactly when it is needed.

## Fix

Use literal mode: `tmux display-message -l "theme: tmux reload failed: ${err//$'\n'/ }"` (the -l behaviour was confirmed on tmux 3.7c in this session).

## Resolution
handlers.d/tmux doubles every # in the failure message before display-message (`${msg//#/##}`), verified to print #(...) and #{...} literally; portable to tmux versions without display-message -l.
title: Reload-failure message is passed to display-message as a format, so #() in the error text runs

body:
## Problem

The Lotus contrast test, the Kanagawa header comments and the plan say every Lotus foreground reaches WCAG AA, but the checker exempts the muted overlays (#88877e 3.01:1, #716e61 4.26:1, #766b90 4.09:1) to a 3:1 floor. Those colours render text: comments, fish autosuggestions and pager descriptions, vim line numbers. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for normal text and has no "muted" exception.

## Evidence

tests/theme-contrast.bats:144 `LOTUS_MUTED='#88877e #716e61 #766b90'`; :146 `@test "kanagawa lotus: every foreground reaches WCAG AA on #f2ecbc"`; check_contrast applies `floor = 3.0 if h in muted`. config/fish/themes/kanagawa-aa.theme [light] uses 88877e for fish_color_comment and fish_color_autosuggestion.

## Impact

The documentation promises a compliance level the palette deliberately does not meet, so a reader relying on it (or a future audit) is misled about comment and autosuggestion readability in light mode.

## Fix

Choose one and make the docs match. Either (a) state the exception honestly: rename the test to "every non-muted foreground reaches WCAG AA; muted comment/overlay colours reach 3:1", and say the same in kanagawa/light/starship.toml's header, the fish theme header and the plan; or (b) darken the three muted colours to 4.5:1 and drop the exemption.

## Resolution
Option (a): test titles now say "every non-muted foreground"; the header and LOTUS_MUTED comment in tests/theme-contrast.bats state the 3:1 muted greys are a deliberate exception below WCAG 1.4.3; the plan's deviations record the correction.
title: "Every foreground reaches WCAG AA" is false: muted foregrounds are held to 3:1

body:
## Problem

Switching families (edit config/theme/family, run apply) updates the handlers and fish, but a running vim reacts only when the mode string changes. s:ApplyThemeMode returns early while the mode is unchanged. nvim reads the family once at startup. The docs describe the switch as edit plus apply, with no restart caveat.

## Evidence

config/vim/vimrc:288-290 `function! s:ApplyThemeMode(...)` / `if l:mode ==# get(s:, 'last_mode', '') | return`. config/nvim/init.lua theme_family() is called once, at `vim.cmd.colorscheme(theme_family() == 'kanagawa' ...)`. config/theme/CLAUDE.md: "Switch with an edit plus `config/theme/apply \"$(theme-mode)\"`".

## Impact

After a switch, open vim/nvim sessions keep the old family's colours alongside new-family terminals and prompts, which is the mixed-palette state the change set out to prevent. vim fixes itself on the next dark/light flip; nvim needs a restart.

## Fix

vim: key the change check on mode plus family (`let l:key = l:mode . ':' . string(s:Schemes())` compared to `s:last_key`). nvim: document "restart nvim after a family switch" in config/theme/CLAUDE.md and config/nvim/README.md; live re-reading is not worth an extra poller.

## Resolution
vimrc keys the change check on the resolved scheme (mode + family), so a running vim follows a family switch within 3 s. New test proves it and fails with the old mode-only logic (planted negative stayed on kanagawa_wave). nvim's restart requirement documented in config/theme/CLAUDE.md and config/nvim/README.md.
title: Running vim and nvim ignore a family-only switch

body:
## Problem

When the active family ships no dircolors palette, handlers.d/dircolors deletes the ls-colors cache so another family's colours don't linger. But theme-switch.fish only sets LS_COLORS when the cache is readable and never unsets it, and bash/zsh (config/exports:485) behave the same. The BAT_THEME branch in the same function was given an `else set -e`; LS_COLORS was not.

## Evidence

config/fish/conf.d/theme-switch.fish:59-61 `if test -r $ls_cache ... set -gx LS_COLORS $ls_value` with no else branch. config/exports:485 `[ -r "$ls_cache" ] && eval "$(cat "$ls_cache")"`.

## Impact

On that path, running shells keep the old family's ls colours next to new-family prompts, defeating the handler's cleanup. It is reachable only when a family omits dircolors, which tests/theme-palettes.bats currently prevents.

## Fix

Add `else; set -e LS_COLORS` to the fish block at :59-61 (mirroring the BAT_THEME branch). Leave bash/zsh as is: their read happens only at shell start, and a new shell without a cache already gets no LS_COLORS from it.

## Resolution
theme-switch.fish unsets LS_COLORS when the ls-colors cache is gone, mirroring the BAT_THEME branch. bash/zsh left as is (read only at shell start).
title: Removed ls-colors cache leaves the previous family's LS_COLORS exported in shells

body:
## Problem

The family choice is re-implemented in four runtimes outside _lib.sh: __dotfiles_theme_name (fish), theme_family() (nvim), s:Schemes() (vim) and theme_family()/Scheme_for_appearance (wezterm). Each was verified only by hand in this session. The bats suite covers only the bash _theme_family.

## Evidence

`git grep -l '__dotfiles_theme_name\|Scheme_for_appearance\|s:Schemes' tests/` finds only a string grep in tests/theme-contrast.bats ("AA overrides stay wired"), which asserts the name appears, not the behaviour. The functions sit at config/fish/functions/__dotfiles_theme_name.fish:1-16, config/nvim/init.lua (theme_family), config/vim/vimrc (s:Schemes), config/wezterm/wezterm.lua (theme_family).

## Impact

A change to the family file format, or to the env override, can break any of the four without a failing test. They already differ: bash and fish reject non-slug names, while nvim, vim and wezterm silently fall back to catppuccin.

## Fix

Add bats cases that run each headlessly with DOTFILES pointed at a temp tree: `fish -c __dotfiles_theme_name` (kanagawa, catppuccin, invalid, missing theme file); `nvim --headless` printing vim.g.colors_name per family; `vim -Nu config/vim/vimrc -es` printing g:colors_name per family and mode (skip when the binary is absent, and provision it in CI per the tests.yml finding). The wezterm resolver can be exercised through `nvim -l` with a stub `wezterm` module, as done manually this session.

## Resolution
New tests/theme-family-resolvers.bats covers fish (__dotfiles_theme_name: tracked, override, invalid), vim (both families, fallback, live switch), nvim (family selection, skips without kanagawa.nvim installed) and wezterm (resolver under nvim Lua with a stub module; every returned scheme registered). 9 cases, all pass.
title: Family resolution in fish, nvim, vim and wezterm has no automated test

body:
## Problem

The contract rule now requires handlers to resolve palettes with `_palette` and to clean up when the family ships none. No hook or test checks it: a handler that builds `palettes.d/<name>.${mode}` by hand (the pre-change pattern the scaffold used to emit) passes every gate and silently keeps another family's palette.

## Evidence

.claude/rules/theme-handler-contract.md:17 "Resolve palettes with `_palette <mode> <file>` from `_lib.sh`, never by building the path by hand". `git grep -n 'palettes\.d' tests/` shows no test asserting handlers avoid a literal palettes.d path. tests/theme-palettes.bats checks palette files, not handler code.

## Impact

The next handler added from memory or an old template reintroduces mixed palettes, and only a reviewer would catch it.

## Fix

Add a bats case to tests/theme-handlers.bats: `run grep -ln 'palettes\.d' "$HD"/*; [ "$status" -eq 1 ]` (handlers must go through _palette). Note the enforcement in the rule file.

## Resolution
tests/theme-handlers.bats fails on any palettes.d literal in a code line of a handler or tmux-palette; the rule file names the enforcement.
title: New "resolve palettes with _palette, never by hand" rule has no enforcement

Deleted config/vim/autoload/lightline/colorscheme/kanagawa_{wave,lotus}.vim, removed them from the generator and from the contrast test targets. Unused catppuccin lightline files predate this change; route to /nitpicker dead-code.

## Problem

.gitkeep exists only to keep an otherwise empty directory tracked. palettes.d now always contains catppuccin/ and kanagawa/, and tests/theme-palettes.bats requires both to exist.

## Evidence

`git ls-files config/theme/palettes.d/.gitkeep` shows it tracked; `ls -la config/theme/palettes.d/` shows `catppuccin`, `kanagawa`, `.gitkeep`. tests/theme-palettes.bats "palettes: at least catppuccin and kanagawa exist" asserts both directories exist.

A dead placeholder file. It also sits among the family directories, the one level where a stray file could later be mistaken for a family by a glob that is not directory-only.

`git rm config/theme/palettes.d/.gitkeep` (git grep shows no references beyond the generic .gitignore/.gitattributes patterns, which stay valid for other directories), and drop the "Keep palettes.d/.gitkeep" note from the plan's task 2.

git rm config/theme/palettes.d/.gitkeep; the plan records the reversal of task 2's keep note.
title: palettes.d/.gitkeep is obsolete now that the tree holds family directories

## Problem

The Kanagawa Wave tmTheme, kanagawa_wave.vim, the fish [dark] values and the wezterm Wave table were copied from rebelot/kanagawa.nvim and menisadi/kanagawa.vim with no commit recorded, and both upstreams track moving branches. The NOTICE entry names only the repositories.

body:
## Problem

The host overlay is chosen by `install` using `hostname -s`, and fish's host sourcing uses `HOSTNAME` from `hostname -s`. The bash/zsh dispatch that sources the linked `~/.config/exports-<host>` file uses plain `hostname` instead. On any machine where `hostname` returns a qualified name, `install` links `~/.config/exports-lakka`, but bash/zsh look for `~/.config/exports-lakka.example.org` and never source it. Qualified names are common: a server with an FQDN in /etc/hostname, or a Mac whose HostName is unset and so reports `<name>.local`. Fish on the same machine does source its host file.

## Evidence

config/exports:572 — `if [ -f "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/exports-$(hostname)" ]; then source "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/exports-$(hostname)"; fi`
config/exports:574 — the same with `-secret`
install:11 — `DOTBOT_HOST="$(hostname -s)"`
config/fish/exports.fish:18 — `set -q HOSTNAME; or set -x HOSTNAME (hostname -s)`, used at :151-157

## Impact

The lakka exports (`MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS`, luarocks PATH, `~/.local/go/bin`, the acme.sh env) stop loading silently in bash/zsh as soon as that host's `hostname` is qualified, while fish keeps working. The result is shell-dependent behaviour with no error. Each startup also spawns `hostname` twice.

## Fix

Resolve the name once with the same command install uses:
```
_host="$(hostname -s 2> /dev/null || hostname)"
if [ -f "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/exports-$_host" ]; then source "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/exports-$_host"; fi
if [ -f "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/exports-$_host-secret" ]; then source "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/exports-$_host-secret"; fi
unset _host
```
Keep the two `# shellcheck source=` directives above their lines.

## Resolution
Filed with off-by-one line numbers (572/574 instead of 573/575). Superseded by a re-filed finding that has the corrected location config/exports:570-575.
title: bash/zsh host-exports dispatch keys on `hostname`, but install and fish key on `hostname -s`

body:
## Problem

Missing. None of .github/CONTRIBUTING.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/CONTRIBUTING.md exists. The repo enforces contributor-facing conventions: commitlint commit-msg hook (.claude/rules/commit-format.md, @ivuorinen/commitlint-config), `yarn lint` (package.json, nine steps), `yarn test`/scripts/bats-run.sh, prek pre-commit, and CI workflows (.github/workflows/linters.yml, tests.yml, semantic-pr.yml). .github/ already has CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md, CODEOWNERS.

## Evidence

`ls .github/CONTRIBUTING.md CONTRIBUTING.md docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` → three "No such file". Contributor rules exist only in agent-facing files (CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md) and docs/commands.md.

## Impact

A human PR author (Renovate aside) finds no statement that `yarn install`, `prek install`, Conventional Commits and a green `yarn lint`/bats suite are required, and learns it from a failing hook or semantic-pr check.

## Fix

Scaffold .github/CONTRIBUTING.md (offered, not written) with sections sourced only from the repo: Intro (README title); Reporting issues (→ .github/SECURITY.md for security); Setup (`yarn install`, `prek install`, `./install --links` per README); Code style (`yarn lint`, `yarn fix`, .editorconfig); Testing (`yarn test`, `scripts/bats-run.sh`, `bats tests/<file>.bats`); Commit convention (copy .claude/rules/commit-format.md types/100-char header); PR process (semantic-pr.yml title check, CODEOWNERS); Adding a script (`#USAGE about`, `x-` prefix, tests/<name>.bats per .claude/rules/local-bin-scripts.md); License (LICENSE, MIT).

## Resolution
Superseded by audit-ef2d09ef. Severity was overstated (High for a missing CONTRIBUTING.md in a single-maintainer repo whose other authors are bots), and the Fix named the license as plain "MIT", contradicting LICENSE:1-2, which defers third-party portions to NOTICE.
title: No CONTRIBUTING.md in a repo that enforces a commit convention, lint gate, test suite and CI checks

body:
## Problem

Dead branch with a destructive side effect. lib::cleanup still deletes `$TEMP_DIR` "for parity with the upstream common.sh". No script in the repo sets TEMP_DIR and then runs lib::cleanup. The only consumers are the EXIT traps in scripts/install-composer.sh and scripts/create-nvim-keymaps.sh, and both register their temp paths through lib::register_cleanup. So the branch serves no caller. It does fire, though, whenever TEMP_DIR arrives through the inherited environment.

## Evidence

config/lib.sh:241-247:
```
# Remove queued temporary paths. Also honors a legacy $TEMP_DIR variable
# for parity with the upstream common.sh. Safe to call more than once.
lib::cleanup()
{
  if [[ -n "${TEMP_DIR:-}" && -d "$TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
    rm -rf "$TEMP_DIR"
  fi
```
Reachability: `git grep -n -w TEMP_DIR` finds only config/lib.sh:241-246 and local/bin/x-ssh-audit. x-ssh-audit does not source lib.sh or shared.sh and uses its own cleanup at :165. `lib::trap_cleanup` callers are scripts/install-composer.sh:17-18 and scripts/create-nvim-keymaps.sh:18-19; neither sets TEMP_DIR. The only thing that exercises the branch is tests/lib.bats:111-115 ("lib::cleanup also honors a legacy TEMP_DIR"). No dynamic or config reference to the variable exists.

## Impact

TEMP_DIR is a generic name that other tools and users export. With `export TEMP_DIR=~/tmp` in the environment, `dfm install composer` (scripts/install-composer.sh) or create-nvim-keymaps.sh runs `rm -rf ~/tmp` on exit. Both scripts run their EXIT trap on success as well as failure. This is user data loss on a path nothing in the repo intends to clean.

## Fix

Delete config/lib.sh:245-247 (the `if [[ -n "${TEMP_DIR:-}" ...` block) and the second sentence of the comment at :241-242. Delete tests/lib.bats:111-115, the test that only pins the legacy behavior. Run `bats tests/lib.bats tests/install-completions.bats` afterwards; the register_cleanup test at tests/lib.bats:105-109 still covers the real path.

## Resolution
git grep -n -w TEMP_DIR: only config/lib.sh and local/bin/x-ssh-audit (own variable, does not source lib.sh). Removed the legacy TEMP_DIR rm -rf branch and comment sentence from lib::cleanup. Replaced the tests/lib.bats legacy test with a regression test asserting an inherited TEMP_DIR survives lib::cleanup. bats lib/dfm/install-completions subset green.
title: lib::cleanup's "legacy $TEMP_DIR" branch has no in-repo producer and rm -rf's whatever TEMP_DIR the caller's environment carries

body:
## Problem

unused-export. Four functions in config/lib.sh have no caller in any script, hook, rc file or config. lib::strict and lib::error::handle are not referenced anywhere except a rule's prose and also have no test. lib::log and logger::debug are referenced only from tests/lib.bats. LIB_E_FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND and LIB_E_FILE_NOT_FOUND are read only inside lib::error::handle. These items are classed as unused exports, not dead code, because CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/lib-sh-side-effects.md document lib.sh as an API available to every script and interactive shell.

## Evidence

`git grep -l -F <fn> -- ':!docs/audit' ':!graphify-out' ':!config/lib.sh'` returned:
- `lib::strict` → .claude/rules/lib-sh-side-effects.md only ("Scripts opt in through `lib::strict` and `lib::trap_cleanup`")
- `lib::error::handle` → nothing
- `lib::log ` → tests/lib.bats only
- `logger::debug` → tests/lib.bats only

The definitions are at config/lib.sh:90-94 (lib::log), :195-221 (lib::error::handle) and :271-276 (lib::strict):
```
lib::strict()
{
  set -euo pipefail
  trap 'lib::error::handle "${LINENO}" "${BASH_COMMAND-?}"' ERR
```
Every script in the repo writes `set -euo pipefail` directly; none calls lib::strict. Channels checked: direct calls, string or trap references, settings.json hooks, dotbot, package.json, and fish (which does not source lib.sh). All were negative. The one channel that cannot be checked is the owner's ad hoc use outside the repo.

## Impact

About 45 lines get loaded into every bash/zsh startup and maintained (the ERR-trap exit-code table, the strict-mode wrapper) without serving any caller. The rule file presents lib::strict as the opt-in mechanism, but no script uses it, so the rule and the practice disagree.

## Fix

Owner decision. Option 1: delete lib::strict (:265-276 with its header) and lib::error::handle (:182-221). Delete LIB_E_FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND and LIB_E_FILE_NOT_FOUND only after confirming nothing else reads them. Change lib-sh-side-effects.md:11-12 to "Scripts opt in through `set -euo pipefail` and `lib::trap_cleanup`". Also delete lib::log (:84-94) and logger::debug (:158-161) together with their tests/lib.bats cases. Option 2: keep them, and record the out-of-repo consumer in a comment next to each.

## Resolution
Kept per fix-run criterion (remove only if no doc presents them as user-facing API). CLAUDE.md "Centralized Logging" documents lib.sh helpers as available in every interactive shell, and .claude/rules/lib-sh-side-effects.md names lib::strict as the scripts' strict-mode opt-in; lib::error::handle is its ERR handler. logger::debug is the DEBUG member of the documented level-filtered logger::{debug,info,warn,error} family. No in-repo caller confirmed (tests only), but these are documented interactive/opt-in API. Fixed a dangling "helpers below" reference in CLAUDE.md.
title: lib::strict, lib::error::handle, lib::log and logger::debug have no production caller (unused-export; consumer surface: the documented lib.sh API / interactive use)

body:
## Problem

Convention vs reality. .claude/rules/shell-scripts.md:5-6: every shell script must start with "`#!/bin/sh` plus a `# shellcheck shell=sh` directive on line 2". Only mise-python-arch and x-quota-usage comply.

## Evidence

Line 2 of each: x-codeql `#USAGE about "CodeQL security scanning wrapper"`; x-list-open-prs `# list-open-prs.sh`; x-ssh-audit, x-ssl-expiry-date, x-until-error, x-until-success all `#USAGE about ...`. None contains `shellcheck shell=` anywhere (grep). x-codeql was touched in 99da9044 after the rule's 9b63cd62 without fixing it.

## Impact

Rule and tree disagree; agents either churn six files or learn the rule is ignorable. shellcheck already infers sh from the shebang, so the directive adds nothing for files that have one — the rule demands redundant machinery.

## Fix

Simplest: edit .claude/rules/shell-scripts.md:6 to "- `#!/bin/sh` — POSIX scripts (shellcheck reads the dialect from the shebang)" and keep the directive requirement only for the shebang-less sourced case. Otherwise insert `# shellcheck shell=sh` as line 2 of the six scripts.

## Resolution
Added `# shellcheck shell=sh` as line 2 of local/bin/x-codeql, x-list-open-prs, x-ssh-audit, x-ssl-expiry-date, x-until-error, x-until-success. All pass dash -n, shellcheck, shfmt -d; their bats tests pass. pushover (#!/usr/bin/env sh) is outside the rule's #!/bin/sh clause and left unchanged.
title: 6 of 8 `#!/bin/sh` scripts lack the line-2 `# shellcheck shell=sh` the shell-scripts rule mandates

body:
## Problem

Class: masked-failure. The `git submodule foreach` body is a double-quoted string, so `$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 origin/HEAD)`, `$(git describe --tags)`, `$tag` and `$name` are all expanded once by the step's bash in the superproject, before foreach runs. The superproject checkout uses fetch-depth 2 with no tags, so both describes fail (printing `fatal: No names found` to stderr, which does not trip `-e` inside a command substitution in an argument), `$tag` is unset, and each submodule evaluates `if [ "" != "" ]` -> false. No submodule is ever checked out to a new tag, `git diff --quiet` succeeds, and the job prints "No updates for submodules." and exits 0.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/update-submodules.yml:47-53:
```
git submodule foreach --quiet "
  tag=\"$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 origin/HEAD)\"
  if [ \"$(git describe --tags)\" != \"$tag\" ]; then
    git checkout --quiet \"$tag\"
    echo \"$name updated to $tag\"
  fi
"
```
Run 36814387948 (2026-10-01, conclusion success) log: exactly two `fatal: No names found, cannot describe anything.` lines (one per outer substitution, not one per each of the 5 submodules), then `No updates for submodules.`. `gh run list` shows the last 8 scheduled runs all success. Last automated commit: c9489ae5 on 2025-02-24. Local checkouts are behind upstream tags: tools/antidote at v1.9.7-5-g64b7864 vs latest v2.3.0; tools/dotbot at v1.21.0 vs v1.24.1. Source: manual sweep (actionlint and zizmor do not flag this).

## Impact

The scheduled job is a green check that does nothing. dotbot (executed by `./install`) and antidote (sourced by every zsh) have been frozen for ~19 months without anyone being told, so upstream fixes never arrive, while the workflow's existence implies they do.

## Fix

Single-quote the foreach body so it is evaluated per submodule, fetch tags there, and skip tagless submodules (dotbot-include and both cheatsheet repos have no tags):
```
git submodule foreach --quiet '
  git fetch --quiet --tags origin
  tag="$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { echo "$name: no tags, skipped"; exit 0; }
  if [ "$(git describe --tags)" != "$tag" ]; then
    git checkout --quiet "$tag"
    echo "$name updated to $tag"
  fi
'
```
Then stage only submodule paths (`git add tools/dotbot tools/antidote ...` instead of `git add .`). Because this job then pushes upstream code straight to main with contents: write, prefer opening a PR (e.g. `gh pr create`) over `git push` so tag bumps to code `./install` executes get reviewed. Note antidote v1 to v2 is a major bump; review before the first run.

## Resolution
foreach body single-quoted (SC2016 disabled inline with reason), fetches tags per submodule, skips tagless submodules; staging changed from `git add .` to `git add --update`. Kept direct push: no PR-creating action is used in any repo workflow, and a GITHUB_TOKEN PR would not trigger checks; reason recorded in a workflow comment. actionlint, yamllint, prettier clean.
title: update-submodules runs green but has updated nothing since 2025-02: foreach script is expanded by the outer shell

## Problem

## Evidence

1c8b3333 "refactor: drop the vendored fzf and iTerm2 files" — deletes the executable `local/bin/fzf-tmux` (249 lines) and its manpages from PATH; a removed CLI command is breaking surface, no `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`. a4645477 "chore(config): remove the act, husky and amethyst configs" — deletes config/amethyst/amethyst.yml (364 lines) and config/act/actrc (user config, behaviour of `act` changes to defaults). d764fd9e "chore(herdr): turn off theme auto_switch" — `auto_switch = true` → `false`, a behaviour change. Releases are date-tagged (26.10.2), so no semver bump is mis-computed; only the changelog section is wrong. All three are pushed (on main before 776e169b).

## Impact

A reader of the release notes sees no removal of `fzf-tmux` or Amethyst config; scripts or muscle memory calling `fzf-tmux` break with no notice.

## Fix

Pushed history is not rewritten. Going forward label such commits `feat(<scope>)!:` with a `BREAKING CHANGE: <what was removed>` footer, e.g. "refactor(fzf)!: drop the vendored fzf and iTerm2 files" + "BREAKING CHANGE: local/bin/fzf-tmux is removed; use fzf --tmux". Optionally add one line to .claude/rules/commit-format.md: "Removing a command, alias or config a user invokes is breaking: add `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer."

## Resolution
History not rewritten. Added 3 lines to .claude/rules/commit-format.md: removing/renaming a user-invoked command, alias or config is breaking and needs `!` plus a BREAKING CHANGE footer.
title: Removals of user-visible commands/configs labelled `refactor:`/`chore:` with no `!`, so the tag changelog files them as Refactors/Chores

## Problem

Six project skills give `allowed-tools: Bash, ...` and fenced bash steps whose commands bash-routing.md says belong in ctx_batch_execute. pre-bash-route.sh denies each, so every invocation of these skills costs a deny round trip and teaches the agent the skill and the rules disagree. bash-routing.md also names `shfmt -w` and `fish_indent --write` as allowed in-place formatters but not `stylua <file>`, which lua-format mandates and the router denies.

## Evidence

fish-validate/SKILL.md `fish_indent --check <file>`; yaml-validate/SKILL.md `yamllint <file>` and fallback `python3 -c "import yaml; ..."`; dotbot-validate/SKILL.md `yamllint -d relaxed <file>` and the same python3 -c fallback; shell-validate/SKILL.md `bash -n`/`sh -n`/`shellcheck <file>`; lua-format/SKILL.md `stylua <file>`; new-fish-function/SKILL.md `fish_indent --check`. ## Impact

Skill instructions contradict the always-loaded routing rule; agents either hit repeated denies or learn to reach for BASH_OK.

## Fix

In each of the six SKILL.md files, state that the check commands run through `ctx_batch_execute` (bash-routing.md) and add the ctx tools to `allowed-tools` (`mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute`). For stylua, either add `stylua <file>` (without --check) to bash-routing.md's in-place-formatter list and remove `stylua` from deny_first_word_re in favour of a `^stylua[[:space:]]+(--check|-c)` compound deny (already present at pre-bash-route.sh:82), or route it through ctx in lua-format.

## Resolution
The *-validate skills and lua-format now route their checks through ctx_batch_execute and list it in allowed-tools (docs fix worker). new-fish-function/SKILL.md no longer restates the fish --no-execute / fish_indent --check commands on a bash fence: step 3 delegates to the fish-validate skill, and allowed-tools drops Bash in favour of Skill.

body:
## Problem

`a decrypt` and `ad` pass `$KEYS_FILE` to `age -d -i`. That file is the one `fetch_keys_if_missing` downloads from `https://github.com/ivuorinen.keys` and that the encrypt path uses with `age -R` — it holds SSH public keys (recipients). age only accepts private keys as identities, so every decrypt with the default configuration fails. No single `AGE_KEYSFILE` value can serve both paths: `-R` rejects private keys and `-i` rejects public keys.

## Evidence

local/bin/a:26-27 `KEYS_FILE="${AGE_KEYSFILE:-$HOME/.ssh/keys.txt}"` / `KEYS_SOURCE="${AGE_KEYSSOURCE:-https://github.com/ivuorinen.keys}"`
local/bin/a:204 `if age -R "$KEYS_FILE" "$file" > "$temp_file" ...` (encrypt: recipients)
local/bin/a:268 `if age -d -i "$KEYS_FILE" "$file" > "$temp_file" && mv "$temp_file" "$output_file"; then` (decrypt: same file as identity)
local/bin/ad:56 `if age -d -i "$KEYS_FILE" "$FILE" > "$TEMP_FILE" && mv "$TEMP_FILE" "$OUTPUT_FILE"; then`
Reproduced with age 1.3.2: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f k; age -R k.pub f > f.age` succeeds; `age -d -i k.pub f.age` exits 1; `age -d -i k f.age` prints the plaintext. No test covers a/ad/ae (no tests/a.bats, tests/ad.bats).

## Impact

The decrypt half of the tool is non-functional by default. `a encrypt --delete` removes the plaintext after encryption, after which the user's own tool cannot restore it; recovery requires running age by hand with the private key.

## Fix

Add a separate identity variable for decryption, e.g. `IDENTITY_FILE="${AGE_IDENTITY:-$HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519}"`, check it exists (`[[ -r "$IDENTITY_FILE" ]] || { log_message "Error: identity '$IDENTITY_FILE' not readable"; return 1; }`), and use `age -d -i "$IDENTITY_FILE"` at a:268 and ad:56. Drop the `fetch_keys_if_missing` call from the decrypt paths (a:263, ad:34-50) since public keys are never needed there. Document `AGE_IDENTITY` in a.md/ad.md and add a bats round-trip test.

## Resolution
a and ad decrypt with new AGE_IDENTITY (default ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, else ~/.ssh/id_rsa), checked readable; ad no longer fetches keys or requires curl. Also fixed a's EXIT trap referencing a function-local under set -u (a exited 1 after every op): TEMP_FILE is now global with one trap. Docs: a help text, a.md, ad.md. Tests (tests/age-wrappers.bats): real age 1.3.2 round trips ae+ad and `a e`+`a d` with a throwaway ssh-keygen ed25519 pair (skip only if age/ssh-keygen missing), ad identity/never-fetches/missing-identity tests.
title: a and ad decrypt with the GitHub public-keys file as the age identity, so decryption can never succeed

body:
## Problem

The keys fetch is `curl -s "$KEYS_SOURCE" -o "$KEYS_FILE"`. Without `-f`, curl exits 0 on a 404/429/5xx and writes the response body (e.g. `Not Found`, a GitHub unicorn HTML page). The only guard is `[[ ! -s "$KEYS_FILE" ]]`, which a non-empty error body passes. The file is then `chmod 0400` and, because every later run only fetches when the file is missing, it is never refetched. No connect/total timeout is set either.

## Evidence

local/bin/a:168 `if ! curl -s "$KEYS_SOURCE" -o "$KEYS_FILE" || [[ ! -s "$KEYS_FILE" ]]; then`
local/bin/a:175 `chmod 0400 "$KEYS_FILE"`
local/bin/ad:41 and local/bin/ae:42: identical curl line; ad:47 / ae:48 `chmod 0400 "$KEYS_FILE"`.
Scenario: AGE_KEYSSOURCE typo, renamed GitHub user, or a transient GitHub 503/429 on first use → `~/.ssh/keys.txt` contains the error body, mode 0400, "Keys file fetched" printed. Every subsequent `a`/`ae` run fails inside age with a recipient parse error until the user finds and deletes the file manually.

## Impact

A one-off transient HTTP failure permanently breaks encryption on that machine, and the error age prints (bad recipient) does not point at the cached file.

## Fix

In all three scripts replace the fetch with `curl -fsS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 "$KEYS_SOURCE" -o "$KEYS_FILE.tmp"`, validate the content (`grep -qE '^(ssh-|sk-|ecdsa-)' "$KEYS_FILE.tmp"`), and only then `mv "$KEYS_FILE.tmp" "$KEYS_FILE"`; on any failure `rm -f "$KEYS_FILE.tmp"` and exit 1.

## Resolution
a and ae fetch with curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 into mktemp "$KEYS_FILE.XXXXXX", require a line matching ^(ssh-|sk-|ecdsa-), chmod 0400, then mv into place; temp removed on any failure. ad no longer fetches at all. Tests: ae/a reject a 200 "Not Found" body and leave no keys file or temp; ae fetch uses curl -fsSL.
title: a, ad and ae cache an HTTP error page as the keys file because curl runs without --fail
