## Problem

This is a coverage hole. audit-5e372164 found that the script aborted before prompting on the machines that need it: `xcode-select -p` exits 2 under `set -e`, and the wait loop had no bound. The fix rewrote main() with xcode_swift_path(), a deferred `sudo -v`, and a 1800 s bound. No file under tests/ references install-xcode-cli-tools (`git grep -n install-xcode-cli-tools -- tests` returns nothing). This is the first-boot macOS bootstrap path, where a regression puts the user back into the original failure.

## Evidence

scripts/install-xcode-cli-tools.sh:66-75:
```
main()
{
  local swift_path
  swift_path="$(xcode_swift_path)"
  if [[ -n "$swift_path" && -x "$swift_path" ]]; then
    msgr run "You have swift from xcode-select. Continuing..."
    return 0
  fi
```
:84 `if ((waited >= XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT)); then`. `ls tests | grep -i xcode` returns nothing.

## Impact

If `xcode-select -p` comes back as a bare call, or `sudo -v` returns to the top level, or the timeout check is dropped, the bug reappears with CI green: the script aborts before prompting on a fresh Mac, or hangs forever with sudo kept alive.

## Fix

Add tests/install-xcode-cli-tools.bats with PATH stubs for `xcode-select`, `sudo` (exit 0), `sleep` (no-op) and `msgr`. Case 1: `xcode-select -p` exits 2, `xcode-select --install` succeeds, and the stub flips to returning a dir containing an executable `usr/bin/swift` after N calls. Assert exit 0, and assert that `xcode-select --install` was recorded, which shows the prompt was reached. Case 2: the tools are present. Assert exit 0, and assert no `sudo` call was recorded. Case 3: the tools never appear. Make the timeout overridable (`XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=${XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT:-1800}`), run with `XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=2`, and assert exit 1 with "Timed out".

## Resolution
scripts/install-xcode-cli-tools.sh: XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT is now overridable (`${XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT:-1800}`). New tests/install-xcode-cli-tools.bats with PATH stubs for xcode-select (-p exits 2 until the READY_AFTER-th call), sudo, osascript, uname (Darwin), sleep (no-op) and msgr, plus a scratch DOTFILES with empty shared.sh. Cases: tools present -> exit 0, no sudo/install recorded; tools missing -> sudo -v and xcode-select --install recorded, exit 0 once they appear; never appear with XCODE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT=3 -> exit 1 "Timed out after 3s"; cancelled dialog -> exit 1, no install. 4/4 pass.
title: audit-5e372164's install-xcode-cli-tools.sh rewrite (no-tools path, bounded wait) has no test

body:
## Problem

split_segments (bash-policy.sh:34-59) cuts on ( ) ; | & with no quote awareness. Any commit message containing a parenthesis or semicolon (every conventional-commit header has `(scope)`) moves the flags after the message into a separate segment whose first word is not `git`, so the git checks in _bp_check_segment never see them. Regression of agent-loopholes-31a486f9 / e0092417 on the normal commit-message shape.

## Evidence

bash-policy.sh:47 `gsub(/\(/, "\n")`, :46 `gsub(/;/, "\n")`, :49 `gsub(/\)/, "")`. Fed to pre-bash-route.sh: `git commit -m 'fix(x): y' --no-verify` -> no decision (allowed); same with `-n` and `-a`; `git commit -m 'a; b' --no-verify` -> allowed. pre-ctx-write-guard.sh on `git commit -m 'fix(x): y' --no-verify` -> rc=0. Control `git commit --no-verify -m x` -> deny.

## Impact

The hook-bypass and git-hunk rules are skipped for the commit-message format the repo requires, on both Bash and the ctx sandbox, with no warning.

## Fix

Run the hook-bypass scan (BP_BYPASS_RE) and the commit -n/-a checks on the whole raw command when it contains `git`, not only on split segments; or strip single- and double-quoted spans (replace with a placeholder) before split_segments so separators inside quotes do not split. Add bats cases for `-m 'fix(x): y' --no-verify|-n|-a` and `-m 'a; b' --no-verify` to tests/pre-bash-route.bats and tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats.

## Resolution
Replaced the quote-unaware split_segments with a real parser: lib/bash-policy.sh runs `shfmt -ln bash --to-json` and one jq pass flattens the AST into argv records with quoting resolved, so `-m 'fix(x): y'` / `-m 'a; b'` no longer split. git commit options are parsed per argv (short clusters, abbreviated long options), so --no-verify/-n/-a after a message are seen. Same code path for Bash and the ctx guard. Tests: pre-bash-route.bats "a quoted commit message cannot hide a bypass flag" + "conventional commit messages pass"; pre-ctx-write-guard.bats "a quoted commit message cannot hide a bypass flag".
title: split_segments ignores quotes: a conventional-commit message with (scope) or ; hides --no-verify, -n and -a from the policy tier

body:
## Problem

pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:62 runs only bash_policy_check on sandbox code. Unlike pre-bash-route.sh (which denies an unresolved command word at :173-178 and a non-normalisable wrapper at :208-211), the sandbox path has no fail-closed branch. Its own comment (:58-61) says the split covers other languages, but only the single-string os.system/execSync shape is caught. Incomplete fix of agent-loopholes-0e8b508f.

## Evidence

pre-ctx-write-guard.sh rc=0 (allowed) for shell `g=git; $g add -A`, `echo 'git add -A' | sh`, `stdbuf -o L -e L git add -A`, `sudo -u root -g wheel git add -A`; javascript `spawnSync('git',['add','-A'])`; python `subprocess.run(["git","add","-A"])`. Control `os.system('git add -A')` -> rc=2.

## Impact

The git-hunk, no-hook-bypass and no-npm rules are not enforced on the tool the routing rules send agents to for nearly every command.

## Fix

In pre-ctx-write-guard.sh, deny (exit 2) when the code contains a policy trigger word (BP_TRIGGER_RE) together with dynamic-exec shapes: a `$var`/`${...}` command word, a pipe into sh|bash|zsh|fish, eval/source of generated text, or an argv array whose first element is a quoted git/npm/pip/curl token (regex `["']\s*(git|npm|npx|pnpm|pip3?|uv|curl|wget)\s*["']\s*,`). Apply the same wrapped-and-unresolved fail-closed rule pre-bash-route.sh uses. Add each payload above as a bats case in tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats.

## Resolution
bash-policy.sh now records dynamic shapes ($var/$(...) command word, shell reading stdin, source of <(...)/$..., unparseable text, non-literal subprocess/exec argument in non-shell code) and denies them when the code names a policy tool (word-anchored BP_TRIGGER_RE); a dynamic command word whose args include add/commit/install etc. is denied outright. Non-shell code (ctx language != shell, python -c/node -e, text that fails to parse) gets a string-literal pass: each literal naming a policy tool and each run of adjacent literals (argv arrays, spawnSync('git',['add'])) is parsed as shell. Wrapped argvs are re-checked at every suffix (stdbuf -o L -e L, sudo -u root -g wheel). Residual documented in the header: fragments with no policy word ("gi"+"t"), argv arrays holding variables, scripts in files. Tests: pre-ctx-write-guard.bats "dynamic command construction naming a policy tool is denied" (all six payloads from the finding plus allowed controls), pre-bash-route.bats "wrappers with several operand options are seen through".
title: ctx sandbox policy tier is text-only with no fail-closed: variables, piped-to-sh strings and array-arg subprocess calls pass

body:
## Problem

strip_env_prefix removes inline assignments before _bp_check_segment runs, so env-driven bypasses are invisible: prek honours SKIP=<hook-ids>, and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE set core.hooksPath without the `-c` text the regex looks for. Removing files under .git/hooks is not checked. `git commit [-i|-o] <path>` stages whole files, which is the reason git-hunk-commits.md bans `commit -a`, but only -a/--all is denied. no-hook-bypass.md does not list SKIP= or hook-file removal.

## Evidence

pre-bash-route.sh gives no decision (allowed) for `SKIP=commitlint,shellcheck git commit -m x`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/dev/null git commit -m x`, `rm .git/hooks/commit-msg`, `git commit -m msg local/bin/dfm`, `git commit -i -m msg local/bin/dfm`. ctx guard rc=0 for `SKIP=commitlint git commit -m x`. bash-policy.sh:110 strips the assignment; :362 checks only -a/--all.

## Impact

The commitlint/shellcheck/test gates and hunk-only staging can be skipped with ordinary-looking commands on both Bash and the sandbox.

## Fix

In bash_policy_check, scan the raw command (before strip_env_prefix) with `grep -qiE '(^|[[:space:]])(SKIP|PRE_COMMIT_ALLOW_NO_CONFIG|GIT_CONFIG_(COUNT|KEY_[0-9]+|PARAMETERS))='` and deny. Add `\.git/hooks` to the write-path check, so any BP_WRITE_SEG_RE segment naming it is denied. For git commit, deny `-i|--include|-o|--only` and any non-option operand after the message (pathspec). Add SKIP= and hook-file removal to the forbidden list in .claude/rules/no-hook-bypass.md and `git commit <path>` to git-hunk-commits.md. Add bats cases.

## Resolution
Policy tier collects every assignment (prefix, export, env VAR=) from the AST and denies SKIP, PRE_COMMIT_ALLOW_NO_CONFIG, GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n/PARAMETERS when the code runs git, git-hunk, prek or pre-commit (text regex for non-shell code). .git/hooks and .git/config added to PROTECTED_PATHS, so writes via redirect, rm/cp/mv/ln, Edit/Write are denied. git commit with a pathspec, -i/--include, -o/--only or --pathspec-from-file is denied like -a. Rules updated: no-hook-bypass.md (env + hook-file items), git-hunk-commits.md (pathspec/-i/-o). Tests: pre-bash-route.bats "environment and hook-file bypasses are denied", "git commit with a pathspec or -i/-o is denied"; ctx test for SKIP=.
title: Hook chain bypassable via SKIP=, GIT_CONFIG_* env, deleting .git/hooks, and git commit <path>; none is in the policy tier or the rules

body:
## Problem

pre-edit-block.sh:14-16 assumes Grep without an explicit secrets path is safe because ripgrep skips the gitignored secrets trees. ripgrep's --glob overrides ignore rules, and a glob naming only the filename carries no secrets.d text, so secrets_referenced misses it. Incomplete fix of agent-loopholes-9168e487.

## Evidence

pre-edit-block.sh rc=0 for `{"tool_name":"Grep","tool_input":{"pattern":"token","path":"config/fish","glob":"**/github.fish"}}`. Scratch repo with `secrets.d/*` gitignored: `rg -l token fish` -> nothing; `rg -l --glob '**/github.fish' token fish` -> fish/secrets.d/github.fish.

## Impact

Credential file content can be read through the Grep tool, which secrets-files.md forbids and the hook claims to prevent.

## Fix

In the Grep branch of pre-edit-block.sh, when a `glob` is set and the effective search root (path, default project root) is an ancestor of config/fish/secrets.d or config/secrets.d, deny unless the glob ends in `.example` or `README.md`. Simplest: deny any Grep with a non-empty `glob` whose path is unset or resolves under `config/`, and correct the comment at :14-16. Add the payload as a bats case in tests/pre-edit-block.bats.

## Resolution
pre-edit-block.sh: a Grep with a non-empty glob is refused when its search root (path, default the project root, relative paths resolved against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, lexically normalised) is an ancestor of config/secrets.d or config/fish/secrets.d, unless the glob can only match *.example or README.md. Comment corrected. Docs checked: Claude Code permissions page says Read deny rules apply to Grep/Glob only "best-effort"; the first-class complement is a permissions.deny Read(**/secrets.d/**) rule, not added (outside this worker's settings scope). Test: pre-edit-block.bats "a Grep glob over a directory holding a secrets tree is refused" (finding payload, root/default/.. forms, allowed controls).
title: Grep glob overrides gitignore: path config/fish + glob **/github.fish reaches secrets.d and passes the guard

body:
## Problem

pre-bash-route.sh:26-28 exits 0 with no decision when jq is absent; pre-ctx-write-guard.sh:25-26 `|| exit 0` on any jq failure. pre-edit-block.sh fails closed (exit 2) in the same situation, so the three guards disagree.

## Evidence

With PATH lacking jq: pre-bash-route.sh on `git add -A` -> rc=0, no output (allowed); pre-ctx-write-guard.sh -> rc=0. Malformed JSON `{"tool_input":{"code":"git add -A",}` to pre-ctx-write-guard.sh -> rc=0.

## Impact

A PATH without jq (a hook env without mise/brew shims) silently disables the whole policy tier, including the secrets guard on Bash and the sandbox.

## Fix

pre-bash-route.sh: replace the `exit 0` at :27 with a stderr message and `exit 2`. pre-ctx-write-guard.sh: change both `|| exit 0` to `|| { echo "BLOCKED: unparseable hook payload or jq missing" >&2; exit 2; }`. Add bats cases running each hook with a PATH that lacks jq.

## Resolution
pre-bash-route.sh and pre-ctx-write-guard.sh exit 2 with a stderr reason when jq is missing or the payload does not parse (matches pre-edit-block.sh); bash_policy_check also fails closed when shfmt is missing. The old "malformed input yields no decision" test now asserts the block. Tests: "malformed input and a missing jq fail closed" in pre-bash-route.bats and pre-ctx-write-guard.bats (PATH=/nonexistent).
title: pre-bash-route.sh and pre-ctx-write-guard.sh fail open when jq is missing or the payload is malformed

body:
## Problem

strip_keywords removes `time` but not its `-p` flag, and `coproc`, `trap`, process substitution and command-substitution command words are not modelled. Each lands an unknown first word, which the routing tier allows by default (pre-bash-route.sh:213-215) and the policy tier never examines.

## Evidence

pre-bash-route.sh returns no decision (allowed) for `time -p git add -A`, `coproc git add -A`, `trap 'git add -A' EXIT`, `source <(echo git add -A)`, `$(printf 'gi%s' t) add -A`, `git commit '--no-verify' -m x`, `git commit "-n" -m x`. The quoted-flag cases fail because BP_BYPASS_RE (bash-policy.sh:294) requires whitespace before `--no-v`.

## Impact

The policy tier, which BASH_OK cannot override by design, is skipped with no escape needed.

## Fix

In strip_keywords, drop `time`'s `-p` flag; add `coproc` to strip_wrappers; in pre-bash-route.sh deny a segment whose first word is `trap` or `source`/`.` reading `<(`; treat a first word that came from `$(`/backtick substitution as unresolved (fail closed). In BP_BYPASS_RE and the -n/-a checks, accept an optional leading quote: `(^|[[:space:]])["']?--no-v...` and `[[:space:]]["']?-[A-Za-z]*n`. Add bats cases for each payload.

## Resolution
The shfmt AST models time -p, coproc, command/process substitution and quoting directly; trap/eval/watch/env -S/bash -c (incl. -o pipefail -c) strings and heredocs fed to a shell are parsed recursively; source/. of generated code is a dynamic shape; a $(...) command word with add/commit args is denied. Quoted flags ('--no-verify', "-n") resolve to plain argv words. Test: pre-bash-route.bats "time -p, coproc, trap, process and command substitution are parsed" (all seven payloads plus pipefail and heredoc forms).
title: Bash router allows time -p, coproc, trap, source <(...) and $(...) command words through both tiers

body:
## Problem

_pp_glob_hits (protected-paths.sh:77-106) counts a hit when one literal component matches and a `*` component matches `secrets.d`, so any one-level wildcard under config/ or config/fish/ reads as a secrets reference. secrets_referenced and BP_BYPASS_RE run on the whole command including quoted -m messages, so a commit about the secrets rule or the bypass ban is blocked by the policy tier with no override.

## Evidence

pre-bash-route.sh deny for `ls config/*`, `fish_indent --write config/fish/*/*.fish`, `git-hunk commit abc123 -m 'docs(secrets): document secrets.d modes'`, `git commit -m 'docs: explain the --no-verify ban'`. ctx guard rc=2 for `fish_indent --check config/fish/*/*.fish` and `rg -n 'secrets\.d' .claude/rules`. Glob tool `config/fish/**/*.fish` -> rc=2.

## Impact

The fish-validate skill's whole-tree check, globbing config/, and committing this audit's own rule edits are refused, which pushes agents toward workarounds.

## Fix

In _pp_glob_hits, require the component matched against `secrets.d` itself to carry a literal character (not only some component in the window), so `*` and `**` alone never match it. Exclude quoted `-m`/`--message` arguments of git and git-hunk commit from secrets_referenced and BP_BYPASS_RE (strip `-m '...'`/`-m "..."` spans first). Add bats cases for each false positive above.

## Resolution
Secrets scan in shell code now runs on parsed words with git/git-hunk commit message values (-m/--message, clusters, attached forms) dropped, and without stripping literal quotes/backslashes (secrets_referenced TEXT parsed), so `rg -n 'secrets\.d'` and messages naming secrets.d or --no-verify pass; bypass flags are matched per argument, anchored. _pp_glob_hits: a wildcard-only component standing for secrets.d counts only when literal file-name components follow it, so `ls config/*`, `fish_indent --write config/fish/*/*.fish` and Glob config/fish/**/*.fish pass while the existing `cp config/fish/*/github.fish` deny stays. Residual (documented): `cat config/fish/*/*.fish` passes. Tests: pre-bash-route.bats "conventional commit messages pass", "globs under config/ and regex arguments are not secrets reads"; pre-ctx-write-guard.bats "globs and regex arguments are not secrets reads".
title: Secrets glob check and whole-string scans block legitimate work: ls config/*, fish_indent on config/fish/*/*.fish, commit messages naming secrets.d or --no-verify

body:
## Problem

bash_segments forks awk/sed/printf several times per segment and loops wrappers to a fixed point. BP_TRIGGER_RE is a substring match (`git` hits `digit`, `http` hits every URL, `uv` hits any word containing it), and naming a protected path anywhere sets filter="" (bash-policy.sh:392-395), so every segment gets the full normalisation.

## Evidence

Measured: 20 lines of `git status --short; git rev-parse HEAD | cut -c1-7; rg -n 'digit' local/bin/xN` -> real 2.108s. 50 lines of `rg -n foo yarn.lock local/bin/aN | sort | uniq -c` -> real 5.347s. This runs before every ctx_execute/ctx_batch_execute call.

## Impact

Multi-second latency on the mandated tool path for every command batch.

## Fix

Anchor BP_TRIGGER_RE as words: `(^|[^[:alnum:]_-])(git|npm|npx|pnpm|pnpx|pip3?|uv|curl|wget|https?|xh|aria2c|prek|pre-commit)([^[:alnum:]_-]|$)`. Under has_protected, normalise only the segments that match BP_WRITE_SEG_RE instead of all of them. Do the per-segment normalisation in one awk pass rather than per-segment subshells. Add a timing bats case asserting under 1s for a 50-line script.

## Resolution
Per-segment awk/sed normalisation replaced by one shfmt --to-json + one jq pass and fork-free bash over argv arrays; BP_TRIGGER_RE word-anchored and used only to gate dynamic-code denials; protected-path check runs only on write-shaped commands and write redirects; bash 3.2 quadratic ${var//pat/} removed from the guard. Measured pre-ctx-write-guard.sh, 20-line batch: 2.39s -> 0.11s; 50-line batch naming yarn.lock: 6.05s -> 0.16s (same under /bin/bash 3.2). Test: pre-ctx-write-guard.bats "a 50-line script is checked in under 2 seconds".
title: pre-ctx-write-guard adds 2.1s to a 20-line batch and 5.3s to a 50-line one that mentions a protected path

Contradiction between rule files. bash-routing.md, no-hook-bypass.md and secrets-files.md were updated this round to say the policy tier lives in `.claude/hooks/lib/bash-policy.sh` and `pre-ctx-write-guard.sh` applies it to sandbox code. ## Resolution

title: Four rules still name pre-bash-route.sh as the only enforcement after the policy tier moved to bash-policy.sh and also runs in the ctx guard

body:
## Problem

The foreach body is now single-quoted, so it actually evaluates per submodule for the first time since 2025-02. It checks out the newest tag reachable from origin/HEAD regardless of major version, and pushes the result directly to main with GITHUB_TOKEN. A GITHUB_TOKEN push does not trigger other workflows, so tests.yml never runs on the bump. The workflow's own comment gives that same reason for not opening a PR, but the reason applies to the direct push too.

## Evidence

update-submodules.yml:74-89:
```
tag="$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 origin/HEAD)" || exit 1
if [ "$(git describe --tags)" != "$tag" ]; then
  git checkout --quiet "$tag"
...
git commit -m "chore(git): Update submodules (automated)"
git push
```
Current state: `git submodule status` -> `tools/antidote (v1.9.7-5-g64b7864)`, `tools/dotbot (v1.21.0)`. `git -C tools/antidote tag --list` ends with `v2.2.1 v2.2.2 v2.3.0`. The workflow is `active` (gh api) and runs on cron `0 4 * * 1,4`. Branch protection on main: `required_pull_request_reviews: null`, `required_status_checks.checks: []`, so nothing blocks or gates the push.

## Impact

On the next Monday or Thursday run, antidote crosses a major version (1.x to 2.3.0) and the commit lands on main with no review and no CI. config/zsh/antidote.zsh now hardcodes the friendly-names layout (`export ZSH="$ANTIDOTE_HOME/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh"`) and the bundle path, so a layout change in antidote 2.x breaks every zsh start on every machine at the next `git pull`. The same job also downgrades any submodule that is pinned ahead of its latest tag, such as the current antidote pin, which is 5 commits past v1.9.7.

## Fix

Use one of these: (a) restrict the tag to the current major, `major=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 | cut -d. -f1); tag=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match "${major}.*" origin/HEAD)`, and skip when the current HEAD is already ahead of that tag (`git merge-base --is-ancestor "$tag" HEAD && exit 0`); (b) push to a branch and open a PR with a GitHub App or PAT token so tests.yml runs; or (c) run `bash test-all.sh` in the same job before `git push`. Option (a) fixes the downgrade on its own; (b) or (c) is needed for the missing gate.

## Resolution
.github/workflows/update-submodules.yml: the foreach body now restricts the target tag to the submodule's current major (`git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match "${major}.*" origin/HEAD`) and only fast-forwards (`git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD "$tag"` or skip), so no major bump lands untested and pins ahead of/off the tag are never downgraded. Comment records why (GITHUB_TOKEN push skips CI; majors go via reviewed PR). Proof: dry run of the extracted body against the real submodules printed `antidote: not a fast-forward to v1.10.3, skipped` and `dotbot updated to v1.24.1` (v2.3.0 not selected). actionlint rc=0, zizmor "No findings", yamllint rc=0, prettier clean. No new actions or permissions added.
title: Repaired submodule job will push antidote v1.9.7-5 -> v2.3.0 (major) straight to main with no test run

The new contributor pins were copied before the rebase onto Renovate commit 5498c3fd, which bumped prek to 0.5.4 in config/mise/config.toml. The comment that states the two files agree is false as written.
