body:
## Problem

The change removes `helper = store --file ~/.cache/git/git-credentials` because the helper writes tokens in plaintext. Nothing deletes, migrates, or warns about the file the old helper already wrote. Every machine that used the old config still holds those tokens in plaintext, and git no longer references the file, so nobody is reminded it exists.

## Evidence

Removed line: `-	helper = store --file ~/.cache/git/git-credentials`. Replacement at config/git/shared:2-7: `# No `store` helper: it writes tokens in plaintext.` / `helper =` / `helper = cache --timeout 30000`. On this workstation, `ls -la ~/.cache/git/git-credentials` shows `-rw-------` (the file exists; its contents were not read). No step in install, install.conf.yaml, or `dfm check` refers to the path.

## Impact

The stated security goal is not met on existing machines. Live tokens stay in a plaintext file under ~/.cache, a directory backup and sync tools commonly include, and they remain valid until revoked.

## Fix

Add a one-time cleanup: a `shell` step in install.conf.yaml, or a `dfm check` item, that warns when `~/.cache/git/git-credentials` exists and tells the user to revoke the listed tokens and then `rm` the file. At minimum, record the manual step in the commit message body. Revoke the tokens before deleting the file.

## Resolution
install: after submodule sync (both full and --links runs) a check warns on stderr when ~/.cache/git/git-credentials exists, saying it holds plaintext tokens from the removed store helper and to revoke each token, then `rm` the file. It does not delete the file. tests/install.bats: HOME isolated to the test tmpdir; two new tests (warning present with exact rm command and file left in place; no warning when absent). bats tests/install.bats 5/5 ok, shellcheck rc=0, shfmt (repo args) clean.
title: Dropping the `store` helper leaves the existing plaintext ~/.cache/git/git-credentials on disk

body:
## Problem

hosts/README.md now documents that a forced host link under `hosts/<host>/config/<app>/` replaces the tracked repo file when `~/.config/<app>` symlinks into the repo. lakka's overlay did exactly that with fish/exports.fish. The change deletes the link target but adds no step to restore the tracked file on machines that already ran `./install`.

## Evidence

hosts/lakka/install.conf.yaml:11-14: `~/.config/:` `glob: true` `force: true` `path: hosts/lakka/config/**`. dotbot link.py:139-141 keeps only files for a `**` glob, so it linked `~/.config/fish/exports.fish`. `~/.config/fish` is a symlink to `config/fish`, so the forced link replaced the tracked `config/fish/exports.fish` with a symlink to `hosts/lakka/config/fish/exports.fish`. This change deletes that target (`D hosts/lakka/config/fish/exports.fish`) and also edits `config/fish/exports.fish`. hosts/README.md: "on a tracked file the forced link replaces it".

## Impact

On lakka, `git pull` aborts because the local typechange of config/fish/exports.fish conflicts with the incoming edit. Forcing it through leaves a dangling symlink, which dotbot's `clean: ~/.config recursive: true` then deletes on the next `./install`. Fish then starts with no exports: no PATH, XDG, or MISE settings.

## Fix

Add the recovery to the change, either as a note in hosts/README.md or as a guarded step in a host `before.d` hook: `[ -L "$DOTFILES/config/fish/exports.fish" ] && git -C "$DOTFILES" checkout -- config/fish/exports.fish`. Run it on lakka before pulling: `git -C ~/.dotfiles checkout -- config/fish/exports.fish && git pull`.

## Resolution
hosts/README.md Overlay layout: added the lakka migration note explaining that the old forced link replaced tracked config/fish/exports.fish (pull aborts on typechange; forced pull leaves a dangling link that ./install cleans) and the exact recovery to run before pulling: `git -C ~/.dotfiles checkout -- config/fish/exports.fish && git -C ~/.dotfiles pull`. An install-time guard cannot help because the pull aborts before new code arrives. markdownlint rc=0, yarn lint:ec rc=0.
title: Moving lakka fish exports out of config/ has no migration for checkouts where the forced link already replaced config/fish/exports.fish

body:
## Problem

The osascript stub prints `button returned:Cancel` and exits 0. Real `display dialog` does not report a Cancel click that way: it raises AppleScript error -128 and osascript exits 1. Under `set -euo pipefail`, the assignment `XCODE_MESSAGE="$(osascript ...)"` then ends the script before the `else` branch runs. The test passes against behaviour the script never meets, and the msgr warn branch it claims to cover is dead code.

## Evidence

tests/install-xcode-cli-tools.bats:43-45: `cat > "$TMP/bin/osascript" << 'STUB'` / `printf 'button returned:%s\n' "${DIALOG_BUTTON:-OK}"`. :86-89 asserts `*"cancelled the installation"*`. scripts/install-xcode-cli-tools.sh:52-61 holds the assignment and the `else msgr warn "You have cancelled the installation..."` branch. Reproduced here: `osascript -e 'error "User canceled." number -128'` gives `rc=1 out=6:22: execution error: User canceled. (-128)`, and `bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; X="$(osascript -e "error number -128" 2>/dev/null)"; echo reached'` gives `bash rc=1` without printing `reached`.

## Impact

A user who clicks Cancel sees a raw AppleScript error instead of the rerun instruction. The suite reports the cancel path as covered and correct when it is not, so a regression in that branch would go unnoticed.

## Fix

Make the stub match real behaviour for Cancel: `[ "${DIALOG_BUTTON:-OK}" = OK ] && { echo 'button returned:OK'; exit 0; }; echo 'execution error: User canceled. (-128)' >&2; exit 1`. Then fix the script so the branch is reachable: `if XCODE_MESSAGE="$(osascript ... 2>/dev/null)" && [[ "$XCODE_MESSAGE" = "button returned:OK" ]]; then xcode-select --install; else msgr warn ...; exit 1; fi`.

## Resolution
scripts/install-xcode-cli-tools.sh: the osascript substitution moved into the if condition (`if XCODE_MESSAGE="$(osascript ... 2> /dev/null)" && [[ ... = "button returned:OK" ]]`), so a Cancel (error -128, exit 1) reaches the msgr warn branch instead of ending the script under set -e. tests/install-xcode-cli-tools.bats: osascript stub now matches real behaviour (OK -> stdout + exit 0; otherwise `execution error: User canceled. (-128)` on stderr + exit 1); cancel test also asserts the raw error does not leak. Proof: new test fails against HEAD's script (`not ok ... [ "$status" -eq 1 ]' failed`) and passes against the fix; bats file 4/4 ok, shellcheck rc=0, shfmt clean.
title: The cancelled-dialog test stubs an osascript output that never occurs; on a real Mac the cancel warning is unreachable

body:
## Problem

Before this change the gnupg files were linked to ~/.config/gnupg, which GnuPG never reads, so `enable-ssh-support` had no effect. The new dotbot links put the file in GNUPGHOME, which activates it for the first time. In the same change, the zshrc comment says ssh-through-gpg-agent is not used, and the OMZ gpg-agent plugin, which repointed SSH_AUTH_SOCK, was removed.

## Evidence

config/gnupg/gpg-agent.conf:1: `enable-ssh-support`. dotbot-links.yaml:119-121 now links it to `~/.local/share/gnupg/gpg-agent.conf`. base/zshrc:23-24: "that only matters for ssh through gpg-agent, and nothing points SSH_AUTH_SOCK there." antidote_plugins.txt: "OMZ's gpg-agent plugin is deliberately absent".

## Impact

The agent opens an S.gpg-agent.ssh socket that nothing consumes. The config and its accompanying comment contradict each other, which leaves the intended ssh-agent setup ambiguous for whoever edits it next.

## Fix

Either delete `enable-ssh-support`, which leaves gpg-agent.conf empty and lets both the file and its dotbot link go, or keep it and change the zshrc comment to say why the socket is enabled but not wired.

## Resolution
Evidence: nothing in the repo points SSH_AUTH_SOCK at gpg-agent (only dfm-ssh, which reads the 1Password ssh-agent socket; ssh/config IdentityAgent is 1Password; OMZ gpg-agent plugin removed). config/gnupg/gpg-agent.conf: removed `enable-ssh-support`, replaced with a comment saying why it is off; file kept so the existing dotbot link into GNUPGHOME (~/.local/share/gnupg, whose parent clean is non-recursive) does not dangle. base/zshrc comment now consistent. `GNUPGHOME=<tmp with this file> gpgconf --check-options gpg-agent` -> `...:1:1:` (options valid), rc=0.
title: gpg-agent.conf turns on enable-ssh-support at the same time as base/zshrc states nothing uses ssh through gpg-agent

body:
## Problem

The new retry backoff reads the retry file's mtime at start (line 69) and only rewrites/removes it after every handler has finished (lines 147-152, up to 5 s later). apply has no mutual exclusion, and it runs from every interactive bash/zsh/fish shell init (config/exports:480, config/fish/config.fish:104) and from the watcher. Two concrete interleavings: (1) check-then-act: N shells opened together after the 10-minute window (tmux restoring panes, several terminal tabs) all pass the mmin check before any of them rewrites the file, so each runs the failing handler — contradicting the "at most once per 10 minutes" contract in CLAUDE.md and the in-code comment. (2) lost update / stale mode: a retry run R at mode dark is mid-handler when the watcher's flip run F to light starts; F writes mode=light, runs the handler at light and records its failure in `retry`; R's dark handler finishes after F's, so the app is left on the dark palette while state says light, and R then hits `rm -f -- "$retry_file"` and deletes F's retry record, so the light failure is never retried until the next flip.

## Evidence

apply:68-72
  [[ -s "$retry_file" ]] || exit 0
  [[ -n "$(find "$retry_file" -mmin -"$RETRY_MINUTES" 2> /dev/null)" ]] && exit 0
  while IFS= read -r name; do ...
apply:147-152
if ((${#failed_names[@]} > 0)); then
  _atomic_write "$retry_file" "$(printf '%s\n' "${failed_names[@]}")"
  ...
else
  rm -f -- "$retry_file"
fi
Reproduced against the working tree with a handler that sleeps 1 s and exits 1: after aging the retry file, 6 concurrent `apply dark` produced 6 handler runs (7 total, contract says 1 per window). Second scenario (handler: dark sleeps 2 s and succeeds, light fails): `apply dark &` then `apply light` → after F: retry=[flaky], mode=light; after R finished: retry file gone, handler run order "dark light" with the dark run completing last.

## Impact

The backoff the change exists to provide does not hold under the normal multi-shell startup path (duplicate concurrent `bat cache --build` / `fish_config theme save` runs against the same files), and a flip that coincides with a retry can leave an app on the wrong mode with no retry recorded, i.e. the exact silent drift the retry file was added to prevent.

## Fix

Serialize apply on a lock taken before the unchanged check and held until the retry file is written, using the existing ln-based `_acquire_lock "$state_dir/apply.lock"` (a loser on the retry path just exits 0; a loser on the flip path waits briefly and re-reads state). Minimum for (1): claim the window by `touch -- "$retry_file"` immediately after the mmin check passes, before forking. For (2): have the retry path re-read `$state_file` after `wait` and discard its results (no rm/rewrite of `retry`) when mode or family changed underneath it. Add a bats case running two retry-eligible applies concurrently and asserting one handler run.

## Resolution
config/theme/apply: the cheap unchanged+not-due path still exits before any lock; every run that writes mode/family/retry takes $state_dir/apply.lock via the existing ln-based _acquire_lock and re-decides (state_unchanged / retry_due) under it. A retry loser exits 0; a flip waits up to 10 s, then logs WARN and exits 1. Lock released on EXIT; stale locks are broken by _acquire_lock. CLAUDE.md and the header document exactly this. Tests (tests/theme-actor.bats): "concurrent applies past the backoff retry once" (6 concurrent applies -> 2 runs total), "a flip during a retry runs after it and keeps its retry list" (order dark,light; mode=light; retry=flaky), "a retry gives way to an apply holding the lock", "a stale lock from a dead apply does not block a flip". All four fail against the pre-fix apply.
title: apply retry file is an unlocked check-then-act: concurrent shells all retry, and a late retry run deletes a newer flip's retry list

body:
## Problem

The new comment promises "a permanent failure costs one handler run per window instead of a full fan-out per shell". The unchanged test requires a non-empty family (line 48), so when `config/theme/family` holds a typo or an unknown family, `unchanged` stays 0 on every call, the retry path is never consulted, and each interactive shell rewrites state, forks every handler (all exit 1 at `_theme_family`), logs ~13 WARN lines and rewrites `retry`.

## Evidence

apply:42-45 family="$(_theme_family 2> /dev/null)" || { family=""; _log "WARN ..."; }
apply:48 if [[ -r "$state_file" && -n "$family" ]]; then ... unchanged=1
apply:60-63 comment: "... a permanent failure costs one handler run per window instead of a full fan-out per shell."

## Impact

A permanent configuration error turns every interactive shell start into a synchronous 11-handler fan-out and floods the 200-line log so earlier diagnostics rotate out; the documented backoff does not apply to the most likely permanent failure.

## Fix

Treat an unresolvable family as its own state key: compare `current_family` against a sentinel (e.g. write `family` as `-` when empty) so an unchanged invalid family takes the `unchanged` branch and the retry backoff, or exit early after the WARN when family is empty and `$state_file` already holds `$mode`. Add a bats case with DOTFILES_THEME_FAMILY=bogus running apply twice and asserting the handler ran once.

## Resolution
config/theme/apply records an unresolvable family as "-" (family_key) in $state_dir/family, so an unchanged invalid family takes the unchanged/retry-backoff path; the "family unresolvable" WARN is logged only on the flip that writes it. Test: tests/theme-actor.bats "an unresolvable family is not re-applied by every shell" (two applies -> 1 handler run, 1 WARN; fixing the family re-runs handlers). Fails pre-fix.
title: With an unresolvable family, apply bypasses the retry backoff and fans out every handler on every shell

body:
## Problem

The change makes handler exit status load-bearing (CLAUDE.md: "a failure must exit non-zero with a stderr line"; apply records non-zero handlers in `retry`). bat's line 30 `_atomic_write "$state_dir/bat-theme" "$theme"` has its status discarded; the script's exit status is that of the trailing `if command -v bat` block, which is 0 when bat is absent or the cache is fresh. television line 41 `_atomic_write "$tvdir/config.toml" "$content"` is likewise unchecked; its final `exit "$rc"` reflects only the two symlinks.

## Evidence

bat:30  _atomic_write "$state_dir/bat-theme" "$theme"   (status unused; script continues to line 38 `if command -v bat ...`)
television:41  _atomic_write "$tvdir/config.toml" "$content"   (status unused) ... 54-57 rc=0; _idempotent_ln_sf ... || rc=1; exit "$rc"
Reproduced: XDG_STATE_HOME under a regular file → bat handler prints `mkdir: ...: Not a directory` and exits rc=0.

## Impact

When the state write fails, shells keep exporting the previous BAT_THEME (or television keeps the old config.toml) while apply records a successful flip and no retry; the failure only shows as an INFO line in the log.

## Fix

bat:30 → `_atomic_write "$state_dir/bat-theme" "$theme" || { echo "bat handler: cannot write $state_dir/bat-theme" >&2; exit 1; }`. television:41 → `_atomic_write "$tvdir/config.toml" "$content" || rc=1` with `rc=0` moved above it. Add a bats case per handler pointing XDG_STATE_HOME under a regular file and asserting status 1.

## Resolution
handlers.d/bat: failed _atomic_write of bat-theme prints "bat handler: cannot write ..." and exits 1. handlers.d/television: rc=0 moved above the config write; a failed write prints "television handler: cannot write ..." and sets rc=1 (links still attempted). Tests in tests/theme-handlers.bats: "bat handler: an unwritable state dir exits 1 with a message" (XDG_STATE_HOME under a regular file, fake bat so the cache block is skipped) and "television handler: a failed config write exits 1 with a message" (links present, tvdir chmod 555). Both fail pre-fix.
title: bat and television handlers ignore a failed _atomic_write and exit 0, so apply never retries the missing state file

body:
## Problem

mutation-blind: the watcher's EXIT trap gained `pkill -P $$` so the backgrounded Linux monitor pipeline dies with the watcher ("no orphaned reader keeps calling apply"). `assert_term_exits_143` only checks the exit status and pidfile removal; nothing checks that the monitor child is gone. The linux test's comment ("exec sleep makes the fake monitor itself the long-running process, so killing it leaves no orphan behind") asserts the property without testing it.

## Evidence

assert_term_exits_143: `[ "$rc" -eq 143 ]` / `[ ! -e "$pidfile" ]` are the only assertions. Mutation run: a copy of config/theme/watcher with the EXIT trap reduced to `trap 'rm -f "$pidfile"' EXIT`, same fake gsettings (`monitor) exec sleep 30`), TERM after 1 s → rc=143, pidfile gone (both assertions pass), and `pgrep -f 'sleep 30'` finds 1 orphan.

## Impact

Dropping or breaking the pkill (e.g. on a host without pkill, where the error is silenced by `2> /dev/null`) leaves an orphaned monitor + while-loop calling apply alongside the respawned watcher, and the suite stays green.

## Fix

In the linux TERM test, have the fake monitor record its pid (`monitor) echo $$ > "$TMPDIR_TEST/monitor.pid"; exec sleep 30 ;;`) and after `assert_term_exits_143` assert `! kill -0 "$(cat "$TMPDIR_TEST/monitor.pid")"` (poll briefly). Optionally replace pkill with the dependency-free `kill $(jobs -p)`.

## Resolution
tests/theme-watcher.bats "watcher linux: TERM exits 143 while the monitor pipeline runs": the fake monitor writes its pid before exec sleep; after assert_term_exits_143 the test polls up to 2 s and fails (killing the orphan) if the monitor is still alive. Verified it fails against a watcher whose EXIT trap lacks `pkill -P $$`, and passes against the real watcher (5/5 runs).
title: Watcher TERM tests are mutation-blind to the new `pkill -P $$` orphan cleanup

body:
## Problem

config/theme/CLAUDE.md now defines the handler contract apply's retry depends on: a failure must exit non-zero with a stderr line, and a missing tool is a skip (stderr note, exit 0). CLAUDE.md sends new handlers through the theme-handler-scaffold skill, but the skill's template and "Conventions enforced" list say nothing about either rule, and its printed reminder tells authors to "wrap it with `&`" — a backgrounded reload's failure never reaches apply, so it is never logged or retried.

## Evidence

SKILL.md:82-84 "The orchestrator forks every handler in parallel under a 5 s timeout; if your reload blocks, wrap it with `&` or short-circuit on failure." Conventions (88-98) list exit 2 on bad mode and exit 1 on `_theme_family` failure only. CLAUDE.md (changed): "a failure must exit non-zero with a stderr line (apply logs it). A missing tool is a skip: stderr note, exit 0."

## Impact

Handlers scaffolded from the skill can exit 1 on a missing tool (retried every 10 minutes forever, as fish/dircolors did before this change) or swallow failures via `&` / `|| true`, defeating the retry mechanism.

## Fix

Add both rules to "Conventions enforced" and the template (a `command -v <app> || { echo "<app> handler: <app> not in PATH; skipping" >&2; exit 0; }` block and `|| { echo ... >&2; exit 1; }` on the reload). Replace the `&` advice with "keep the reload under 5 s; never background it or append `|| true`".

## Resolution
.claude/skills/theme-handler-scaffold/SKILL.md: template gains a `command -v <app> || { stderr note; exit 0; }` skip block and `|| { echo ... >&2; exit 1; }` on _link_palette; the printed reminder now says keep the reload under 5 s, end it with `|| { echo ... >&2; exit 1; }`, never background with & or append `|| true`; "Conventions enforced" adds the non-zero-with-stderr failure rule and the missing-tool-is-a-skip rule. Docs-only; yarn lint:ec clean.
title: theme-handler-scaffold skill omits the new handler exit-code contract and advises backgrounding reloads with `&`

body:
## Problem

parse_flags assigns VERBOSE/DELETE_ORIGINAL/FORCE, but main calls it as `mapfile -t ARGS < <(parse_flags "$@")` (line 372). Process substitution runs it in a subshell, so the assignments are discarded; the parent keeps the defaults (false). Every documented option of `a` is a no-op. The ad.md/ae.md rewrites in this change describe their new --force as matching `a`, which does not work.

## Evidence

line 372: `mapfile -t ARGS < <(parse_flags "$@")`; parse_flags lines 82-90 set VERBOSE=true / DELETE_ORIGINAL=true / FORCE=true. Reproduced with a stub age: `a -f e f` (f.age exists) -> rc=1, log "Output file 'f.age' already exists. Use --force"; same for `--force e f` and `e f --force`. `a --delete e g` -> rc=0, both g and g.age remain. `a -v e g2` prints nothing. tests/age-wrappers.bats has no test exercising a --force/--delete/-v (all 200 slice tests pass).

## Impact

`a --delete e secret.txt` reports nothing and leaves the plaintext on disk while the user believes it was removed after encryption. `a -f` can never overwrite; `a d dir` after a re-encrypt fails. Verbose never shows the error messages (see the log-only error finding).

## Fix

Parse flags in the current shell: replace parse_flags+mapfile with a loop in main that builds a local array, e.g. `local args=(); for arg; do case $arg in -v|--verbose) VERBOSE=true;; --delete) DELETE_ORIGINAL=true;; -f|--force) FORCE=true;; *) args+=("$arg");; esac; done; set -- "${args[@]}"`, then read command/target from $1/$2. Add bats tests: `a --delete e` removes the original, `a -f e` overwrites an existing .age, `a -v` echoes messages.

## Resolution
local/bin/a: removed parse_flags + `mapfile < <(parse_flags)`; main now parses -v/--delete/-f in the current shell (anywhere on the command line). Proved by new tests in tests/age-wrappers.bats: "a: --delete removes the original after encrypting", "a: --delete removes the .age file after decrypting", "a: -f overwrites an existing .age file", "a: --force after the target overwrites too", "a: -v prints progress on stdout" (all failed before, pass after).
title: a: -f/--force, --delete and -v are set in a process-substitution subshell and never take effect

body:
## Problem

coverage-hole: the `a` tests (from "a e + a d: round trip" at line 387 onward) cover only key fetching and a round trip. No test runs `a --delete`, `a -f/--force`, `a -v`, or `a` against an existing output file, so the fully broken flag parsing (audit-23596201) passes the suite. ae/ad have --force tests; a has none.

## Evidence

`grep -n 'force\|delete\|verbose' tests/age-wrappers.bats` hits only ae/ad tests (lines 233-357); the `a:` tests are titled "rejects an HTTP error body", "refetches keys older...", "keeps fresh keys", "a failed refresh warns...", "a directory refreshes the keys at most once", "an interrupted keys download...". Mutation: delete parse_flags' `--delete) DELETE_ORIGINAL=true` arm -> no test fails (the arm is already dead and the suite is green: 200/200).

## Impact

Plaintext-retention and overwrite-guard regressions in the encryption wrapper ship silently.

## Fix

Add tests with the existing age stub: `a --delete e file` -> file gone, file.age present; `a e file` with existing file.age -> non-zero and file.age unchanged; `a -f e file` -> file.age replaced; `a -v e file` -> stdout contains "File encrypted successfully"; `a --delete d file.age` -> file.age removed.

## Resolution
tests/age-wrappers.bats: added 12 `a` tests via an a_args helper covering --delete (encrypt and decrypt), refusing an existing .age (stderr, file unchanged, age not called), -f / trailing --force overwrite, -v output, silent success without -v, directory continue-past-failure, directory-at-output refusal with -f (encrypt and decrypt), recursive decrypt, missing target. Setup now exports AGE_LOGFILE into $TMP so ae/ad runs do not write ~/.cache/a.log. 11 of the new tests failed against the old `a`.
title: age-wrappers.bats never exercises a's --delete/--force/--verbose or its overwrite guard (coverage-hole on a data-loss path)

body:
## Problem

ignored-error-signal: log_message appends to $LOG_FILE and echoes to stdout only when VERBOSE is true. All error paths (output exists, identity unreadable, encrypt/decrypt failed, unknown command, keys fetch failed) go through log_message, so without -v (which is itself broken, audit-23596201) nothing reaches the terminal, and with -v errors go to stdout, not stderr. ae/ad were changed in this diff to send errors to stderr; a was not.

## Evidence

lines 121-130: `echo "$(date ...) - $message" >> "$LOG_FILE"` / `if [[ "$VERBOSE" == true ]]; then echo "$message"; fi`. Repro: `a e f` with existing f.age -> rc=1, empty stdout/stderr; message only in ~/.cache/a.log.

## Impact

A failed encryption or decryption of a secret looks like an unexplained exit 1; in a directory run the user cannot tell which file failed or why.

## Fix

Route messages starting with "Error:"/"Warning:" to stderr unconditionally (e.g. a log_error helper that logs and `echo "$message" >&2`), keep informational messages behind VERBOSE.

## Resolution
local/bin/a log_message: messages starting "Error:"/"Warning:" now always go to stderr (and the log); progress goes to stdout only with -v. The duplicated explicit stderr echo in the keys-refresh fallback was folded into one log_message. Proved by "a: refuses to overwrite an existing .age file, on stderr" (stdout empty, stderr has "already exists") and "a: a target that does not exist is an error"; "a: without -v a success prints nothing" guards the quiet path. a.md/print_help document the routing.
title: a: every error is written only to the log file; the user gets a bare exit status

body:
## Problem

format_grouped_review_comments passes the entire reviews array, including every review body, as one argv string: `jq -r --argjson reviews "$reviews"`. CodeRabbit review bodies are tens of KB each. Linux caps a single argument at 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN); macOS caps total argv+env at ~1 MiB. Exceeding it makes exec fail, stderr is discarded (`2> /dev/null`), and the fallback prints "Error parsing grouped review comments." with exit 0.

## Evidence

line 102: `echo "$review_comments" | jq -r --argjson reviews "$reviews" '`; line 134-137: `' 2> /dev/null || { logger::debug ...; echo "Error parsing grouped review comments."; }`. Repro on this macOS host: a 20-review array of 60 KB bodies (1,202,130 bytes) -> `jq --argjson reviews "$R" 'length'` exits 126 (argument list too long). Only id/user/state/submitted_at of each review are used by the filter.

## Impact

On any PR with a few large bot reviews the report contains no review comments at all, exits 0, and the LLM consumer gets an empty work list.

## Fix

Pass only the fields used and pass them via a file: `jq -r --slurpfile reviews <(jq '[.[] | {id, user: {login: .user.login}, submitted_at, state}]' <<< "$reviews")` and use `$reviews[0]` in the filter; also stop discarding jq's stderr so the failure is logged at error level.

## Resolution
local/bin/x-pr-comments format_grouped_review_comments: both arrays now reach jq on stdin (`{ echo comments; echo reviews; } | jq -r -s`) instead of `--argjson reviews`; jq stderr is no longer discarded and a failure logs logger::error and returns 1 (set -e stops the run) instead of printing a placeholder and exiting 0. Proved by "pr-comments: large review bodies do not drop the comments" (20 x 60 KB review bodies; failed before with "Error parsing", passes after).
title: x-pr-comments: full reviews JSON passed to jq via --argjson overflows the argument limit and drops every comment

body:
## Problem

The rewritten footer item 1 says "Evaluate every comment, including nitpicks and \"Outside diff range comments\"". CodeRabbit puts outside-diff and nitpick comments in the review body, not in /pulls/N/comments. The script fetches /reviews but only uses id/user/state/submitted_at; review bodies (and PR conversation comments from /issues/N/comments) are never printed.

## Evidence

line 257: `1. **Evaluate every comment, including nitpicks and "Outside diff range comments"**`; lines 109-111 use only `$review.user.login`, `$review.submitted_at`, `$review.state`, `$review.id`; no `.body` of a review is emitted anywhere; fetch_and_display_pr_data (lines 300-301) fetches only /pulls/N/comments and /pulls/N/reviews.

## Impact

The consumer is told the report covers outside-diff and nitpick comments; they are missing, so those review requests are silently skipped while the report claims completeness.

## Fix

Emit each non-empty review body inside an <untrusted-comment> fence (with the same `fence` defang) under its "### Review by" heading, or drop the outside-diff/nitpick wording from the instructions.

## Resolution
local/bin/x-pr-comments now emits each non-empty review body in an <untrusted-comment> fence (same fence defang) under its "### Review by" heading, including reviews that have a body but no file comments; orphan comment groups keep the "unknown" section. The footer's nitpick/outside-diff wording is now accurate. The CodeRabbit "Addressed in commit" filter uses `.body // ""` so null review bodies do not abort it. Proved by "pr-comments: review bodies are reported, fenced" (failed before, passes after).
title: x-pr-comments: instructions demand evaluation of "Outside diff range comments", which the report never contains

body:
## Problem

Under `set -euo pipefail`, encrypt_single_file/decrypt_single_file `return 1` on a per-file error; the caller `encrypt_file_or_directory "$f"` in the for loop (line 292, and decrypt_single_file at 357) is a plain command, so errexit ends the script there. Remaining files are skipped with no summary.

## Evidence

Repro: dir w3 with a1, a1.age (pre-existing), b2, c3 -> `a e w3` rc=1, `ls w3` = a1 a1.age b2 c3 (b2, c3 not encrypted). Combined with log-only errors, nothing is printed.

## Impact

A partial batch encryption leaves plaintext files unencrypted while the user sees only exit 1.

## Fix

Collect failures: `encrypt_file_or_directory "$f" || failed=1` in both loops, continue, and exit non-zero at the end with a count of failed files.

## Resolution
local/bin/a: new process_path walker calls the per-file action as `"$action" "$path" || FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))`, so a directory run continues past a failed file; main exits 1 with "Error: N file(s) failed under '<dir>'." on stderr. Proved by "a: a directory encrypt continues past a failed file" (a1 fails, b2/c3 encrypted, rc 1, count on stderr; failed before).
title: a: a directory run aborts at the first file that fails, leaving the rest unprocessed

body:
## Problem

The overwrite guard tests `-f "$output_file"` (lines 252 and 314), so a directory at the output path passes; `mv "$TEMP_FILE" "$output_file"` then moves the temp file into that directory as tmp.XXXXXXXXXX. ad/ae use `-e` and refuse.

## Evidence

Repro: w1/foo.age plus directory w1/foo -> `a d w1/foo.age` rc=0, log "File decrypted successfully: w1/foo", plaintext lands at w1/foo/tmp.7oU5huols0. Same for `a e w2/bar` with directory w2/bar.age -> ciphertext at w2/bar.age/tmp.YGw2DBSK2F, rc=0. With --delete working, the source would then be deleted.

## Impact

Decrypted plaintext is dropped under an unexpected name; with --delete the original is removed while the output is not where the message says.

## Fix

Use `-e` (or `-e || -L`) in both guards, and refuse a directory even with --force; use `mv -T`-equivalent semantics by checking `[[ -d "$output_file" ]]` before mv.

## Resolution
local/bin/a: new check_output refuses a directory at the output path even with --force, and guards existing outputs with `-e || -L` instead of `-f`. Proved by "a: -f never moves the output into a directory of that name" and "a: -f decrypt never moves the plaintext into a directory" (the latter with --delete: source kept, no tmp file in the directory); both failed before.
title: a: an existing directory at the output path swallows the result under a random temp name and reports success

body:
## Problem

encrypt_file_or_directory recurses into subdirectories (line 292 calls itself), while decrypt_file_or_directory globs only "$file"/*.age (line 348) and calls decrypt_single_file, never recursing. `a e dir` followed by `a d dir` cannot restore nested files.

## Evidence

line 348: `local files=("$file"/*.age)`; line 357: `decrypt_single_file "$f"`. Encrypt side line 292: `encrypt_file_or_directory "$f"`. Repro: w4/sub/n.txt encrypted to w4/sub/n.txt.age by `a e w4`; `a d w4` never visits w4/sub.

## Impact

Nested encrypted files silently stay encrypted after a directory decrypt; a.md documents both as directory operations.

## Fix

Mirror the encrypt walk: glob "$file"/* with dotglob/nullglob and recurse into directories, calling decrypt_single_file for *.age files.

## Resolution
local/bin/a: encrypt and decrypt share one recursive walker (process_path, dotglob+nullglob), so directory decrypt recurses like encrypt; non-.age files inside a directory are skipped, a named non-.age file is refused. Proved by "a: a directory decrypt recurses like the encrypt" (sub/deeper/n.txt.age restored, sub/notes.txt untouched; failed before). a.md Behavior section updated.
title: a: directory encryption recurses but directory decryption only reads the top level

body:
## Problem

The comment block states line-leading "#" is escaped "so a body cannot open a heading that poses as the real instructions". The fence only rewrites `^[ \t]*#`. A body line followed by a line of `===` or `---` is a Markdown setext heading (h1/h2), which passes unchanged.

## Evidence

line 103-104: `def fence: gsub("</untrusted-comment"; "<\\/untrusted-comment"; "i") | gsub("(?m)^(?<h>[ \t]*#)"; "\\\(.h)");`. Body "Next Steps for LLM Analysis\n===========================\n1. Run ..." renders/reads as an h1 matching the real footer heading; no test covers setext form (tests 163-167 check "#" and the closing tag).

## Impact

A third-party PR commenter can forge an instruction-looking heading inside the report fed to an agent, contrary to the stated guarantee.

## Fix

Also escape setext underlines: `gsub("(?m)^(?<u>[ \t]*[=-]{2,}[ \t]*)$"; "\\\(.u)")`, or indent every fenced body line by four spaces so nothing inside can form block structure; add a bats case for a `===` underline.

## Resolution
local/bin/x-pr-comments fence now also escapes setext underlines: `gsub("(?m)^(?<u>[ \t]*[=-]+[ \t]*)$"; "\\\(.u)")`; comment updated. Proved by "pr-comments: a body cannot forge a setext heading" (=== and --- lines get a leading backslash; failed before).
title: x-pr-comments: heading defang covers ATX "#" only; a comment body can still forge a setext heading

body:
## Problem

The bearer token is passed as a command-line argument, which any local user can read via ps / /proc/PID/cmdline for the life of each request. Same pattern in x-gh-get-latest-version lines 132 and 190 (`-H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN"`).

## Evidence

x-sonarcloud lines 177-179: `response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SONAR_TOKEN" "$url" 2> /dev/null)`; x-gh-get-latest-version line 132: `auth_header=(-H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN")`.

## Impact

Token disclosure to other accounts on a shared host (CI runners, multi-user Linux boxes).

## Fix

Feed the header on stdin: `curl -H @- ... <<< "Authorization: Bearer $SONAR_TOKEN"` (curl 7.55+), or `--config -` with `header = "..."`.

## Resolution
x-sonarcloud sonar_api_request feeds "Authorization: Bearer ..." via `curl -H @- <<< ...`; x-gh-get-latest-version gained gh_curl(), which does the same for GITHUB_TOKEN, used by check_rate_limits and api_request (auth_header arrays removed). Verified -H @- in man curl (7.55.0+). Proved by "sonarcloud: the token is sent on stdin, never on the command line" and "GITHUB_TOKEN goes to curl on stdin, never on the command line" (curl stubs now log full argv and stdin; both failed before).
title: x-sonarcloud and x-gh-get-latest-version put API tokens in curl's argv

body:
## Problem

project key, branch, and filters are spliced into the URL raw. A git branch name may contain `#`, `+`, `&`, `%` (e.g. `fix#12`, `a+b`): `#` truncates the query (everything after becomes a fragment, dropping p/ps/filters), `+` decodes to a space, `&` injects a parameter. sonar_api_request also runs `curl -s` with no --connect-timeout/--max-time, so a stalled connection hangs indefinitely inside $(...).

## Evidence

line 237: `url="${url}&branch=${branch}"`; line 229: `local url="${base_url}/api/issues/search?componentKeys=${project_key}"`; line 177: `curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -H ... "$url"` (no timeout flags).

## Impact

`x-sonarcloud --branch 'fix#12'` silently queries the wrong scope (whole project, default page) and reports those issues as the branch's; a network stall hangs the tool.

## Fix

Use `curl -G --data-urlencode "componentKeys=$project_key" --data-urlencode "branch=$branch" ...` against the bare endpoint, and add `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60`.

## Resolution
x-sonarcloud: fetch_issues_page builds name=value params passed to sonar_api_request, which sends them with `curl -G --data-urlencode` against the bare /api/issues/search endpoint, plus `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60`. Proved by "sonarcloud: query values are URL-encoded" (--branch 'fix#12') and "sonarcloud: requests carry a timeout" (both failed before); existing query-param tests still pass with the stub logging full argv.
title: x-sonarcloud: query parameters are concatenated unencoded and the request has no timeout

body:
## Problem

This change copies the same ~30-line stale-key refresh (mktemp beside KEYS_FILE, curl -fsSL with timeouts, grep for ssh- prefix, chmod 0400, mv -f, cached fallback) into both a (lines 195-236) and ae (lines 69-99), and the AGE_IDENTITY default chain into both a (35-41) and ad (9-15). The two copies already diverge (a guards output with -f, ae/ad with -e; a logs errors only to file, ae/ad print to stderr), and the divergences are where the defects sit (audit-0bf592bc, audit-1d81bc3d).

## Evidence

ae lines 81-98 and a lines 217-235 are the same fetch block; ad.md/ae.md now say the behaviour matches `a` "as a encrypt/decrypt does".

## Impact

Every future fix (revocation policy, key validation) must be made three times; the copies have already drifted in this same diff.

## Fix

Reduce ae and ad to `exec a encrypt "$@"` / `exec a decrypt "$@"` (after fixing a's flag parsing), keeping their usage text; delete the duplicated blocks and the duplicated tests.

## Resolution
local/bin/ae and ad reduced to `exec "$(dirname -- "$0")/a" -v encrypt|decrypt "$@"` (#USAGE kept, --delete added). `a` adopted the ae/ad contract they relied on: stderr errors, curl required only for encrypt, "age is not installed" wording, missing target is an error, named non-.age file refused for decrypt. git grep found no other callers. All 30 existing ae/ad tests kept unchanged and pass against the wrapper (only setup change: AGE_LOGFILE exported into $TMP). ae.md/ad.md now describe them as shorthands for `a -v encrypt|decrypt` (adds directory and --delete support).
title: ae/ad duplicate a's key-refresh, identity selection and temp-file logic instead of delegating to a

body:
## Problem

The exclusion regex is unanchored, so it matches substrings; the branch list is also word-split (`for branch in $output`), so a worktree-checked-out branch line `+ name` yields a `+` "branch".

## Evidence

line 405: `output=$(git branch --merged | grep -v -E "^\*|master|main|develop" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//')`; line 413: `for branch in $output; do`. A merged branch `fix-domain-check` or `maintenance` matches `main` and is never deleted; the count echoed to the caller (now captured after this change) excludes them.

## Impact

--cleanup silently leaves merged branches behind and logs a WARNING for the bogus `+` entry.

## Fix

Use `git for-each-ref --merged HEAD --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/` and filter exact names with `grep -vxE 'master|main|develop'` (plus the current branch), reading line by line with `while IFS= read -r branch`.

## Resolution
local/bin/git-update-dirs cleanup_branches: uses `git for-each-ref --merged HEAD --format='%(if)%(worktreepath)%(then)%(else)%(refname:short)%(end)' refs/heads/` (branches checked out in any worktree, incl. current, become empty lines) filtered with `grep -vxE '(master|main|develop)?'`, read line by line with `while IFS= read -r`. Proved by "git-update-dirs: --cleanup matches protected names exactly" (maintenance and fix-domain-check deleted, worktree branch and main kept, no WARNING in log; failed before).
title: git-update-dirs --cleanup skips any merged branch whose name contains "main", "master" or "develop"

body:
## Problem

_bp_call peels only a fixed wrapper set. Any other command that runs its arguments as a command leaves `git` in argv position >0, so _bp_check_argv never sees it, and the suffix re-check at 538-543 runs only when `wrapped=1`, which these wrappers never set. `mise` is on the router's own allow list, and mise is the repo's tool manager.

## Evidence

Wrapper set (468): `sudo | doas | xargs | nohup | builtin | exec | time | timeout | stdbuf | nice | ionice)`; default `*) break ;;`. Suffix re-check guarded by `if [[ $wrapped -eq 1 && -z $BP_REASON ]]` (538). Hook runs (pre-bash-route.sh and pre-ctx-write-guard.sh, both): ALLOW for `mise exec -- git add -A`, `mise x -- git commit --no-verify -m x`, `setsid git add -A`, `caffeinate git add -A`, `unbuffer git add .`, `xcrun git add .`, `chronic git add .`, `flock /tmp/l git add .`, `yarn exec git add .`, `mise exec python -- -m pip install foo`. Control: `git add -A` is denied.

## Impact

git-hunk-commits.md, no-hook-bypass.md, mise-packages.md and no-npm.md all state that bash-policy.sh denies these forms in Bash and the sandbox; one prefix word defeats every argv check, BASH_OK not required.

## Fix

Add `mise exec`/`mise x` (peel through `--`), `yarn exec`/`yarn run` when followed by a policy tool, `setsid`, `caffeinate`, `unbuffer`, `chronic`, `flock` (drop its lock-file operand), `xcrun`, `arch`, `script -q`, `taskset`, `chrt` to the peel list with wrapped=1. Add a bats case per wrapper in tests/pre-bash-route.bats and tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats.

## Resolution
bash-policy.sh _bp_final now re-checks every argv suffix that starts at a verb tool (BP_VERB_TOOL_RE: git, git-hunk, pip*, python*, uv, prek, pre-commit) for any command, so a runner of any name cannot hide git add/--no-verify/pip install. Runners in BP_RUNNER_RE (mise, yarn, setsid, caffeinate, unbuffer, chronic, flock, xcrun, arch, script, taskset, chrt) get the full suffix scan, which also covers name-only bans (curl, npm). Ceiling documented in no-hook-bypass.md / no-npm.md / context-mode.md: curl/npm behind a runner missing from BP_RUNNER_RE stays unseen. Tests: "pre-bash-route: unlisted runners cannot hide a policy command", "a mere mention of a policy tool is not a command", and "pre-ctx-write-guard: runners, config files and aliases cannot hide a policy command".
title: Unlisted command wrappers (mise exec, yarn exec, setsid, caffeinate, flock, ...) hide git add and --no-verify from the policy tier

body:
## Problem

The bypass scan looks for the literal key `core.hooksPath` in argv and for a fixed env list. Git also reads hooksPath from any config file it is pointed at: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL / GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, or `-c include.path=<file>`. Neither the env names nor `include.path`/`includeIf` are in the patterns, and the file itself is written with an ordinary printf redirect to /tmp.

## Evidence

BP_ENV_BYPASS_RE (142): `^(SKIP|PRE_COMMIT_ALLOW_NO_CONFIG|GIT_CONFIG_COUNT|GIT_CONFIG_KEY_[0-9]+|GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_[0-9]+|GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS)$`; BP_HOOKCFG_RE (160-161) matches only core.hooksPath and commit.gpgsign. Hook runs: ALLOW for `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/tmp/c git commit -m x` and `git -c include.path=/tmp/c commit -m x` (both tiers). Scratch repo with a failing pre-commit hook and a file holding `[core] hooksPath = /nonexistent`: plain commit rc=1 (HOOKRAN); `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file> git commit` rc=0; `git -c include.path=<file> commit` rc=0. This repo's .git/config sets no core.hooksPath, so a global value applies.

## Impact

The whole commit-time gate (shellcheck, shfmt, biome, commitlint, ...) is skipped by an agent in one tool call, which no-hook-bypass.md says the hooks deny.

## Fix

Add GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and GIT_CONFIG to BP_ENV_BYPASS_RE (and the _TEXT_ variant); add case-insensitive `include\.path` and `includeif\.` to BP_HOOKCFG_RE so `-c include.path=` and `git config include.path` are denied. Add bats cases for each; list the forms in no-hook-bypass.md.

## Resolution
BP_ENV_BYPASS_RE and BP_ENV_BYPASS_TEXT_RE now include GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and GIT_CONFIG; BP_HOOKCFG_RE matches include.path and includeIf.* case-insensitively, so -c include.path=, -c includeIf.*, and git config include.path are denied. no-hook-bypass.md lists the forms. Tests: "pre-bash-route: config files that can set core.hooksPath are denied" and the ctx runner/config/alias case.
title: core.hooksPath delivered through a config file (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, -c include.path) disables the commit hooks unseen

body:
## Problem

_bp_git keys every check on the literal subcommand. `-c alias.*` globals are collected but only scanned for hooksPath/gpgsign, and `git config alias.st add` is allowed. The aliased subcommand (`st`, `c`) then matches none of add/stage/commit. On Bash the routing tier happens to deny the unknown subcommand (BASH_OK-overridable); pre-ctx-write-guard.sh has no routing tier, so the sandbox allows it outright.

## Evidence

`_bp_bypass_args ${globals[@]+...}` (712) is the only check on globals; `if [[ $sub == add || $sub == stage ]]` (742). Hook runs, ctx guard: ALLOW `git -c alias.st=add st -A`, ALLOW `git -c alias.c='commit --no-verify' c -m x`, ALLOW `git config alias.st add`. Scratch repo: `git -c alias.st=add st f` staged f.

## Impact

git-hunk-commits.md and no-hook-bypass.md claim both hooks deny these forms in sandbox code; whole-file staging and --no-verify commits are one alias away on the path agents are told to use.

## Fix

In _bp_git deny any global `-c alias.*` (and `--config-env=alias.*`), and deny `git config` writes to an `alias.*` key whose value names add/stage/update-index/commit or starts with `!`. For persistent aliases, resolve `git config --get alias.<sub>` when sub is not a builtin and re-run _bp_git on the expansion. Add bats cases on both hooks.

## Resolution
_bp_git denies any global word matching alias.* (-c alias.x=..., --config-env=alias.x=VAR). New _bp_git_config denies non-read git config forms that name an alias.* key. New _bp_git_alias resolves persistent aliases with `git [-C dir] config --get alias.<sub>` and walks the expansion (a ! alias is parsed as shell) with the caller's BP_SEGMENTS/BP_KEEP preserved and depth capped. Tests: "pre-bash-route: git aliases cannot rename a denied subcommand", "persistent aliases are resolved before the checks" (temp repo with alias.st=add, a ! alias, and a -C form; alias undo=reset --soft still allowed), plus the ctx guard case.
title: A git alias (-c alias.X=add, git config alias.X ...) renames add and commit --no-verify past the policy tier; the sandbox has no fallback

body:
## Problem

The guard reads `commands`, `code`, `language` and `path` from tool_input, but not `cwd`, which both execute tools accept. Relative names inside a secrets tree or protected tree carry no `secrets.d` / protected-path text, so neither predicate fires.

## Evidence

Extraction (34-43) reads `.tool_input.commands`, `.tool_input.code`, `.tool_input.language`, `.tool_input.path` only; no reference to cwd in the file. Hook runs, exit 0 (allowed): ctx_batch_execute `{cwd:"config/fish/secrets.d", commands:[{command:"cat github.fish"}]}`; ctx_execute `{cwd:"config/fish/secrets.d", language:"shell", code:"cat *"}`; ctx_execute `{cwd:"tools/dotbot", code:"echo x > setup.py"}`. No bats test passes a cwd (`rg cwd` in the three hook test files: 0 hits).

## Impact

Live credentials print into the conversation, which secrets-files.md says pre-ctx-write-guard.sh prevents for the sandbox tools; vendored/submodule trees are writable the same way.

## Fix

Extract `.tool_input.cwd`; block when `secrets_referenced "$cwd"` succeeds, and run protected_referenced on the cwd joined with each write target (or block any write-shaped code when protected_referenced "$cwd/" succeeds). Add bats cases for both tools.

## Resolution
pre-ctx-write-guard.sh reads tool_input.cwd: a cwd naming a secrets.d tree is blocked outright; BP_CWD is passed to bash-policy.sh, whose new _bp_protected resolves relative redirect targets and write-command operands against it (absolute/home paths ignore it); for non-shell code a protected cwd counts as a protected path in the co-occurrence heuristic. Tests: "pre-ctx-write-guard: a secrets.d cwd is refused" and "writes resolved against a protected cwd are refused" (both tools; reads and /tmp writes in a protected cwd still pass).
title: ctx_execute / ctx_batch_execute `cwd` is never checked: a secrets.d or protected directory as cwd defeats the secrets and protected-path guards

body:
## Problem

update-index updates the index entry for every tracked path operand without --add. The check converts update-index to add only when an `--add` prefix is present, and `update-index` is on the router's allow list, so the plain form passes both tiers.

## Evidence

`[[ $a =~ ^--add?(=.*)?$ ]] && sub=add` (739). Hook runs: ALLOW `git update-index config/alias` on Bash and ctx. Scratch repo: after `echo b > f; git update-index f`, `git diff --cached --name-only` printed `f`.

## Impact

git-hunk-commits.md forbids whole-file staging; this is the unguarded spelling of `git add <tracked file>`.

## Fix

Treat update-index as staging unless every argument is a refresh/flag-only form (`--refresh`, `--really-refresh`, `-q`, `--assume-unchanged`, `--no-assume-unchanged`, `--skip-worktree`, `--no-skip-worktree`); deny path operands, `--again`, `--cacheinfo`, `--index-info`, `--stdin`, `--replace`, `--remove`. Add a bats case.

## Resolution
New _bp_update_index treats update-index as staging: path operands are denied unless a mark flag (--[no-]assume-unchanged, --[no-]skip-worktree, --[no-]fsmonitor-valid) precedes them; --add prefixes, --again/-g, --cacheinfo, --index-info, --stdin, --replace, --remove, --force-remove, --chmod are denied; --refresh/--really-refresh/-q pass. git-hunk-commits.md updated. Tests: "pre-bash-route: update-index with path operands is staging" and the ctx guard case.
title: git update-index <path> stages whole tracked files; only --add is treated as staging

body:
## Problem

BP_WRITE_SEG_RE lists tee/cp/mv/rm/ln/truncate/install/dd/chmod/unlink, `sed -i` and some git subcommands. In-place editors outside that list (perl -i, ruby -i, ex/vim -c, ed, patch) and an awk program's own `print > file` are not write-shaped to it, and the ctx co-occurrence regex (`writeish`) does not match them either.

## Evidence

Line 149: `BP_WRITE_SEG_RE='(^|[[:space:]])(tee|cp|mv|rm|ln|truncate|install|dd|chmod|unlink)([[:space:]]|$)|sed[[:space:]].*-i|git[[:space:]]+(checkout|restore|rm|mv|apply|reset)'`. Hook runs: ALLOW on Bash and ctx for `perl -pi -e s/a/b/ config/fish/functions/fisher.fish` and `vim -c wq yarn.lock`; ctx ALLOW `awk '{print > "yarn.lock"}' /dev/null`. Control: `sed -i '' s/a/b/ config/fish/functions/fisher.fish` is denied.

## Impact

vendored-files.md says the hooks refuse every write to the listed paths; a vendored fish plugin or yarn.lock is rewritten in place with no edit-hook vetting.

## Fix

Extend BP_WRITE_SEG_RE with `(perl|ruby)[[:space:]].*-[A-Za-z]*i`, `(^|[[:space:]])(ed|ex|vi|vim|nvim|patch|rsync)([[:space:]]|$)`, and treat `awk`/`gawk` programs containing `>` as write-shaped; add `perl -.*i` and `print >` to the ctx `writeish` pattern. Add bats cases.

## Resolution
BP_WRITE_SEG_RE extended, anchored to the command word: perl/ruby -*i (incl. -i.bak), ed/ex/vi/vim/nvim/patch/rsync, awk/gawk with print/printf > or -i inplace. _bp_protected also tests words containing braces with the braces removed, since the path normaliser collapsed awk's {print > "yarn.lock"} to `*`. Shell code in both hooks goes through this tier, so the ctx writeish heuristic was not widened. Tests: "pre-bash-route: in-place editors writing protected paths are denied" (rg -n patch yarn.lock and perl -ne reads still pass) and the ctx counterpart.
title: perl -pi, vim/ex and awk-internal redirects write vendored files past both tiers

body:
## Problem

ok_fw is the first word of segments[0]; when the user named it, the hook returns `allow` for the entire command, so every later segment skips the routing tier.

## Evidence

`ok_fw=$(normalise_cmd "$(first_word "${segments[0]:-}")")` then `permissionDecision: "allow"` (139-147). With CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a dir whose .claude/.last-prompt reads `please run yarn build for me`: `BASH_OK yarn build; cat README.md` → allow; `BASH_OK yarn build && git log -p` → allow.

## Impact

bash-routing.md case 4 limits the escape to "a single one-line command the user names"; unbounded readers (git log -p) ride along and flood context.

## Fix

Require `${#segments[@]} -eq 1`, or require every segment's normalised first word to appear in the prompt file before allowing. Add a bats case for a compound BASH_OK command.

## Resolution
pre-bash-route.sh BASH_OK now requires the normalised first word of every segment to appear in .claude/.last-prompt; the deny names the first unnamed command. bash-routing.md states this. Test: "pre-bash-route: BASH_OK requires every command in the line to be named" (yarn build; cat and && git log -p denied, cat | wc allowed when both named).
title: BASH_OK checks only the first segment against the prompt, then allows the whole compound command

body:
## Problem

The pip checks match exact command names `pip|pip3|python|python3` and the three separate words `-m pip install`. mise installs versioned binaries (python3.12, pip3.12), and Python accepts `-mpip`.

## Evidence

`pip | pip3) [[ $sub == install ]] ...` and `python | python3)` loop requiring `${w[i]} == -m && ${w[i + 1]} == pip` (565-569). ctx guard runs: ALLOW `python3.12 -m pip install foo`, `pip3.12 install foo`, `python3 -mpip install foo`; control `python3 -m pip install foo` BLOCKED.

## Impact

mise-packages.md names `python3 -m pip install` as denied by both hooks; the equivalent spellings install packages outside config/mise/default-python-packages.

## Fix

Match `fw` against `^pip[0-9.]*$` and `^python[0-9.]*$`, and accept `-mpip` as well as `-m pip`. Add bats cases.

## Resolution
_bp_check_argv matches pip | pip[0-9]* and python | python[0-9]*, and accepts -mpip install as well as -m pip install; the foreign-code scan in _bp_final also covers python[0-9]*. mise-packages.md updated. Tests: "pre-bash-route: versioned pip and python spellings are denied" and the ctx counterpart (python3.12 -m pip list passes).
title: Versioned interpreters and attached -mpip slip past the pip-install ban

body:
## Problem

bash_policy_check fails closed when shfmt is absent, but both hook suites only test PATH=/nonexistent, which removes jq too and exits at the jq check in the hook before bash-policy.sh's shfmt check runs.

## Evidence

bash-policy.sh 809-811: `if ! command -v shfmt ...; then BP_REASON="shfmt is not on PATH, ..."`. tests/pre-bash-route.bats:449 and tests/pre-ctx-write-guard.bats:195 run with `PATH=/nonexistent` and assert `"jq is not on PATH"`. `rg 'shfmt is not'` over the three suites: 0 hits.

## Impact

A regression that makes the parser-missing path fail open (every policy check skipped) would pass the suite.

## Fix

Add a case per hook that builds a temp PATH containing only jq, bash and coreutils (symlinks) but no shfmt, sends `git add -A`, and asserts a deny/exit 2 with "shfmt is not on PATH".

## Resolution
Added "pre-bash-route: a missing shfmt fails closed" and "pre-ctx-write-guard: a missing shfmt fails closed": PATH is a temp dir with a jq symlink plus /usr/bin:/bin (no shfmt), payload git add -A, asserting deny / exit 2 with "shfmt is not on PATH". Both ran (no skip) on this machine.
title: The shfmt-missing fail-closed branch of the policy tier has no test; the "missing jq" tests exit before reaching it

body:
## Problem

The bats rule matches the raw code text, not a command word, so any code that merely mentions the path (a search for it) is refused. _bp_bypass_args runs on every non-commit git argument, so reading the hooksPath key with `git config --get` is denied as if it set it.

## Evidence

Line 830: `if [[ $code == *node_modules/.bin/bats* ]]; then _bp_deny ...`. A ctx_execute whose code ran `rg -c -e 'node_modules/.bin/bats' tests/...` was BLOCKED with "Use bare `bats` from PATH". `git config --local --get core.hooksPath` in ctx_execute was BLOCKED with "The command bypasses the project's hook chain" (via `_bp_bypass_args ${rest[@]...}` at 734 and BP_HOOKCFG_RE at 160).

## Impact

Agents verifying the hook state (exactly what commit-format.md asks them to check) or auditing tests are refused and pushed toward workarounds.

## Fix

Check the bats path against command words (`fw` or argv[0] in _bp_final) instead of `$code`. In _bp_git, skip the hooksPath match for `git config` when a read flag (`--get`, `--get-all`, `--list`, `-l`, `get`) is present and no value operand follows the key.

## Resolution
The node_modules/.bin/bats check moved from raw code text to the command word (w[0]) in _bp_final. New _bp_git_config skips the hooksPath/alias scan when a read flag (--get*, --list/-l, get/list) is present and no write flag is. Tests: "pre-bash-route: reading core.hooksPath or an alias is allowed", "node_modules/.bin/bats is denied as a command only", and "pre-ctx-write-guard: reading hook state and searching for the bats path pass" (writes still denied).
title: Policy tier refuses read-only inspection: raw substring match on node_modules/.bin/bats, and `git config --get core.hooksPath` treated as a bypass

body:
## Problem

Codacy analyses this repo through the GitHub App and runs its own Bandit with default patterns. As of this run the repo records its Bandit decisions in `[tool.bandit]` in `pyproject.toml`, but Codacy only reads a tool's own config file when "use configuration file" is enabled for that tool in the repository's Code patterns page — a setting that cannot be expressed in `.codacy.yml`. Until it is toggled, Codacy and the local gate disagree about the same code.

## Evidence

Codacy API for `gh/ivuorinen/dotfiles` at commit `e1836f1`: grade A (95), `issuesCount: 23`, every one in the Security category. By pattern:

```
Bandit_B101   11   local/bin/x-compare-versions.py:50-66
Bandit_B607    7   local/bin/x-git-largest-files.py:106,111,116,119,159,160,190
Bandit_B603    2   config/fish/functions/__bass.py:64,71
Bandit_B404    1   config/fish/functions/__bass.py:13
Opengrep dangerous-subprocess-use-audit  2   config/fish/functions/__bass.py:64,71
```

The local gate now reports zero on the same tree:

```
$ bandit -c pyproject.toml -r . -q; echo "rc=$?"
rc=0
```

`.codacy.yml` (added this run) excludes `config/fish/functions/__bass.py`, which retires the 5 `__bass.py` issues. The remaining 18 (11x B101, 7x B607) are in first-party files that must stay analysed, so exclusion is the wrong instrument for them.

## Impact

Two gates disagree on the same commit: `yarn lint` passes while the Codacy check reports 18 security issues, 11 of them at High. A reviewer cannot tell an accepted decision from an unreviewed one, and the standing count trains everyone to ignore the Codacy status — at which point a genuinely new Bandit finding lands unnoticed among the 18.

## Fix

One of two, both requiring dashboard access (https://app.codacy.com/gh/ivuorinen/dotfiles):

1. Preferred — Code patterns > Bandit > enable "use configuration file". Codacy then reads `[tool.bandit]` from `pyproject.toml`, and the B101/B607 decisions plus their recorded reasons apply in both places from one source.
2. Fallback, if that toggle is unavailable on the plan — disable patterns `Bandit_B101` and `Bandit_B607` in the Default coding standard. This drifts from `pyproject.toml`, so add a comment in `[tool.bandit]` pointing at the UI as a second place to update.

After either, re-check the count:

```
curl -s https://app.codacy.com/api/v3/analysis/organizations/gh/ivuorinen/repositories/dotfiles | jq .data.issuesCount
```

Expect 0. Anything else is a pattern the repo has not yet ruled on.

## Status (2026-09-21)

Not applied in the fix run: both options are Codacy dashboard settings with no file-level equivalent, so no repo change can close this. It stays open until someone with dashboard access toggles option 1 (or 2) and re-runs the count.

## Resolution
The finding's premise was wrong: Codacy's "use configuration file" for Bandit was already on (owner, 2026-10-04). Codacy honours pyproject's top-level [tool.bandit] (exclude_dirs, per-line nosec cleared the B607/__bass issues) but not the per-plugin [tool.bandit.assert_used] skips, so the 11 remaining issues were all B101 in local/bin/x-compare-versions.py:50-66. Fix removes the cause instead of configuring around it: test() now calls check(expr, expected), which raises AssertionError explicitly (also survives python -O, where bare asserts were stripped), and the [tool.bandit.assert_used] section is deleted. Local: bandit rc=0 with no skip, tests/x-compare-versions.bats pass. Confirm after push: Codacy issuesCount expected 0.
title: Codacy still reports 18 Bandit issues the repo has explicitly decided to accept, pending a UI-only toggle
